mcqs.why: Working: Put u = tan x, y = u^2, du/dx = sec^2 x. Chain rule: dy/dx = 2u du/dx = 2 tan x sec^2 x.

mcqs.q: What is dy/dx for y = sqrt(tan x)?
mcqs.why: Working: Put u = tan x, y = sqrt(u), du/dx = sec^2 x. Chain rule: dy/dx = (1/(2 sqrt(u))) sec^2 x = sec^2 x/(2 sqrt(tan x)).

mcqs.q: What is dy/dx for y = x^2 sec 4x?
mcqs.why: Working: Product rule: d/dx (x^2) = 2x and d/dx (sec 4x) = 4 sec 4x tan 4x. Hence dy/dx = 2x sec 4x + x^2 (4 sec 4x tan 4x) = 2x sec 4x + 4x^2 sec 4x tan 4x.

mcqs.q: Find dy/dx if y = x cos y
mcqs.why: Working: Differentiate w.r.t. x using the product rule on x cos y: dy/dx = cos y - x sin y dy/dx. Collect dy/dx: (1 + x sin y) dy/dx = cos y, so dy/dx = cos y/(1 + x sin y).

mcqs.q: Differentiate w.r.t. x: Cos^(-1) (x/a)
mcqs.why: Working: Put u = x/a, du/dx = 1/a. Then dy/dx = (-1/sqrt(1 - u^2))(1/a) = -1/[a sqrt(1 - x^2/a^2)] = -1/sqrt(a^2 - x^2).

lessons.title: Exercise 2.6
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find f'(x) if

Q1(i). f(x) = e^(sqrt(x) - 1). Put u = sqrt(x) - 1; then f = e^u and du/dx = 1/(2 sqrt(x)).

By the chain rule, f'(x) = e^u du/dx.

Answer: f'(x) = e^(sqrt(x) - 1) / (2 sqrt(x)).

Q1(ii). f(x) = x3 e^(1/x) (x not equal to 0). Use the product rule: d/dx (x3) = 3x2; d/dx (e^(1/x)) = e^(1/x) (-1/x2).

f'(x) = 3x2 e^(1/x) + x3 e^(1/x) (-1/x2) = e^(1/x)(3x2 - x).

Answer: f'(x) = e^(1/x)(3x2 - x).

Q1(iii). f(x) = e^x (1 + ln x). Use the product rule: d/dx (e^x) = e^x; d/dx (1 + ln x) = 1/x.

f'(x) = e^x (1 + ln x) + e^x (1/x).

Answer: f'(x) = e^x (1 + ln x + 1/x).

Q1(iv). f(x) = e^x / (e^(-x) + 1). Use the quotient rule: numerator derivative e^x; denominator derivative -e^(-x).

f'(x) = [e^x (e^(-x) + 1) - e^x (-e^(-x))] / (e^(-x) + 1)2 = (e^x + 2) / (e^(-x) + 1)2.

Since e^(-x) + 1 = (1 + e^x)/e^x, this simplifies to e^(2x)(e^x + 2)/(e^x + 1)2.

Answer: f'(x) = e^(2x)(e^x + 2) / (e^x + 1)2.

Q1(v). f(x) = ln(e^x + e^(-x)). By the chain rule, f'(x) = (e^x - e^(-x)) / (e^x + e^(-x)).

Answer: f'(x) = (e^x - e^(-x)) / (e^x + e^(-x)) = tanh x.

Q1(vi). f(x) = (e^(a x) - e^(-a x)) / (e^(a x) + e^(-a x)). This is tanh(a x). Use the quotient rule with S = e^(a x) + e^(-a x) and D = e^(a x)

- e^(-a x).

S' = a D and D' = a S, so f'(x) = a(S2 - D2) / S2.

Since S2 - D2 = 4, f'(x) = 4a / S2.

Answer: f'(x) = 4a / (e^(a x) + e^(-a x))2 = a sech2(a x).

Q1(vii). f(x) = sqrt(ln(e^(2x) + e^(-2x))). Put u = ln(e^(2x) + e^(-2x)); then f = sqrt(u) and du/dx = (2e^(2x) - 2e^(-2x)) / (e^(2x) + e^(-2x)).

By the chain rule, f'(x) = (1/(2 sqrt(u))) du/dx.

Answer: f'(x) = (e^(2x) - e^(-2x)) / [(e^(2x) + e^(-2x)) sqrt(ln(e^(2x) + e^(-2x)))].

Q1(viii). f(x) = ln(sqrt(e^(2x) + e^(-2x))). Write f(x) = (1/2) ln(e^(2x) + e^(-2x)).

Differentiate: f'(x) = (1/2) (2e^(2x) - 2e^(-2x)) / (e^(2x) + e^(-2x)).

Answer: f'(x) = (e^(2x) - e^(-2x)) / (e^(2x) + e^(-2x)).

Q2. Find dy/dx if

Q2(i). y = x2 ln sqrt(x). Write y = (1/2) x2 ln x.

By the product rule, dy/dx = x ln x + (1/2) x2 (1/x) = x ln x + x/2.

Answer: dy/dx = x(ln x + 1/2).

Q2(ii). y = x sqrt(ln x). Use the product rule: dy/dx = sqrt(ln x) + x (1/(2 sqrt(ln x))) (1/x).

Answer: dy/dx = sqrt(ln x) + 1/(2 sqrt(ln x)).

Q2(iii). y = x / ln x. Use the quotient rule: dy/dx = [(ln x) - x(1/x)] / (ln x)2.

Answer: dy/dx = (ln x - 1) / (ln x)2.

Q2(iv). y = x2 ln(1/x). Write y = -x2 ln x.

By the product rule, dy/dx = -2x ln x - x.

Answer: dy/dx = -x(2 ln x + 1).

Q2(v). y = ln sqrt((x2 - 1)/(x2 + 1)). Write y = (1/2)[ln(x2 - 1) - ln(x2 + 1)].

dy/dx = (1/2)[2x/(x2 - 1) - 2x/(x2 + 1)] = x[1/(x2 - 1) - 1/(x2 + 1)].

Answer: dy/dx = 2x / (x4 - 1).

Q2(vi). y = ln(x + sqrt(x2 + 1)). By the chain rule, dy/dx = [1 + x/sqrt(x2 + 1)] / (x + sqrt(x2 + 1)).

The numerator is (sqrt(x2 + 1) + x)/sqrt(x2 + 1), which cancels the denominator.

Answer: dy/dx = 1/sqrt(x2 + 1).

Q2(vii). y = ln(9 - x2). By the chain rule, dy/dx = (-2x)/(9 - x2).

Answer: dy/dx = -2x/(9 - x2).

Q2(viii). y = e^(-2x) sin 2x. Use the product rule: dy/dx = -2e^(-2x) sin 2x + 2e^(-2x) cos 2x.

Answer: dy/dx = 2e^(-2x)(cos 2x - sin 2x).

Q2(ix). y = e^(-x)(x3 + 2x2 + 1). Use the product rule: dy/dx = -e^(-x)(x3 + 2x2 + 1) + e^(-x)(3x2 + 4x).

Answer: dy/dx = e^(-x)(-x3 + x2 + 4x - 1).

Q2(x). y = x e^(sin x). Use the product rule: dy/dx = e^(sin x) + x e^(sin x) cos x.

Answer: dy/dx = e^(sin x)(1 + x cos x).

Q2(xi). y = 5e^(3x - 4).

By the chain rule, dy/dx = 5e^(3x - 4) x 3.

Answer: dy/dx = 15e^(3x - 4).

Q2(xii). y = (x + 1)^x. Take logarithms: ln y = x ln(x + 1).

Differentiate: y'/y = ln(x + 1) + x/(x + 1).

Answer: dy/dx = (x + 1)^x [ln(x + 1) + x/(x + 1)].

Q2(xiii). y = (ln x)^(ln x). Take logarithms: ln y = (ln x)(ln ln x).

Differentiate: y'/y = (1/x) ln ln x + (ln x)(1/(x ln x)) = (1 + ln ln x)/x.

Answer: dy/dx = (ln x)^(ln x) (1 + ln ln x)/x.

Q2(xiv). y = sqrt(x2 - 1)(x + 1) / (x3 + 1)^(3/2). Simplify first: x3 + 1 = (x + 1)(x2 - x + 1), so y = sqrt(x2 - 1) / [sqrt(x + 1)(x2 - x + 1)^(3/2)].

Take logarithms: ln y = (1/2) ln(x2 - 1) - (1/2) ln(x + 1) - (3/2) ln(x2 - x + 1).

Differentiate: y'/y = x/(x2 - 1) - 1/[2(x + 1)] - 3(2x - 1)/[2(x2 - x + 1)].

The first two terms combine to 1/[2(x - 1)], so y'/y = (-5x2 + 8x - 2)/[2(x - 1)(x2 - x + 1)].

Answer: dy/dx = y (-5x2 + 8x - 2) / [2(x - 1)(x2 - x + 1)], with y as given.

Q3. Find dy/dx if

Q3(i). y = cosh 2x. By the chain rule, dy/dx = 2 sinh 2x.

Answer: dy/dx = 2 sinh 2x.

Q3(ii). y = sinh 3x. By the chain rule, dy/dx = 3 cosh 3x.

Answer: dy/dx = 3 cosh 3x.

Q3(iii). y = tanh^{-1}(sin x), -pi/2 < x < pi/2. By the chain rule, dy/dx = [1/(1 - sin2 x)] cos x = cos x / cos2 x.

Answer: dy/dx = sec x.

Q3(iv). y = sinh^{-1}(x3). By the chain rule, dy/dx = (3x2)/sqrt(1 + x6).

Answer: dy/dx = 3x2/sqrt(1 + x6).

Q3(v). y = ln(tanh x).

By the chain rule, dy/dx = (1/tanh x) sech2 x = 1/(sinh x cosh x).

Answer: dy/dx = 2/sinh 2x.

Q3(vi). y = sinh^{-1}(x/2). By the chain rule, dy/dx = (1/2)/sqrt(1 + x2/4).

Answer: dy/dx = 1/sqrt(4 + x2).

mcqs.q: Find f'(x) if f(x) = e^(sqrt(x) - 1)
mcqs.why: Working: Put u = sqrt(x) - 1, f = e^u, du/dx = 1/(2 sqrt(x)). Chain rule: f'(x) = e^u du/dx = e^(sqrt(x) - 1)/(2 sqrt(x)).

mcqs.q: Find f'(x) if f(x) = x^3 e^(1/x), x not 0
mcqs.why: Working: Product rule: d/dx (x^3) = 3x^2 and d/dx (e^(1/x)) = e^(1/x)(-1/x^2). So f'(x) = 3x^2 e^(1/x) + x^3 e^(1/x)(-1/x^2) = e^(1/x)(3x^2 - x).

mcqs.q: Find f'(x) if f(x) = ln(e^x + e^(-x))
mcqs.why: Working: Chain rule for ln: f'(x) is the derivative of the inside divided by the inside. The inside e^x + e^(-x) has derivative e^x - e^(-x), so f'(x) = (e^x - e^(-x))/(e^x + e^(-x)), which is tanh x.

mcqs.q: Find dy/dx if y = x/ln x
mcqs.why: Working: Quotient rule: dy/dx = [(ln x)(1) - x(1/x)]/(ln x)^2. Since x(1/x) = 1, this simplifies to dy/dx = (ln x - 1)/(ln x)^2.

mcqs.q: Find dy/dx if y = ln(9 - x^2)
mcqs.why: Working: Chain rule for ln: differentiate the inside 9 - x^2 to get -2x, then divide by the inside itself. Hence dy/dx = (-2x)/(9 - x^2).

mcqs.q: Find dy/dx if y = e^(-2x) sin 2x
mcqs.why: Working: Product rule: dy/dx = -2e^(-2x) sin 2x + e^(-2x)(2 cos 2x). Factorising 2e^(-2x) gives dy/dx = 2e^(-2x)(cos 2x - sin 2x).

mcqs.q: Find dy/dx if y = 5e^(3x - 4)
mcqs.why: Working: Chain rule: the derivative of the exponent 3x - 4 is 3. Hence dy/dx = 5e^(3x - 4) x 3 = 15e^(3x - 4).

mcqs.q: Find dy/dx if y = (x + 1)^x
mcqs.why: Working: Take logarithms: ln y = x ln(x + 1). Differentiate: y'/y = ln(x + 1) + x/(x + 1). Multiplying by y gives dy/dx = (x + 1)^x [ln(x + 1) + x/(x + 1)].

mcqs.q: Find dy/dx if y = cosh 2x
mcqs.why: Working: The derivative of cosh u is sinh u, and here u = 2x with du/dx = 2. By the chain rule, dy/dx = sinh 2x x 2 = 2 sinh 2x.

mcqs.q: Find dy/dx if y = sinh^(-1) (x/2)
mcqs.why: Working: By the chain rule, dy/dx = (1/2)/sqrt(1 + x^2/4). Simplifying, (1/2)/sqrt((4 + x^2)/4) = (1/2)/(sqrt(4 + x^2)/2) = 1/sqrt(4 + x^2).

lessons.title: Exercise 2.7
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find y2 if

Q1(i). y = 2x5 - 3x4 + 4x3 + x - 2. First derivative: y1 = 10x4 - 12x3 + 12x2 + 1.

Second derivative: y2 = 40x3 - 36x2 + 24x.

Answer: y2 = 40x3 - 36x2 + 24x.

Q1(ii). y = (2x + 5)^(3/2). First derivative: y1 = 3(2x + 5)^(1/2).

Second derivative: y2 = 3(2x + 5)^(-1/2).

Answer: y2 = 3/sqrt(2x + 5).

Q1(iii). y = sqrt(x) + 1/sqrt(x).

Write y = x^(1/2) + x^(-1/2).

First derivative: y1 = (1/2)x^(-1/2) - (1/2)x^(-3/2).

Second derivative: y2 = -(1/4)x^(-3/2) + (3/4)x^(-5/2).

Answer: y2 = (3 - x) / (4 x^(5/2)).

Q2. Find y2 if

Q2(i). y = x2 e^(-x). First derivative: y1 = e^(-x)(2x - x2).

Second derivative: y2 = e^(-x)(2 - 2x) - e^(-x)(2x - x2).

Answer: y2 = e^(-x)(x2 - 4x + 2).

Q2(ii). y = ln((2x + 3)/(3x + 2)). First derivative: y1 = 2/(2x + 3) - 3/(3x + 2) = -5/[(2x + 3)(3x + 2)].

Second derivative: y2 = 5(12x + 13)/[(2x + 3)2(3x + 2)2].

Answer: y2 = 5(12x + 13) / [(2x + 3)2(3x + 2)2].

Q3. Find y2 if

Q3(i). x2 + y2 = a2.

Differentiate: 2x + 2y y1 = 0, so y1 = -x/y.

Differentiate again: y2 = [-(y) + x y1]/y2 = [-(y) - x2/y]/y2.

Since x2 + y2 = a2, this simplifies to y2 = -a2/y3.

Answer: y2 = -a2/y3.

Q3(ii). x3 - y3 = a. Differentiate: 3x2 - 3y2 y1 = 0, so y1 = x2/y2.

Differentiate again: y2 = [2x y2 - x2 (2y y1)]/y4 = 2x(y3 - x3)/y5.

Since x3 - y3 = a, y3 - x3 = -a.

Answer: y2 = -2a x/y5.

Q3(iii). x = a cos theta, y = a sin theta. dy/dx = (a cos theta)/(-a sin theta) = -cot theta.

y2 = [d/d theta (-cot theta)] / (dx/d theta) = cosec2 theta / (-a sin theta).

Answer: y2 = -1/(a sin3 theta).

Q3(iv). x = a t2, y = b t4. dx/dt = 2a t; dy/dt = 4b t3, so y1 = (2b/a) t2.

y2 = [d/dt (2b t2/a)] / (dx/dt) = (4b t/a)/(2a t).

Answer: y2 = 2b/a2.

Q3(v). x2 + y2 + 2g x + 2f y + c = 0. Differentiate: (x + g) + (y + f) y1 = 0, so y1 = -(x + g)/(y + f).

Differentiate again: 1 + (y1)2 + (y + f) y2 = 0, so y2 = -(1 + y1^2)/(y + f).

Answer: y2 = -[(y + f)2 + (x + g)2] / (y + f)3.

Q4. Find y4 if

Q4(i). y = sin 3x. y1 = 3 cos 3x; y2 = -9 sin 3x; y3 = -27 cos 3x.

Fourth derivative: y4 = 81 sin 3x.

Answer: y4 = 81 sin 3x.

Q4(ii). y = cos3 x. Use cos3 x = (3 cos x + cos 3x)/4.

Fourth derivatives: d4/dx4 cos x = cos x; d4/dx4 cos 3x = 81 cos 3x.

Answer: y4 = (3 cos x + 81 cos 3x)/4.

Q4(iii). y = ln(x2 - 9).

y1 = 2x/(x2 - 9); y2 = -2(x2 + 9)/(x2 - 9)2.

y3 = 4x(x2 + 27)/(x2 - 9)3.

Differentiating once more gives y4 = -12(x4 + 54x2 + 81)/(x2 - 9)4.

Answer: y4 = -12(x4 + 54x2 + 81) / (x2 - 9)4.

Q5. If x = sin theta, y = sin m theta, show that (1 - x2) y2 - x y1 + m2 y = 0

Q5. Proof. dx/d theta = cos theta; dy/d theta = m cos m theta, so y1 = m cos m theta / cos theta.

Differentiating y1 w.r.t. theta and dividing by dx/d theta gives y2 = m[-m sin m theta + cos m theta tan theta] / cos2 theta.

Now (1 - x2) = cos2 theta, so (1 - x2) y2 = -m2 sin m theta + m cos m theta tan theta.

Also -x y1 = -m sin theta cos m theta / cos theta = -m cos m theta tan theta.

Adding m2 y = m2 sin m theta cancels everything: total 0.

Answer: proved.

Q6. If y = e^x sin x, show that d2y/dx2 - 2 dy/dx + 2y = 0

Q6. Proof. y1 = e^x (sin x + cos x).

y2 = e^x (2 cos x).

Then y2 - 2y1 + 2y = e^x[2 cos x - 2 sin x - 2 cos x + 2 sin x] = 0.

Answer: proved.

Q7. If y = e^(a x) sin b x, show that d2y/dx2 - 2a dy/dx + (a2 + b2) y = 0

Q7. Proof. y1 = e^(a x)(a sin b x + b cos b x).

y2 = e^(a x)[(a2 - b2) sin b x + 2a b cos b x].

Then y2 - 2a y1 + (a2 + b2) y = e^(a x)[(a2 - b2 - 2a2 + a2 + b2) sin b x + (2a b 2a b) cos b x] = 0.

Answer: proved.

Q8. If y = (Cos^{-1} x)2, prove that (1 - x2) y2 - x y1 - 2 = 0

Q8. Proof.

y1 = 2 Cos^{-1} x (-1/sqrt(1 - x2)) = -2 Cos^{-1} x / sqrt(1 - x2).

So sqrt(1 - x2) y1 = -2 Cos^{-1} x.

Differentiate: (-x/sqrt(1 - x2)) y1 + sqrt(1 - x2) y2 = 2/sqrt(1 - x2).

Multiply by sqrt(1 - x2): -x y1 + (1 - x2) y2 = 2.

Answer: proved, (1 - x2) y2 - x y1 - 2 = 0.

Q9. If y = a cos(ln x) + b sin(ln x), prove that x2 d2y/dx2 + x dy/dx + y = 0

Q9. Proof. y1 = (-a sin(ln x) + b cos(ln x))/x, so x y1 = -a sin(ln x) + b cos(ln x).

Differentiating y1 by the quotient rule gives x2 y2 = -a cos(ln x) - b sin(ln x) + a sin(ln x) - b cos(ln x).

Add: x2 y2 + x y1 + y = (-a cos - b sin + a sin - b cos) + (-a sin + b cos) + (a cos + b sin) = 0.

Answer: proved.

mcqs.q: Find y2 if y = 2x^5 - 3x^4 + 4x^3 + x - 2
mcqs.why: Working: First derivative: y1 = 10x^4 - 12x^3 + 12x^2 + 1. Differentiate again term by term: 40x^3 - 36x^2 + 24x + 0, so y2 = 40x^3 - 36x^2 + 24x.

mcqs.q: Find y2 if y = (2x + 5)^(3/2)
mcqs.why: Working: First derivative: y1 = (3/2)(2x + 5)^(1/2) x 2 = 3(2x + 5)^(1/2). Differentiate again: y2 = 3 x (1/2)(2x + 5)^(-1/2) x 2 = 3(2x + 5)^(-1/2) = 3/sqrt(2x + 5).

mcqs.q: Find y2 if y = sqrt(x) + 1/sqrt(x)
Find y2 if y = x^2 e^(-x)
mcqs.why: Working: First derivative: y1 = e^(-x)(2x - x^2). Differentiate again: y2 = e^(-x)(2 - 2x) - e^(-x)(2x - x^2) = e^(-x)(x^2 - 4x + 2).

mcqs.q: Find y2 if x^2 + y^2 = a^2
mcqs.why: Working: Differentiate: 2x + 2y y1 = 0, so y1 = -x/y. Differentiate again: y2 = [-(y) + x y1]/y^2 = [-(y) - x^2/y]/y^2. Using x^2 + y^2 = a^2 this simplifies to y2 = -a^2/y^3.

mcqs.q: Find y2 if x = a t^2, y = b t^4
mcqs.why: Working: dx/dt = 2a t and dy/dt = 4b t^3, so y1 = (2b/a) t^2. Then y2 = [d/dt (2b t^2/a)]/(dx/dt) = (4b t/a)/(2a t) = 2b/a^2.

mcqs.q: Find y4 if y = sin 3x
mcqs.why: Working: Differentiate repeatedly: y1 = 3 cos 3x, y2 = -9 sin 3x, y3 = -27 cos 3x, and y4 = -27 x (-3 sin 3x) = 81 sin 3x.

mcqs.q: Find y4 if y = cos^3 x
mcqs.why: Working: Use cos^3 x = (3 cos x + cos 3x)/4. The fourth derivative of cos x is cos x and of cos 3x is 3^4 cos 3x = 81 cos 3x. Hence y4 = (3 cos x + 81 cos 3x)/4.

mcqs.q: The function y = e^x sin x satisfies which differential equation?
mcqs.why: Working: y1 = e^x (sin x + cos x) and y2 = e^x (2 cos x). Then y2 - 2y1 + 2y = e^x[2 cos x - 2 sin x - 2 cos x + 2 sin x] = 0, so y satisfies y2 - 2y1 + 2y = 0.

mcqs.q: If y = (Cos^(-1) x)^2, the proved relation is?
mcqs.why: Working: y1 = -2 Cos^(-1) x/sqrt(1 - x^2), so sqrt(1 - x^2) y1 = -2 Cos^(-1) x. Differentiating and multiplying by sqrt(1 - x^2) gives -x y1 + (1 - x^2) y2 = 2, i.e. (1 - x^2) y2 - x y1 - 2 = 0.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.8
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Apply the Maclaurin series expansion to prove that

Q1(i). ln(1 + x) = x - x2/2 + x3/3 - x4/4 + ...

Let f(x) = ln(1 + x). Then f(0) = 0.

f'(x) = 1/(1 + x), so f'(0) = 1; f''(x) = -1/(1 + x)2, so f''(0) = -1.

f'''(x) = 2/(1 + x)3, so f'''(0) = 2; f''''(x) = -6/(1 + x)4, so f''''(0) = -6.

Maclaurin: f(x) = f(0) + f'(0) x + f''(0) x2/2! + f'''(0) x3/3! + f''''(0) x4/4! + ...

So ln(1 + x) = x - x2/2 + x3/3 - x4/4 + ..., as required.

Answer: proved.

Q1(ii). cos x = 1 - x2/2! + x4/4! - x6/6! + ... Let f(x) = cos x. Then f(0) = 1, f'(0) = 0, f''(0) = -1, f'''(0) = 0, f''''(0) = 1, and the pattern repeats every four derivatives.

Maclaurin: f(x) = 1 + 0 x - x2/2! + 0 x3/3! + x4/4! + 0 x5/5! - x6/6! + ...

Answer: proved, cos x = 1 - x2/2! + x4/4! - x6/6! + ...

Q1(iii). sqrt(1 + x) = 1 + x/2 - x2/8 + x3/16 - ... Let f(x) = (1 + x)^(1/2). Then f(0) = 1.

f'(x) = (1/2)(1 + x)^(-1/2), so f'(0) = 1/2.

f''(x) = (-1/4)(1 + x)^(-3/2), so f''(0) = -1/4.

f'''(x) = (3/8)(1 + x)^(-5/2), so f'''(0) = 3/8.

Maclaurin: f(x) = 1 + (1/2) x + (-1/4) x2/2! + (3/8) x3/3! + ... = 1 + x/2 - x2/8 + x3/16 - ...

Answer: proved.

Q1(iv). e^x = 1 + x + x2/2! + x3/3! + ... Let f(x) = e^x. Every derivative is e^x, so every derivative at 0 is 1.

Maclaurin: f(x) = 1 + x + x2/2! + x3/3! + ...

Answer: proved.

Q1(v). e^(2x) = 1 + 2x + 4x2/2! + 8x3/3! + ... Let f(x) = e^(2x). Then f'(x) = 2e^(2x), f''(x) = 4e^(2x), f'''(x) = 8e^(2x), so f(0) = 1, f'(0) = 2, f''(0) = 4, f'''(0) = 8.

Maclaurin: f(x) = 1 + 2x + 4x2/2! + 8x3/3! + ...

Answer: proved.

Q2. Show that cos(x + h) = cos x - h sin x - (h2/2) cos x + (h3/6) sin x + ... and evaluate cos 61 degrees

Q2. Taylor expansion and cos 61 degrees. Let f(x) = cos x. Taylor in h: f(x + h) = f(x) + h f'(x) + (h2/2) f''(x) + (h3/6) f'''(x) + ...

With f'(x) = -sin x, f''(x) = -cos x, f'''(x) = sin x, this gives cos(x + h) = cos x - h sin x - (h2/2) cos x + (h3/6) sin x + ...

For cos 61 degrees, take x = 60 degrees and h = 1 degree = pi/180 radians approx. 0.017453.

cos 60 degrees = 0.5 and sin 60 degrees = sqrt(3)/2 approx. 0.8660.

cos 61 degrees approx. 0.5 - (0.017453)(0.8660) - (0.0174532/2)(0.5) = 0.5 0.015114 - 0.000076.

Answer: cos 61 degrees approx. 0.48481.

Q3. Show that 2^(x + h) = 2^x {1 + (ln 2) h + (ln 2)2 h2/2! + (ln 2)3 h3/3! + ...}

Q3. Proof. Let f(x) = 2^x. Then f'(x) = 2^x ln 2, f''(x) = 2^x (ln 2)2, f'''(x) = 2^x (ln 2)3, and so on.

Taylor in h: f(x + h) = f(x) + h f'(x) + (h2/2) f''(x) + (h3/6) f'''(x) + ...

Factor out 2^x: 2^(x + h) = 2^x [1 + (ln 2) h + (ln 2)2 h2/2! + (ln 2)3 h3/3! + ...].

Answer: proved.

mcqs.q: In the Maclaurin series for ln(1 + x), the term in x^2 is?
For f(x) = ln(1 + x), f''(0) equals?
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = 1/(1 + x) and f''(x) = -1/(1 + x)^2. Substituting x = 0 gives f''(0) = -1/(1)^2 = -1, which produces the -x^2/2 term in the Maclaurin series.

mcqs.q: In the Maclaurin series for cos x, the term in x^4 is?
mcqs.why: Working: For f(x) = cos x, f(0) = 1, f''(0) = -1 and f''''(0) = 1, with odd derivatives 0 at 0. The x^4 term is f''''(0) x^4/4! = x^4/4!, giving cos x = 1 - x^2/2! + x^4/4! - ...

mcqs.q: In the Maclaurin series for sqrt(1 + x), the term in x^2 is?
For f(x) = e^x, f'''(0) equals?
mcqs.why: Working: Every derivative of e^x is e^x itself: f'(x) = f''(x) = f'''(x) = e^x. Substituting x = 0 gives f'''(0) = e^0 = 1, which is why every Maclaurin coefficient is 1/n!.

mcqs.q: The Maclaurin series of e^(2x) up to the x^2 term is?
Using the Taylor expansion of cos(x + h) with x = 60 degrees and h = 1 degree, cos 61 degrees is approximately?
In the Taylor expansion cos(x + h) = cos x - h sin x - (h^2/2) cos x + ..., the coefficient of h^2 is?
mcqs.why: Working: Taylor: f(x + h) = f(x) + h f'(x) + (h^2/2) f''(x) + ... For f = cos, f''(x) = -cos x, so the h^2 term is (h^2/2)(-cos x), i.e. the coefficient of h^2 is -(1/2) cos x.

mcqs.q: For f(x) = 2^x, f'(x) equals?
mcqs.why: Working: Differentiating 2^x repeatedly gives f'(x) = 2^x ln 2, f''(x) = 2^x (ln 2)^2 and f'''(x) = 2^x (ln 2)^3. This is what produces the Taylor series 2^(x + h) = 2^x {1 + (ln 2) h + (ln 2)^2 h^2/2! + ...}.

mcqs.q: For f(x) = sqrt(1 + x), f'(0) equals?
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = (1/2)(1 + x)^(-1/2). Substituting x = 0 gives f'(0) = (1/2)(1)^(-1/2) = 1/2, which is the coefficient of x in sqrt(1 + x) = 1 + x/2 - x^2/8 + ...

lessons.title: Exercise 2.9
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Determine the intervals in which f is increasing or decreasing for the domain mentioned in each case

Q1(i). f(x) = sin x, x in (-pi, pi). f'(x) = cos x.

cos x > 0 on (-pi/2, pi/2), so f is increasing there.

cos x < 0 on (-pi, -pi/2) and on (pi/2, pi), so f is decreasing there.

Answer: increasing on (-pi/2, pi/2); decreasing on (-pi, -pi/2) and (pi/2, pi).

Q1(ii). f(x) = cos x, x in (-pi/2, pi/2). f'(x) = -sin x.

-sin x > 0 when sin x < 0, i.e. on (-pi/2, 0), so f is increasing there.

-sin x < 0 on (0, pi/2), so f is decreasing there.

Answer: increasing on (-pi/2, 0); decreasing on (0, pi/2).

Q1(iii). f(x) = 4 - x2, x in (-2, 2). f'(x) = -2x.

f'(x) > 0 for x < 0, so f is increasing on (-2, 0).

f'(x) < 0 for x > 0, so f is decreasing on (0, 2).

Answer: increasing on (-2, 0); decreasing on (0, 2).

Q1(iv). f(x) = x2 + 3x + 2, x in (-4, 1). f'(x) = 2x + 3, which is zero at x = -3/2.

f'(x) < 0 for x < -3/2, so f is decreasing on (-4, -3/2).

f'(x) > 0 for x > -3/2, so f is increasing on (-3/2, 1).

Answer: decreasing on (-4, -3/2); increasing on (-3/2, 1).

Q2. Find the extreme values for the following functions

Q2(i). f(x) = 1 - x3. f'(x) = -3x2, which is zero only at x = 0; f''(0) = 0.

f'(x) <= 0 on both sides of 0, so f does not change from increasing to decreasing or back.

Answer: no maximum or minimum; (0, 1) is a point of inflexion.

Q2(ii). f(x) = x2 - x - 2. f'(x) = 2x - 1, zero at x = 1/2; f''(x) = 2 > 0.

So f has a minimum at x = 1/2, value 1/4 - 1/2 - 2 = -9/4.

Answer: minimum value -9/4 at x = 1/2.

Q2(iii). f(x) = 5x2 - 6x + 2. f'(x) = 10x - 6, zero at x = 3/5; f''(x) = 10 > 0.

So f has a minimum at x = 3/5, value 5(9/25) - 6(3/5) + 2 = 1/5.

Answer: minimum value 1/5 at x = 3/5.

Q2(iv). f(x) = 3x2. f'(x) = 6x, zero at x = 0; f''(x) = 6 > 0.

So f has a minimum at x = 0, value 0.

Answer: minimum value 0 at x = 0.

Q2(v). f(x) = 3x2 - 4x + 5. f'(x) = 6x - 4, zero at x = 2/3; f''(x) = 6 > 0.

So f has a minimum at x = 2/3, value 3(4/9) - 4(2/3) + 5 = 11/3.

Answer: minimum value 11/3 at x = 2/3.

Q2(vi). f(x) = 2x3 - 2x2 - 36x + 3. f'(x) = 6x2 - 4x - 36 = 2(3x2 - 2x - 18), zero at x = (1 + sqrt(55))/3 and x = (1 sqrt(55))/3.

f''(x) = 12x - 4: positive at the first point, negative at the second.

Using 3x2 - 2x - 18 = 0 to reduce the value gives f = (-220x - 9)/9 at a critical point.

Answer: maximum value (220 sqrt(55) - 247)/27 approx. 51.28 at x = (1 sqrt(55))/3; minimum value -(220 sqrt(55) + 247)/27 approx. -69.57 at x = (1 + sqrt(55))/3.

Q2(vii). f(x) = x4 - 4x2. f'(x) = 4x3 - 8x = 4x(x2 - 2), zero at x = 0 and x = plus or minus sqrt(2).

f''(x) = 12x2 - 8: at x = 0 it is -8 (maximum, value 0); at x = plus or minus sqrt(2) it is 16 (minimum, value 4 - 8 = -4).

Answer: maximum value 0 at x = 0; minimum value -4 at x = sqrt(2) and at x = -sqrt(2).

Q2(viii). f(x) = (x - 2)2(x - 1). Expand: f(x) = x3 - 5x2 + 8x - 4.

f'(x) = 3x2 - 10x + 8 = (3x - 4)(x - 2), zero at x = 4/3 and x = 2.

f''(x) = 6x - 10: at x = 4/3 it is -2 (maximum, value (4/9)(1/3) = 4/27); at x = 2 it is 2 (minimum, value 0).

Answer: maximum value 4/27 at x = 4/3; minimum value 0 at x = 2.

Q2(ix). f(x) = 5 + 3x - x3. f'(x) = 3 - 3x2, zero at x = 1 and x = -1; f''(x) = -6x.

At x = -1, f'' = 6 > 0: minimum value 5 - 3 + 1 = 3.

At x = 1, f'' = -6 < 0: maximum value 5 + 3 - 1 = 7.

Answer: minimum value 3 at x = -1; maximum value 7 at x = 1.

Q3. Find the maximum and minimum values of f(x) = sin x + cos x in the interval [0, 2pi]

Q3. Maxima and minima on [0, 2pi]. f'(x) = cos x - sin x, zero when tan x = 1, i.e. at x = pi/4 and x = 5pi/4 in [0, 2pi].

f''(x) = -sin x - cos x: at pi/4 it is -sqrt(2) < 0 (maximum); at 5pi/4 it is sqrt(2) > 0 (minimum).

f(pi/4) = sqrt(2)/2 + sqrt(2)/2 = sqrt(2); f(5pi/4) = -sqrt(2).

Endpoint values f(0) = f(2pi) = 1 lie between these.

Answer: maximum value sqrt(2) at x = pi/4; minimum value -sqrt(2) at x = 5pi/4.

Q4. Show that y = (ln x)/x has maximum value at x = e

Q4. Proof. y' = (1 - ln x)/x2, which is zero when ln x = 1, i.e. at x = e.

For x < e, 1 - ln x > 0 so y is increasing; for x > e, 1 - ln x < 0 so y is decreasing.

So y changes from increasing to decreasing at x = e.

Answer: proved, y has its maximum value 1/e at x = e.

Q5. Show that y = x^x has a minimum value at x = 1/e

Q5. Proof. Take logarithms: ln y = x ln x.

Differentiate: y'/y = ln x + 1, which is zero when ln x = -1, i.e. at x = 1/e.

For x < 1/e, ln x + 1 < 0 so y is decreasing; for x > 1/e it is positive so y is increasing.

So y changes from decreasing to increasing at x = 1/e.

Answer: proved, y has its minimum value (1/e)^(1/e) at x = 1/e.

mcqs.q: For f(x) = sin x on (-pi, pi), f is increasing on?
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = cos x. cos x > 0 on (-pi/2, pi/2), so f is increasing there; cos x < 0 on (-pi, -pi/2) and (pi/2, pi), where f is decreasing.

mcqs.q: For f(x) = cos x on (-pi/2, pi/2), f is decreasing on?
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = -sin x. On (0, pi/2), sin x > 0 so -sin x < 0 and f is decreasing there; on (-pi/2, 0), -sin x > 0 and f is increasing.

mcqs.q: For f(x) = 4 - x^2 on (-2, 2), f is increasing on?
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = -2x. f'(x) > 0 when -2x > 0, i.e. for x < 0, so f is increasing on (-2, 0); f'(x) < 0 for x > 0, so f is decreasing on (0, 2).

mcqs.q: For f(x) = x^2 + 3x + 2 on (-4, 1), f is decreasing on?
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = 2x + 3, which is zero at x = -3/2. f'(x) < 0 for x < -3/2, so f is decreasing on (-4, -3/2); f'(x) > 0 for x > -3/2, so f is increasing on (-3/2, 1).

mcqs.q: For f(x) = 1 - x^3, the extreme values are?
options: No maximum or minimum; (0, 1) is a point of inflexion
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = -3x^2, zero only at x = 0, and f''(0) = 0. f'(x) <= 0 on both sides of 0, so f does not change from increasing to decreasing or back: there is no maximum or minimum, and (0, 1) is a point of inflexion.

mcqs.q: For f(x) = x^2 - x - 2, the minimum value is?
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = 2x - 1, zero at x = 1/2, and f''(x) = 2 > 0, so this is a minimum. The value is f(1/2) = 1/4 - 1/2 - 2 = -9/4.

mcqs.q: For f(x) = 5x^2 - 6x + 2, the minimum value is?
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = 10x - 6, zero at x = 3/5, and f''(x) = 10 > 0, so this is a minimum. The value is f(3/5) = 5(9/25) - 6(3/5) + 2 = 9/5 - 18/5 + 10/5 = 1/5.

mcqs.q: For f(x) = x^4 - 4x^2, the minimum value is?
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = 4x^3 - 8x = 4x(x^2 - 2), zero at 0 and plus or minus sqrt(2). f''(x) = 12x^2 - 8 is 16 > 0 at plus or minus sqrt(2), and the value there is 4 - 8 = -4, so the minimum value is -4.

mcqs.q: The maximum of f(x) = sin x + cos x on [0, 2pi] is?
mcqs.why: Working: f'(x) = cos x - sin x, zero when tan x = 1, at pi/4 and 5pi/4. f''(pi/4) = -sqrt(2) < 0, so pi/4 gives a maximum, with value f(pi/4) = sqrt(2)/2 + sqrt(2)/2 = sqrt(2).

mcqs.q: The function y = (ln x)/x has its maximum value at?
mcqs.why: Working: y' = (1 - ln x)/x^2, zero when ln x = 1, i.e. x = e. For x < e, y' > 0 (increasing) and for x > e, y' < 0 (decreasing), so the maximum is at x = e, with value (ln e)/e = 1/e.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.10
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find two positive integers whose sum is 30 and their product will be maximum

Q1. Two numbers, sum 30, product maximum. Let one number be x; the other is 30 - x. Product P = x(30 - x) = 30x - x2.

P' = 30 - 2x, zero at x = 15; P'' = -2 < 0, so this is a maximum.

The numbers are 15 and 15.

Answer: 15 and 15, maximum product 225.

Q2. Divide 20 into two parts so that the sum of their squares will be minimum

Q2. Two parts of 20, sum of squares minimum. Let one part be x; the other is 20 - x. Sum S = x2 + (20 - x)2.

S' = 2x - 2(20 - x) = 4x - 40, zero at x = 10; S'' = 4 > 0, so this is a minimum.

The parts are 10 and 10.

Answer: 10 and 10, minimum sum of squares 200.

Q3. Find two positive integers whose sum is 12 and the product of one with the square of the other will be maximum

Q3. Two numbers, sum 12, x(12 - x)2 maximum. Let the numbers be x and 12 - x. Product P = x(12 - x)2.

P' = (12 - x)2 - 2x(12 - x) = (12 - x)(12 - 3x), zero at x = 12 or x = 4 (x = 12 gives product 0, rejected).

P'' at x = 4 is negative, so this is a maximum.

The numbers are 4 and 8.

Answer: 4 and 8, maximum product 4 x 64 = 256.

Q4. The perimeter of a triangle is 16 centimetres. If one side is of length 6 cm, what are the lengths of the other sides for maximum area of the triangle?

Q4. Triangle, perimeter 16, one side 6, maximum area. Let the other sides be x and 10 - x (since 6 + x + (10 - x) = 16). Semiperimeter s = 8.

By Heron, (area)2 = 8(8 - 6)(8 - x)(8 - (10 - x)) = 16(8 - x)(x - 2) = 16(-x2 + 10x 16).

Maximise -x2 + 10x - 16: derivative -2x + 10, zero at x = 5; second derivative -2 < 0.

The other sides are 5 cm and 5 cm.

Answer: 5 cm and 5 cm (with the given 6 cm side).

Q5. Find the dimensions of a rectangle of largest area having perimeter 120 centimetres

Q5. Rectangle, perimeter 120, largest area. Let one side be x; the other is 60 - x. Area A = x(60 - x).

A' = 60 - 2x, zero at x = 30; A'' = -2 < 0, so this is a maximum.

The sides are 30 cm and 30 cm.

Answer: 30 cm by 30 cm (a square), area 900 cm2.

Q6. Find the lengths of the sides of a variable rectangle having area 36 cm2 when its perimeter is minimum

Q6. Rectangle, area 36, perimeter minimum. Let one side be x; the other is 36/x. Perimeter P = 2x + 72/x.

P' = 2 - 72/x2, zero at x2 = 36, i.e. x = 6 (positive side). P'' = 144/x3 > 0, so this is a minimum.

The sides are 6 cm and 6 cm.

Answer: 6 cm by 6 cm (a square), perimeter 24 cm.

Q7. A box with a square base and open top is to have a volume of 4 cubic dm. Find the dimensions of the box which will require the least material

Q7. Open-top square-base box, volume 4, least material. Let the base side be x dm and the height be h dm. Volume x2 h = 4, so h = 4/x2.

Material (surface) S = base + 4 sides = x2 + 4x h = x2 + 16/x.

S' = 2x - 16/x2, zero at x3 = 8, i.e. x = 2; S'' = 2 + 32/x3 > 0, so this is a minimum.

Then h = 4/4 = 1 dm.

Answer: base 2 dm by 2 dm, height 1 dm.

Q8. Find the dimensions of a rectangular garden having perimeter 80 metres if its area is to be maximum

Q8. Garden, perimeter 80, maximum area. Let one side be x metres; the other is 40 - x. Area A = x(40 - x).

A' = 40 - 2x, zero at x = 20; A'' = -2 < 0, so this is a maximum.

The sides are 20 m and 20 m.

Answer: 20 m by 20 m (a square), area 400 m2.

Q9. An open tank of square base of side x and vertical sides is to be constructed to contain a given quantity of water. Find the depth in terms of x if the expense of lining the inside of the tank with lead will be least

Q9. Open tank, square base x, least lining area, depth in terms of x. Let the volume be V and the depth be h. Then V = x2 h, so h = V/x2.

Lining area A = base + 4 sides = x2 + 4x h = x2 + 4V/x.

A' = 2x - 4V/x2, zero at x3 = 2V, i.e. V = x3/2.

Then h = V/x2 = x/2.

Answer: depth h = x/2, i.e. half the side of the base.

Q10. Find the dimensions of the rectangle of maximum area which fits inside the semi-circle of radius 8 cm as shown in the figure

Q10. Largest rectangle in a semicircle of radius 8 cm. Let the half-width be x cm; the height is sqrt(64 - x2) cm, since the top corner lies on the circle.

Area A = 2x sqrt(64 - x2). Maximise A2 = 4x2(64 - x2).

d/dx [x2(64 - x2)] = 128x - 4x3, zero (for x > 0) at x2 = 32, i.e. x = 4 sqrt(2).

Height = sqrt(64 - 32) = 4 sqrt(2) cm; full width = 2x = 8 sqrt(2) cm.

Answer: width 8 sqrt(2) cm, height 4 sqrt(2) cm, area 64 cm2.

Q11. Find the point on the curve y = x2 - 1 that is closest to the point (3, -1)

Q11. Closest point on y = x2 - 1 to (3, -1). Let the point be (x, x2 - 1). Squared distance D = (x - 3)2 + (x2 - 1 + 1)2 = (x - 3)2 + x4.

D' = 2(x - 3) + 4x3 = 2(2x3 + x - 3).

2x3 + x - 3 = (x - 1)(2x2 + 2x + 3); the quadratic has discriminant 4 - 24 < 0, so the only real critical point is x = 1.

D'' = 2 + 12x2 > 0, so this is a minimum.

Answer: the point (1, 0).

Q12. Find the point on the curve y = x2 + 1 that is closest to the point (18, 1)

Q12. Closest point on y = x2 + 1 to (18, 1). Let the point be (x, x2 + 1). Squared distance D = (x - 18)2 + (x2 + 1 - 1)2 = (x 18)2 + x4.

D' = 2(x - 18) + 4x3 = 2(2x3 + x - 18).

2x3 + x - 18 = (x - 2)(2x2 + 4x + 9); the quadratic has discriminant 16 - 72 < 0, so the only real critical point is x = 2.

D'' = 2 + 12x2 > 0, so this is a minimum.

Answer: the point (2, 5).

mcqs.q: Two positive integers have sum 30 and maximum product. The numbers and product are?
mcqs.why: Working: Let one number be x, the other 30 - x. P = x(30 - x) = 30x - x^2, P' = 30 - 2x = 0 gives x = 15, and P'' = -2 < 0 confirms a maximum. The numbers are 15 and 15, product 15 x 15 = 225.

mcqs.q: Divide 20 into two parts so the sum of their squares is minimum. The parts are?
mcqs.why: Working: Let one part be x, the other 20 - x. S = x^2 + (20 - x)^2, S' = 2x - 2(20 - x) = 4x - 40 = 0 gives x = 10, and S'' = 4 > 0 confirms a minimum. The parts are 10 and 10, minimum sum 100 + 100 = 200.

mcqs.q: Two positive integers have sum 12, and the product of one with the square of the other is maximum. The numbers are?
mcqs.why: Working: P = x(12 - x)^2, P' = (12 - x)^2 - 2x(12 - x) = (12 - x)(12 - 3x) = 0 gives x = 4 (x = 12 gives product 0, rejected), and P'' at 4 is negative. The numbers are 4 and 8, product 4 x 64 = 256.

mcqs.q: A triangle has perimeter 16 cm and one side 6 cm. For maximum area, the other sides are?
mcqs.why: Working: The other sides are x and 10 - x, s = 8. By Heron, (area)^2 = 8(2)(8 - x)(x - 2) = 16(-x^2 + 10x - 16). Maximise -x^2 + 10x - 16: derivative -2x + 10 = 0 gives x = 5, second derivative -2 < 0. The other sides are 5 cm and 5 cm.

mcqs.q: The rectangle of largest area with perimeter 120 cm has sides?
mcqs.why: Working: Let one side be x, the other 60 - x. A = x(60 - x), A' = 60 - 2x = 0 gives x = 30, and A'' = -2 < 0 confirms a maximum. The sides are 30 cm and 30 cm (a square), area 900 cm^2.

mcqs.q: A rectangle has area 36 cm^2 and minimum perimeter. Its sides are?
mcqs.why: Working: Let one side be x, the other 36/x. P = 2x + 72/x, P' = 2 - 72/x^2 = 0 gives x^2 = 36, x = 6, and P'' = 144/x^3 > 0 confirms a minimum. The sides are 6 cm and 6 cm, perimeter 24 cm.

mcqs.q: An open-top box with square base has volume 4 cubic dm and uses least material. Its dimensions are?
mcqs.why: Working: Base side x, height h, x^2 h = 4 so h = 4/x^2. Material S = x^2 + 4x h = x^2 + 16/x, S' = 2x - 16/x^2 = 0 gives x^3 = 8, x = 2, and S'' > 0. Then h = 4/4 = 1 dm: base 2 dm by 2 dm, height 1 dm.

mcqs.q: A rectangular garden has perimeter 80 m and maximum area. Its sides are?
mcqs.why: Working: Let one side be x metres, the other 40 - x. A = x(40 - x), A' = 40 - 2x = 0 gives x = 20, and A'' = -2 < 0 confirms a maximum. The sides are 20 m and 20 m (a square), area 400 m^2.

mcqs.q: An open tank has square base of side x and given volume. For least lining expense, the depth h in terms of x is?
mcqs.why: Working: V = x^2 h so h = V/x^2. Lining area A = x^2 + 4x h = x^2 + 4V/x, A' = 2x - 4V/x^2 = 0 gives x^3 = 2V, i.e. V = x^3/2. Then h = V/x^2 = (x^3/2)/x^2 = x/2, half the side of the base.

mcqs.q: The rectangle of maximum area inside a semicircle of radius 8 cm has dimensions?
options: Width 8 sqrt(2) cm, height 4 sqrt(2) cm
Width 4 sqrt(2) cm, height 8 sqrt(2) cm
mcqs.why: Working: Half-width x, height sqrt(64 - x^2), A = 2x sqrt(64 - x^2). Maximise A^2 = 4x^2(64 - x^2): d/dx [x^2(64 - x^2)] = 128x - 4x^3 = 0 gives x^2 = 32, x = 4 sqrt(2). Height = sqrt(64 - 32) = 4 sqrt(2) cm and full width = 2x = 8 sqrt(2) cm, area 64 cm^2.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find delta y and dy in the following cases (delta y = exact change, dy = differential approximation)

Q1(i). y = x2 - 1, when x changes from 3 to 3.02. dx = 3.02 - 3 = 0.02.

dy = f'(x) dx = 2x dx = 2(3)(0.02) = 0.12.

Exact change: delta y = f(3.02) - f(3) = (9.1204 - 1) - (9 - 1) = 0.1204.

Answer: dy = 0.12, delta y = 0.1204.

Q1(ii). y = x2 + 2x, when x changes from 2 to 1.8. dx = 1.8 - 2 = -0.2.

dy = f'(x) dx = (2x + 2) dx = (6)(-0.2) = -1.2.

Exact change: delta y = f(1.8) - f(2) = (3.24 + 3.6) - (4 + 4) = -1.16.

Answer: dy = -1.2, delta y = -1.16.

Q1(iii). y = sqrt(x), when x changes from 4 to 4.41. dx = 4.41 - 4 = 0.41.

dy = f'(x) dx = dx / (2 sqrt(x)) = 0.41 / 4 = 0.1025.

Exact change: delta y = sqrt(4.41) - sqrt(4) = 2.1 - 2 = 0.1.

Answer: dy = 0.1025, delta y = 0.1.

Q2. Using differentials find dy/dx and dx/dy in the following equations

Q2(i). x y + x = 4. Differentiate both sides: y dx + x dy + dx = 0.

So (y + 1) dx + x dy = 0, giving dy/dx = -(y + 1)/x.

Answer: dy/dx = -(y + 1)/x, dx/dy = -x/(y + 1).

Q2(ii). x2 + 2y2 = 16. Differentiate both sides: 2x dx + 4y dy = 0.

So dy/dx = -x/(2y).

Answer: dy/dx = -x/(2y), dx/dy = -2y/x.

Q2(iii). x4 + y2 = x y2. Differentiate both sides: 4x3 dx + 2y dy = y2 dx + 2x y dy.

Collect: (2y - 2x y) dy = (y2 - 4x3) dx.

Answer: dy/dx = (y2 - 4x3)/(2y - 2x y), dx/dy = (2y - 2x y)/(y2 - 4x3).

Q2(iv). x y - ln x = c.

Differentiate both sides: y dx + x dy - dx/x = 0.

So x dy = (1/x - y) dx, giving dy/dx = 1/x2 - y/x.

Answer: dy/dx = (1 - x y)/x2, dx/dy = x2/(1 - x y).

Q3. Use differentials to approximate the values of

Q3(i). (17)^(1/4). Let f(x) = x^(1/4). Take x = 16, dx = 1, so f(16) = 2.

f'(x) = 1/(4 x^(3/4)), so f'(16) = 1/(4 x 8) = 1/32 = 0.03125.

dy = f'(16) dx = 0.03125.

Answer: (17)^(1/4) approx. 2 + 0.03125 = 2.03125.

Q3(ii). (31)^(1/5). Let f(x) = x^(1/5). Take x = 32, dx = -1, so f(32) = 2.

f'(x) = 1/(5 x^(4/5)), so f'(32) = 1/(5 x 16) = 1/80 = 0.0125.

dy = f'(32) dx = -0.0125.

Answer: (31)^(1/5) approx. 2 - 0.0125 = 1.9875.

Q3(iii). cos 29 degrees.

Let f(x) = cos x. Take x = 30 degrees, dx = -1 degree = -pi/180 approx. -0.017453 radians.

dy = -sin x dx = -sin 30 degrees x (-0.017453) = (0.5)(0.017453) = 0.008727.

cos 30 degrees = sqrt(3)/2 approx. 0.8660.

Answer: cos 29 degrees approx. 0.8660 + 0.008727 = 0.87473.

Q3(iv). sin 61 degrees. Let f(x) = sin x. Take x = 60 degrees, dx = 1 degree = pi/180 approx. 0.017453 radians.

dy = cos x dx = (0.5)(0.017453) = 0.008727.

sin 60 degrees = sqrt(3)/2 approx. 0.8660.

Answer: sin 61 degrees approx. 0.8660 + 0.008727 = 0.87473.

Q4. Find the approximate increase in the volume of a cube if the length of its each edge changes from 5 to 5.02

Q4. Cube edge 5 to 5.02. Let V = x3, with x = 5 and dx = 0.02.

dV = 3x2 dx = 3(25)(0.02) = 1.5.

Answer: approximate increase in volume 1.5 cubic units (exact increase 5.02^3 125 = 1.506 approx.).

Q5. Find the approximate increase in the area of a circular disc if its diameter is ? (FLAGGED: values not legible in the source copy)

Q5. FLAGGED - question incomplete in the source copy; no numerical answer given. As printed in this copy, Q5 reads: 'Find the approximate increase in the area of a circular disc if its diameter is ?' - the diameter value and its change are not legible (a '?' stands where the numbers should be).

Method (general): for diameter d, area A = pi d2 / 4, so dA = (pi d / 2) dd.

Once the diameter and its change are known, substitute them in dA = (pi d / 2) dd.

Answer: NOT COMPUTED - the printed values are missing in the source copy; nothing has been invented here.

mcqs.q: For y = x^2 - 1, when x changes from 3 to 3.02, what is the differential dy?
mcqs.why: dx = 3.02 - 3 = 0.02. dy = f'(x) dx = 2x dx, so at x = 3: dy = 2(3)(0.02) = 0.12. This is the differential approximation, not the exact change.

mcqs.q: For y = x^2 - 1, when x changes from 3 to 3.02, what is the exact change delta y?
For y = x^2 + 2x, when x changes from 2 to 1.8, what is dy?
For y = sqrt(x), when x changes from 4 to 4.41, what is dy?
For y = sqrt(x), when x changes from 4 to 4.41, what is the exact change delta y?
mcqs.why: delta y = f(4.41) - f(4) = sqrt(4.41) - sqrt(4) = 2.1 - 2 = 0.1 exactly, while the differential approximation dy = 0.1025 is slightly bigger.

mcqs.q: Using differentials, for x y + x = 4, what is dy/dx?
mcqs.why: Differentiate term by term: y dx + x dy + dx = 0, so (y + 1) dx + x dy = 0. Hence x dy = -(y + 1) dx and dy/dx = -(y + 1)/x.

mcqs.q: Using differentials, for x^2 + 2y^2 = 16, what is dy/dx?
mcqs.why: Differentiating both sides gives 2x dx + 4y dy = 0, so 4y dy = -2x dx and dy/dx = -2x/(4y) = -x/(2y).

mcqs.q: Using differentials, for x^4 + y^2 = x y^2, what is dy/dx?
mcqs.why: Differentiate: 4x^3 dx + 2y dy = y^2 dx + 2xy dy. Collect dy terms: (2y - 2xy) dy = (y^2 - 4x^3) dx, so dy/dx = (y^2 - 4x^3)/(2y - 2xy).

lessons.title: Exercise 3.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Evaluate the following indefinite integrals (c = constant of integration)

Q1(i). Int (3x2 - 2x + 1) dx. Integrate term by term: Int 3x2 dx = x3; Int (-2x) dx = -x2; Int 1 dx = x.

Answer: x3 - x2 + x + c.

Q1(ii). Int (sqrt(x) + 1/sqrt(x)) dx, x > 0.

Write as Int (x^(1/2) + x^(-1/2)) dx.

Int x^(1/2) dx = (2/3) x^(3/2); Int x^(-1/2) dx = 2 x^(1/2).

Answer: (2/3) x^(3/2) + 2 sqrt(x) + c.

Q1(iii). Int x(sqrt(x) + 1) dx, x > 0. Expand: x(sqrt(x) + 1) = x^(3/2) + x.

Int x^(3/2) dx = (2/5) x^(5/2); Int x dx = x2/2.

Answer: (2/5) x^(5/2) + x2/2 + c.

Q1(iv). Int (2x + 3)^(1/2) dx. Put u = 2x + 3; then du = 2 dx, so dx = du/2.

Int u^(1/2) (du/2) = (1/2) (2/3) u^(3/2) = (1/3) u^(3/2).

Answer: (2x + 3)^(3/2) / 3 + c.

Q1(v). Int (sqrt(x) + 1)2 dx, x > 0. Expand: (sqrt(x) + 1)2 = x + 2 sqrt(x) + 1.

Int x dx = x2/2; Int 2 sqrt(x) dx = (4/3) x^(3/2); Int 1 dx = x.

Answer: x2/2 + (4/3) x^(3/2) + x + c.

Q1(vi). Int (sqrt(x) - 1/sqrt(x))2 dx, x > 0.

Expand: (sqrt(x) - 1/sqrt(x))2 = x - 2 + 1/x.

Int x dx = x2/2; Int (-2) dx = -2x; Int (1/x) dx = ln x.

Answer: x2/2 - 2x + ln x + c.

Q1(vii). Int (3x + 2)/sqrt(x) dx, x > 0. Divide: (3x + 2)/sqrt(x) = 3 sqrt(x) + 2/sqrt(x).

Int 3 sqrt(x) dx = 2 x^(3/2); Int 2/sqrt(x) dx = 4 sqrt(x).

Answer: 2 x^(3/2) + 4 sqrt(x) + c.

Q1(viii). Int sqrt(y)(y + 1)/y dy, y > 0. Simplify: sqrt(y)(y + 1)/y = sqrt(y) + 1/sqrt(y).

Int sqrt(y) dy = (2/3) y^(3/2); Int 1/sqrt(y) dy = 2 sqrt(y).

Answer: (2/3) y^(3/2) + 2 sqrt(y) + c.

Q1(ix). Int (sqrt(theta) - 1)2/sqrt(theta) d theta, theta > 0. Expand the numerator: (sqrt(theta) - 1)2 = theta - 2 sqrt(theta) + 1.

Divide by sqrt(theta): sqrt(theta) - 2 + theta^(-1/2).

Integrate: (2/3) theta^(3/2) - 2 theta + 2 sqrt(theta).

Answer: (2/3) theta^(3/2) - 2 theta + 2 sqrt(theta) + c.

Q1(x). Int (1 - sqrt(x))2/sqrt(x) dx, x > 0. Expand the numerator: 1 - 2 sqrt(x) + x; divide by sqrt(x): x^(-1/2) - 2 + sqrt(x).

Integrate: 2 sqrt(x) - 2x + (2/3) x^(3/2).

Answer: 2 sqrt(x) - 2x + (2/3) x^(3/2) + c.

Q1(xi). Int (e^(2x) + e^x)/e^x dx. Divide: (e^(2x) + e^x)/e^x = e^x + 1.

Int e^x dx = e^x; Int 1 dx = x.

Answer: e^x + x + c.

Q2. Evaluate (c = constant of integration)

Q2(i). Int dx / (sqrt(x + a) + sqrt(x + b)), x + a > 0, x + b > 0. Rationalize: multiply top and bottom by (sqrt(x + a) - sqrt(x + b)).

The denominator becomes (x + a) - (x + b) = a - b.

So the integral = (1/(a - b)) Int (sqrt(x + a) - sqrt(x + b)) dx.

Answer: [(2/3)(x + a)^(3/2) - (2/3)(x + b)^(3/2)] / (a - b) + c.

Q2(ii). Int (1 - x2)/(1 + x2) dx.

Divide: (1 - x2)/(1 + x2) = -1 + 2/(1 + x2).

Int (-1) dx = -x; Int 2/(1 + x2) dx = 2 Tan^{-1} x.

Answer: -x + 2 Tan^{-1} x + c.

Q2(iii). Int dx / (sqrt(x + a) + sqrt(x)), x > 0, a > 0. Rationalize: multiply top and bottom by (sqrt(x + a) - sqrt(x)).

The denominator becomes a, so the integral = (1/a) Int (sqrt(x + a) - sqrt(x)) dx.

Answer: [(2/3)(x + a)^(3/2) - (2/3) x^(3/2)] / a + c.

Q2(iv). Int (a - 2x)^(3/2) dx. Put u = a - 2x; then du = -2 dx, so dx = -du/2.

Int u^(3/2) (-du/2) = -(1/2) (2/5) u^(5/2) = -(1/5) u^(5/2).

Answer: -(a - 2x)^(5/2) / 5 + c.

Q2(v). Int (1 + e^x)3 / e^x dx. Expand: (1 + e^x)3 / e^x = e^(-x) + 3 + 3e^x + e^(2x).

Integrate term by term: -e^(-x) + 3x + 3e^x + e^(2x)/2.

Answer: -e^(-x) + 3x + 3e^x + e^(2x)/2 + c.

Q2(vi). Int sin((a + b) x) dx. Put u = (a + b) x; then du = (a + b) dx.

Int sin u (du/(a + b)) = -cos u / (a + b).

Answer: -cos((a + b) x) / (a + b) + c.

Q2(vii). Int sqrt(1 - cos 2x) dx, 1 - cos 2x > 0. Use 1 - cos 2x = 2 sin2 x, so sqrt(1 - cos 2x) = sqrt(2) |sin x|.

Where sin x > 0, Int sqrt(2) sin x dx = -sqrt(2) cos x.

Answer: -sqrt(2) cos x + c (on intervals where sin x > 0; with |sin x| in general).

Q2(viii). Int (ln x) (1/x) dx, x > 0. Put u = ln x; then du = dx/x.

Int u du = u2/2.

Answer: (ln x)2 / 2 + c.

Q2(ix). Int sin2 x dx. Use sin2 x = (1 - cos 2x)/2.

Int (1/2) dx - Int (cos 2x)/2 dx = x/2 - sin 2x/4.

Answer: x/2 - (sin 2x)/4 + c.

Q2(x). Int dx / (1 + cos x), -pi/2 < x < pi/2. Use 1 + cos x = 2 cos2(x/2).

Int dx / (2 cos2(x/2)) = tan(x/2).

Answer: tan(x/2) + c.

Q2(xi). Int (a x + b)/(a x2 + 2b x + c) dx. The derivative of the denominator is 2a x + 2b = 2(a x + b).

So the integral = (1/2) Int (denominator)'/(denominator) dx = (1/2) ln|denominator|.

Answer: (1/2) ln|a x2 + 2b x + c| + c.

Q2(xii). Int cos 3x sin 2x dx. Use cos 3x sin 2x = (1/2)(sin 5x - sin x).

Int (1/2) sin 5x dx = -cos 5x/10; Int (-(1/2) sin x) dx = cos x/2.

Answer: -cos 5x/10 + cos x/2 + c.

Q2(xiii). Int (cos 2x - 1)/(1 + cos 2x) dx, 1 + cos 2x not equal to 0. Use cos 2x - 1 = -2 sin2 x and 1 + cos 2x = 2 cos2 x, so the integrand = -tan2 x.

Since -tan2 x = 1 - sec2 x, the integral = x - tan x.

Answer: x - tan x + c.

Q2(xiv). Int tan2 x dx. Use tan2 x = sec2 x - 1.

Int sec2 x dx = tan x; Int (-1) dx = -x.

Answer: tan x - x + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (3x^2 - 2x + 1) dx
mcqs.why: Integrate term by term: integral of 3x^2 dx = x^3, integral of -2x dx = -x^2, integral of 1 dx = x. Adding the constant gives x^3 - x^2 + x + c; differentiating it returns 3x^2 - 2x + 1.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (sqrt(x) + 1/sqrt(x)) dx, x > 0
mcqs.why: Write the integrand as x^(1/2) + x^(-1/2). Integral of x^(1/2) dx = x^(3/2)/(3/2) = (2/3)x^(3/2); integral of x^(-1/2) dx = x^(1/2)/(1/2) = 2 sqrt(x). Total: (2/3)x^(3/2) + 2 sqrt(x) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (2x + 3)^(1/2) dx
Evaluate: integral of (sqrt(x) + 1)^2 dx, x > 0
mcqs.why: Expand: (sqrt(x) + 1)^2 = x + 2 sqrt(x) + 1. Integrate term by term: x^2/2 + 2 x (2/3)x^(3/2) = (4/3)x^(3/2), plus x. Result: x^2/2 + (4/3)x^(3/2) + x + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (sqrt(x) - 1/sqrt(x))^2 dx, x > 0
mcqs.why: Expand: (sqrt(x) - 1/sqrt(x))^2 = x - 2 + 1/x. Integrate term by term: x^2/2 - 2x + ln x, since integral of 1/x dx = ln x for x > 0. Result: x^2/2 - 2x + ln x + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (1 - x^2)/(1 + x^2) dx
mcqs.why: Divide: (1 - x^2)/(1 + x^2) = -1 + 2/(1 + x^2). Integrate: integral of -1 dx = -x and integral of 2/(1 + x^2) dx = 2 Tan^(-1) x. Result: -x + 2 Tan^(-1) x + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (a - 2x)^(3/2) dx
mcqs.why: Put u = a - 2x, du = -2 dx, so dx = -du/2. Integral = -(1/2) integral of u^(3/2) du = -(1/2)(2/5) u^(5/2) = -(a - 2x)^(5/2)/5 + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of sin^2 x dx
mcqs.why: Use sin^2 x = (1 - cos 2x)/2. Integrate: integral of 1/2 dx = x/2 and integral of -(cos 2x)/2 dx = -(sin 2x)/4. Result: x/2 - (sin 2x)/4 + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of dx/(1 + cos x), for -pi/2 < x < pi/2
mcqs.why: Use 1 + cos x = 2 cos^2(x/2). The integral becomes integral of (1/2) sec^2(x/2) dx = (1/2) x 2 tan(x/2) = tan(x/2) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of cos 3x sin 2x dx
mcqs.why: Use cos 3x sin 2x = (1/2)(sin 5x - sin x). Integrate: (1/2) integral of sin 5x dx = -cos 5x/10, and -(1/2) integral of sin x dx = +cos x/2. Result: -cos 5x/10 + cos x/2 + c.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.3 — Evaluate the following integrals (c = constant of integration)
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Int (-2x)/sqrt(4 - x2) dx.

Put u = 4 - x2; then du = -2x dx.

The integral becomes Int u^(-1/2) du = 2 sqrt(u).

Answer: 2 sqrt(4 - x2) + c.

Q2. Int dx / (x2 + 4x + 13).

Complete the square: x2 + 4x + 13 = (x + 2)2 + 9.

Int dx / ((x + 2)2 + 9) = (1/3) Tan^{-1}((x + 2)/3).

Answer: (1/3) Tan^{-1}((x + 2)/3) + c.

Q3. Int x2 / (4 + x2) dx.

Divide: x2/(4 + x2) = 1 - 4/(4 + x2).

Int 1 dx = x; Int 4/(4 + x2) dx = 2 Tan^{-1}(x/2).

Answer: x - 2 Tan^{-1}(x/2) + c.

Q4. Int dx / (x ln x).

Put u = ln x; then du = dx/x.

The integral becomes Int du/u = ln|u|.

Answer: ln|ln x| + c.

Q5. Int e^x / (e^x + 3) dx.

Put u = e^x + 3; then du = e^x dx.

The integral becomes Int du/u = ln|u|.

Answer: ln(e^x + 3) + c.

Q6. Int (x + b) / sqrt(x2 + 2b x + c) dx.

(Print note: the first term of the radicand shows as x in this copy, its superscript 2 apparently dropped, as with the Q8 misprints below; solved in the standard form.) The derivative of x2 + 2b x + c is 2x + 2b = 2(x + b).

So the integrand is (1/2) times (derivative of the radicand)/(sqrt of the radicand).

Int (1/2) (2x + 2b)/sqrt(x2 + 2b x + c) dx = sqrt(x2 + 2b x + c).

Answer: sqrt(x2 + 2b x + c) + c.

Q7. Int sec2 x / sqrt(tan x) dx.

Put u = tan x; then du = sec2 x dx.

The integral becomes Int u^(-1/2) du = 2 sqrt(u).

Answer: 2 sqrt(tan x) + c.

Q8. Show that Int dx / sqrt(x2 - a2) = ln(x + sqrt(x2 - a2)) + c.

(Print note: this copy prints the integrand as dx/(x2 - a2), which is a misprint; the proved form is the one with sqrt(x2 - a2) in the denominator.) Put x = a sec theta; then dx = a sec theta tan theta d theta and sqrt(x2 - a2) = a tan theta.

The integral becomes Int sec theta d theta = ln|sec theta + tan theta| + c.

Since sec theta = x/a and tan theta = sqrt(x2 - a2)/a, this is ln(x + sqrt(x2 - a2)) + c (absorbing -ln a into c).

Answer: proved.

Q8(b). Show that Int sqrt(a2 - x2) dx = (a2/2) Sin^{-1}(x/a) + (x/2) sqrt(a2 - x2) + c. (Print note: this copy prints the right-hand side as (a/a) Sin^{-1}(x/a) + (x/a) sqrt(a2 - x2), which is a misprint; the standard form is proved here.) Put x = a sin theta; then dx = a cos theta d theta and sqrt(a2 - x2) = a cos theta.

The integral becomes Int a2 cos2 theta d theta = (a2/2) Int (1 + cos 2 theta) d theta.

This equals (a2/2)(theta + sin theta cos theta) + c.

Since theta = Sin^{-1}(x/a), sin theta = x/a and cos theta = sqrt(a2 - x2)/a, the result is (a2/2) Sin^{-1}(x/a) + (x/2) sqrt(a2 - x2) + c.

Answer: proved.

Q9. Int dx / (1 + x2)^(3/2).

Put x = tan theta; then dx = sec2 theta d theta and (1 + x2)^(3/2) = sec3 theta.

The integral becomes Int cos theta d theta = sin theta.

Since sin theta = x/sqrt(1 + x2), the answer is x/sqrt(1 + x2) + c.

Answer: x/sqrt(1 + x2) + c.

Q10. Int dx / ((1 + x2) Tan^{-1} x).

Put u = Tan^{-1} x; then du = dx/(1 + x2).

The integral becomes Int du/u = ln|u|.

Answer: ln|Tan^{-1} x| + c.

Q11. Int sqrt((1 + x)/(1 - x)) dx.

Multiply top and bottom inside the root: sqrt((1 + x)/(1 - x)) = (1 + x)/sqrt(1 - x2).

Split: Int dx/sqrt(1 - x2) + Int x dx/sqrt(1 - x2) = Sin^{-1} x - sqrt(1 - x2).

Answer: Sin^{-1} x - sqrt(1 - x2) + c.

Q12. Int sin theta / (1 + cos2 theta) d theta.

Put u = cos theta; then du = -sin theta d theta.

The integral becomes -Int du/(1 + u2) = -Tan^{-1} u.

Answer: -Tan^{-1}(cos theta) + c.

Q13. Int a x / sqrt(a2 - x4) dx.

Put u = x2; then du = 2x dx, so x dx = du/2.

The integral becomes (a/2) Int du/sqrt(a2 - u2) = (a/2) Sin^{-1}(u/a).

Answer: (a/2) Sin^{-1}(x2/a) + c.

Q14. Int dx / sqrt(7 - 6x - x2).

Complete the square: 7 - 6x - x2 = 16 - (x + 3)2.

Int dx/sqrt(16 - (x + 3)2) = Sin^{-1}((x + 3)/4).

Answer: Sin^{-1}((x + 3)/4) + c.

Q15. Int cos x / (sin x ln sin x) dx.

Put u = ln sin x; then du = (cos x / sin x) dx.

The integral becomes Int du/u = ln|u|.

Answer: ln|ln sin x| + c.

Q16. Int cos x (ln sin x / sin x) dx.

Put u = ln sin x; then du = (cos x / sin x) dx.

The integral becomes Int u du = u2/2.

Answer: (ln sin x)2 / 2 + c.

Q17. Int x dx / (4 + 2x + x2).

Write x = (1/2)(2x + 2) - 1, splitting the integral into (1/2) Int (2x + 2)/(x2 + 2x + 4) dx - Int dx/(x2 + 2x + 4).

The first part is (1/2) ln(x2 + 2x + 4); the second, with x2 + 2x + 4 = (x + 1)2 + 3, is (1/sqrt(3)) Tan^{-1}((x + 1)/sqrt(3)).

Answer: (1/2) ln(x2 + 2x + 4) - (1/sqrt(3)) Tan^{-1}((x + 1)/sqrt(3)) + c.

Q18. Int x dx / (x4 + 2x2 + 5).

Put u = x2; then du = 2x dx, so x dx = du/2.

The integral becomes (1/2) Int du/(u2 + 2u + 5) = (1/2) Int du/((u + 1)2 + 4).

This equals (1/2)(1/2) Tan^{-1}((u + 1)/2) = (1/4) Tan^{-1}((x2 + 1)/2).

Answer: (1/4) Tan^{-1}((x2 + 1)/2) + c.

Q19. Int cos(sqrt(x) - x/2) (1/sqrt(x) - 1) dx.

Put u = sqrt(x) - x/2; then du/dx = 1/(2 sqrt(x)) - 1/2 = (1/2)(1/sqrt(x) - 1).

So (1/sqrt(x) - 1) dx = 2 du, and the integral becomes 2 Int cos u du = 2 sin u.

Answer: 2 sin(sqrt(x) - x/2) + c.

Q20. Int (x + 2)/sqrt(x + 3) dx.

Put u = x + 3; then x + 2 = u - 1 and dx = du.

The integral becomes Int (u - 1)/sqrt(u) du = Int (u^(1/2) - u^(-1/2)) du = (2/3) u^(3/2) - 2 sqrt(u).

Answer: (2/3)(x + 3)^(3/2) - 2 sqrt(x + 3) + c.

Q21. Int sqrt(2) / (sin x + cos x) dx.

Since sin x + cos x = sqrt(2) sin(x + pi/4), the integrand is 1/sin(x + pi/4).

Int cosec(x + pi/4) dx = ln|tan((x + pi/4)/2)|.

Answer: ln|tan(x/2 + pi/8)| + c.

Q22. Int dx / ((1/2) sin x + (sqrt(3)/2) cos x).

Since (1/2) sin x + (sqrt(3)/2) cos x = sin(x + pi/3), the integral is Int cosec(x + pi/3) dx.

Int cosec(x + pi/3) dx = ln|tan((x + pi/3)/2)|.

Answer: ln|tan(x/2 + pi/6)| + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (-2x)/sqrt(4 - x^2) dx
mcqs.why: Put u = 4 - x^2, du = -2x dx. The integral becomes integral of u^(-1/2) du = u^(1/2)/(1/2) = 2 sqrt(u) = 2 sqrt(4 - x^2) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of dx/(x^2 + 4x + 13)
mcqs.why: Complete the square: x^2 + 4x + 13 = (x + 2)^2 + 9 = (x + 2)^2 + 3^2. Using integral of dx/(x^2 + a^2) = (1/a) Tan^(-1)(x/a) with a = 3 gives (1/3) Tan^(-1)((x + 2)/3) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of x^2/(4 + x^2) dx
mcqs.why: Divide: x^2/(4 + x^2) = 1 - 4/(4 + x^2). Integrate: integral of 1 dx = x, and integral of 4/(4 + x^2) dx = 4 x (1/2) Tan^(-1)(x/2) = 2 Tan^(-1)(x/2). Result: x - 2 Tan^(-1)(x/2) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of dx/(x ln x)
mcqs.why: Put u = ln x, du = dx/x. The integrand dx/(x ln x) becomes du/u, whose integral is ln|u| = ln|ln x| + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of e^x/(e^x + 3) dx
mcqs.why: Put u = e^x + 3, du = e^x dx. The integral becomes integral of du/u = ln|u| = ln(e^x + 3) + c, since e^x + 3 is always positive.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of sec^2 x / sqrt(tan x) dx
mcqs.why: Put u = tan x, du = sec^2 x dx. The integral becomes integral of u^(-1/2) du = u^(1/2)/(1/2) = 2 sqrt(u) = 2 sqrt(tan x) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of dx/(1 + x^2)^(3/2)
mcqs.why: Put x = tan theta, dx = sec^2 theta d theta and (1 + x^2)^(3/2) = sec^3 theta. The integral becomes integral of cos theta d theta = sin theta = x/sqrt(1 + x^2) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of dx/sqrt(7 - 6x - x^2)
mcqs.why: Complete the square: 7 - 6x - x^2 = 16 - (x + 3)^2 = 4^2 - (x + 3)^2. Using integral of dx/sqrt(a^2 - x^2) = Sin^(-1)(x/a) with a = 4 gives Sin^(-1)((x + 3)/4) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of sqrt(a^2 - x^2) dx
options: a Sin^(-1)(x/a) + x sqrt(a^2 - x^2) + c
mcqs.why: Put x = a sin theta, dx = a cos theta d theta, sqrt(a^2 - x^2) = a cos theta. Integral = a^2 integral of cos^2 theta d theta = (a^2/2)(theta + sin theta cos theta), which back-substitutes to (a^2/2) Sin^(-1)(x/a) + (x/2) sqrt(a^2 - x^2) + c. Note: this copy misprints the right side coefficients; the form shown here is the one that differentiates back correctly.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of dx/((1 + x^2) Tan^(-1) x)
mcqs.why: Put u = Tan^(-1) x, du = dx/(1 + x^2). The integral becomes integral of du/u = ln|u| = ln|Tan^(-1) x| + c.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.4
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Evaluate the following integrals by parts (c = constant of integration)

Q1(i). Int x sin x dx. Take u = x, dv = sin x dx; then du = dx, v = -cos x.

By parts: -x cos x + Int cos x dx = -x cos x + sin x.

Answer: -x cos x + sin x + c.

Q1(ii). Int ln x dx. Take u = ln x, dv = dx; then du = dx/x, v = x.

By parts: x ln x - Int x (dx/x) = x ln x - x.

Answer: x ln x - x + c.

Q1(iii). Int x ln x dx. Take u = ln x, dv = x dx; then du = dx/x, v = x2/2.

By parts: (x2/2) ln x - Int (x/2) dx = (x2/2) ln x - x2/4.

Answer: (x2/2) ln x - x2/4 + c.

Q1(iv). Int x2 ln x dx.

Take u = ln x, dv = x2 dx; then du = dx/x, v = x3/3.

By parts: (x3/3) ln x - Int (x2/3) dx = (x3/3) ln x - x3/9.

Answer: (x3/3) ln x - x3/9 + c.

Q1(v). Int x3 ln x dx. Take u = ln x, dv = x3 dx; then du = dx/x, v = x4/4.

By parts: (x4/4) ln x - Int (x3/4) dx = (x4/4) ln x - x4/16.

Answer: (x4/4) ln x - x4/16 + c.

Q1(vi). Int x4 ln x dx. Take u = ln x, dv = x4 dx; then du = dx/x, v = x5/5.

By parts: (x5/5) ln x - Int (x4/5) dx = (x5/5) ln x - x5/25.

Answer: (x5/5) ln x - x5/25 + c.

Q1(vii). Int Tan^{-1} x dx. Take u = Tan^{-1} x, dv = dx; then du = dx/(1 + x2), v = x.

By parts: x Tan^{-1} x - Int x dx/(1 + x2) = x Tan^{-1} x - (1/2) ln(1 + x2).

Answer: x Tan^{-1} x - (1/2) ln(1 + x2) + c.

Q1(viii). Int x2 sin x dx.

Take u = x2, dv = sin x dx: the integral becomes -x2 cos x + Int 2x cos x dx.

Integrate Int 2x cos x dx by parts: 2x sin x - Int 2 sin x dx = 2x sin x + 2 cos x.

Answer: -x2 cos x + 2x sin x + 2 cos x + c.

Q1(ix). Int x2 Tan^{-1} x dx. Take u = Tan^{-1} x, dv = x2 dx; then du = dx/(1 + x2), v = x3/3.

By parts: (x3/3) Tan^{-1} x - (1/3) Int x3 dx/(1 + x2).

Since x3/(1 + x2) = x - x/(1 + x2), the remaining integral is x2/2 - (1/2) ln(1 + x2).

Answer: (x3/3) Tan^{-1} x - x2/6 + (1/6) ln(1 + x2) + c.

Q1(x). Int x Tan^{-1} x dx. Take u = Tan^{-1} x, dv = x dx; then du = dx/(1 + x2), v = x2/2.

By parts: (x2/2) Tan^{-1} x - (1/2) Int x2 dx/(1 + x2).

Since x2/(1 + x2) = 1 - 1/(1 + x2), the remaining integral is x - Tan^{-1} x.

Answer: ((x2 + 1)/2) Tan^{-1} x - x/2 + c.

Q1(xi). Int x3 Tan^{-1} x dx. Take u = Tan^{-1} x, dv = x3 dx; then du = dx/(1 + x2), v = x4/4.

By parts: (x4/4) Tan^{-1} x - (1/4) Int x4 dx/(1 + x2).

Since x4/(1 + x2) = x2 - 1 + 1/(1 + x2), the remaining integral is x3/3 - x + Tan^{-1} x.

Answer: ((x4 - 1)/4) Tan^{-1} x - x3/12 + x/4 + c.

Q1(xii). Int x3 cos x dx. Take u = x3, dv = cos x dx: the integral becomes x3 sin x - Int 3x2 sin x dx.

Integrate Int 3x2 sin x dx by parts twice: -3x2 cos x + 6x sin x + 6 cos x.

Answer: x3 sin x + 3x2 cos x - 6x sin x - 6 cos x + c.

Q1(xiii). Int Sin^{-1} x dx. Take u = Sin^{-1} x, dv = dx; then du = dx/sqrt(1 - x2), v = x.

By parts: x Sin^{-1} x - Int x dx/sqrt(1 - x2) = x Sin^{-1} x + sqrt(1 - x2).

Answer: x Sin^{-1} x + sqrt(1 - x2) + c.

Q1(xiv). Int x Sin^{-1} x dx. Take u = Sin^{-1} x, dv = x dx; then du = dx/sqrt(1 - x2), v = x2/2.

By parts: (x2/2) Sin^{-1} x - (1/2) Int x2 dx/sqrt(1 - x2).

With x = sin theta, Int x2 dx/sqrt(1 - x2) = (1/2)(Sin^{-1} x - x sqrt(1 - x2)).

Answer: ((2x2 - 1)/4) Sin^{-1} x + (x/4) sqrt(1 - x2) + c.

Q1(xv). Int e^x sin x cos x dx. Use sin x cos x = (1/2) sin 2x, so the integral is (1/2) Int e^x sin 2x dx.

Int e^x sin 2x dx = e^x (sin 2x - 2 cos 2x)/5.

Answer: e^x (sin 2x - 2 cos 2x)/10 + c.

Q1(xvi). Int x sin x cos x dx. Use sin x cos x = (1/2) sin 2x, so the integral is (1/2) Int x sin 2x dx.

By parts, Int x sin 2x dx = -x cos 2x/2 + sin 2x/4.

Answer: -x cos 2x/4 + sin 2x/8 + c.

Q1(xvii). Int x cos2 x dx. Use cos2 x = (1 + cos 2x)/2, so the integral is (1/2) Int x dx + (1/2) Int x cos 2x dx.

Int x cos 2x dx = x sin 2x/2 + cos 2x/4.

Answer: x2/4 + x sin 2x/4 + cos 2x/8 + c.

Q1(xviii). Int x sin2 x dx. Use sin2 x = (1 - cos 2x)/2, so the integral is (1/2) Int x dx - (1/2) Int x cos 2x dx.

Int x cos 2x dx = x sin 2x/2 + cos 2x/4.

Answer: x2/4 - x sin 2x/4 - cos 2x/8 + c.

Q1(xix). Int (ln x)2 dx. Take u = (ln x)2, dv = dx; then du = 2 ln x (dx/x), v = x.

By parts: x (ln x)2 - Int 2 ln x dx = x (ln x)2 - 2(x ln x - x).

Answer: x (ln x)2 - 2x ln x + 2x + c.

Q1(xx). Int ln(tan x) sec2 x dx. Take u = ln(tan x), dv = sec2 x dx; then du = (sec2 x / tan x) dx, v = tan x.

By parts: tan x ln(tan x) - Int sec2 x dx = tan x ln(tan x) - tan x.

Answer: tan x ln(tan x) - tan x + c.

Q1(xxi). Int x Sin^{-1} x / sqrt(1 - x2) dx. Take u = Sin^{-1} x, dv = x dx/sqrt(1 - x2); then du = dx/sqrt(1 - x2), v = -sqrt(1 x2).

By parts: -sqrt(1 - x2) Sin^{-1} x + Int dx = -sqrt(1 - x2) Sin^{-1} x + x.

Answer: x - sqrt(1 - x2) Sin^{-1} x + c.

Q2. Evaluate the following integral (c = constant of integration)

Q2(i). Int tan4 x dx.

Write tan4 x = tan2 x (sec2 x - 1) = tan2 x sec2 x - tan2 x.

Int tan2 x sec2 x dx = tan3 x/3; Int tan2 x dx = tan x - x.

Answer: tan3 x/3 - tan x + x + c.

Q2(ii). Int sec4 x dx. Write sec4 x = (1 + tan2 x) sec2 x.

Put u = tan x: Int (1 + u2) du = u + u3/3.

Answer: tan x + tan3 x/3 + c.

Q2(iii). Int e^x sin 2x cos x dx. Use sin 2x cos x = (1/2)(sin 3x + sin x).

Int e^x sin 3x dx = e^x (sin 3x - 3 cos 3x)/10; Int e^x sin x dx = e^x (sin x - cos x)/2.

Answer: e^x (sin 3x - 3 cos 3x)/20 + e^x (sin x - cos x)/4 + c.

Q2(iv). Int tan3 x sec x dx. Write tan3 x sec x = (sec2 x - 1) tan x sec x.

Put u = sec x: Int (u2 - 1) du = u3/3 - u.

Answer: sec3 x/3 - sec x + c.

Q2(v). Int x3 e^(5x) dx. Integrate by parts repeatedly (or use the reduction formula).

Each step lowers the power of x and divides by 5.

Answer: e^(5x) (x3/5 - 3x2/25 + 6x/125 - 6/625) + c.

Q2(vi). Int e^(-x) sin 2x dx. Use Int e^(a x) sin b x dx = e^(a x)(a sin b x - b cos b x)/(a2 + b2) with a = -1, b = 2.

Answer: e^(-x)(-sin 2x - 2 cos 2x)/5 + c.

Q2(vii). Int e^(2x) cos 3x dx. Use Int e^(a x) cos b x dx = e^(a x)(a cos b x + b sin b x)/(a2 + b2) with a = 2, b = 3.

Answer: e^(2x)(2 cos 3x + 3 sin 3x)/13 + c.

Q2(viii). Int cosec3 x dx. Write cosec3 x = cosec x (1 + cot2 x) = cosec x + cosec x cot2 x.

Integrate by parts (or use the reduction formula): Int cosec3 x dx = -(1/2) cosec x cot x + (1/2) Int cosec x dx.

Int cosec x dx = ln|tan(x/2)|.

Answer: -(1/2) cosec x cot x + (1/2) ln|tan(x/2)| + c.

Q3. Show that Int e^(a x) sin b x dx = (1/sqrt(a2 + b2)) e^(a x) sin(b x - Tan^{-1}(b/a)) + c (Print note: this copy prints '+' before Tan^{-1}; the proof gives '-'; the printed sign is a misprint.)

Q3. Proof. Let I = Int e^(a x) sin b x dx and J = Int e^(a x) cos b x dx.

Integrating I by parts twice gives I = e^(a x)(a sin b x - b cos b x)/(a2 + b2).

Write a sin b x - b cos b x = sqrt(a2 + b2) sin(b x - alpha), where cos alpha = a/sqrt(a2 + b2) and sin alpha = b/sqrt(a2 + b2), i.e. alpha = Tan^{-1}(b/a).

Hence I = e^(a x) sin(b x - Tan^{-1}(b/a))/sqrt(a2 + b2) + c.

Answer: proved (with the minus sign; the '+' printed in this copy does not differentiate back to e^(a x) sin b x).

Q4. Evaluate the following indefinite integrals (c = constant of integration)

Q4(i). Int sqrt(a2 - x2) dx. This is Exercise 3.3 Q8(b): put x = a sin theta.

Answer: (a2/2) Sin^{-1}(x/a) + (x/2) sqrt(a2 - x2) + c.

Q4(ii). Int sqrt(x2 - a2) dx. Put x = a sec theta; then dx = a sec theta tan theta d theta and sqrt(x2 - a2) = a tan theta.

The integral becomes a2 Int tan2 theta sec theta d theta, which by parts gives (x/2) sqrt(x2 - a2) - (a2/2) ln|x + sqrt(x2 - a2)|.

Answer: (x/2) sqrt(x2 - a2) - (a2/2) ln|x + sqrt(x2 - a2)| + c.

Q4(iii). Int sqrt(4 - 5x2) dx. Use Int sqrt(A2 - B2 x2) dx = (x/2) sqrt(A2 - B2 x2) + (A2/(2B)) Sin^{-1}(B x/A) with A = 2, B = sqrt(5).

Answer: (x/2) sqrt(4 - 5x2) + (2/sqrt(5)) Sin^{-1}(sqrt(5) x/2) + c.

Q4(iv). Int sqrt(3 - 4x2) dx. Use the same formula with A = sqrt(3), B = 2.

Answer: (x/2) sqrt(3 - 4x2) + (3/4) Sin^{-1}(2x/sqrt(3)) + c.

Q4(v). Int sqrt(x2 + 4) dx. Put x = 2 tan theta; the integral becomes 4 Int sec3 theta d theta.

Using Int sec3 theta d theta = (1/2)(sec theta tan theta + ln|sec theta + tan theta|), and back-substituting, gives (x/2) sqrt(x2 + 4) + 2 ln|x + sqrt(x2 + 4)|.

Answer: (x/2) sqrt(x2 + 4) + 2 ln|x + sqrt(x2 + 4)| + c.

Q4(vi). Int x2 e^(a x) dx. Integrate by parts twice: Int x2 e^(a x) dx = (x2/a) e^(a x) - (2/a) Int x e^(a x) dx.

Int x e^(a x) dx = e^(a x)(x/a - 1/a2).

Answer: e^(a x)(x2/a - 2x/a2 + 2/a3) + c.

Q5. Evaluate the following integrals (using Int e^(a x)[a f(x) + f'(x)] dx = e^(a x) f(x) + c) (c = constant of integration)

Q5(i). Int e^x (1/x + ln x) dx. Take f(x) = ln x; then f'(x) = 1/x, so the integrand is e^x [f(x) + f'(x)].

Answer: e^x ln x + c.

Q5(ii). Int e^x (cos x + sin x) dx. Take f(x) = sin x; then f'(x) = cos x, so the integrand is e^x [f(x) + f'(x)].

Answer: e^x sin x + c.

Q5(iii). Int e^(a x) [a Sec^{-1} x + 1/(x sqrt(x2 - 1))] dx. Take f(x) = Sec^{-1} x; then f'(x) = 1/(x sqrt(x2 - 1)), so the integrand is e^(a x)[a f(x) + f'(x)].

Answer: e^(a x) Sec^{-1} x + c.

Q5(iv). Int e^(3x) [(3 sin x - cos x)/sin2 x] dx. Rewrite the bracket: (3 sin x - cos x)/sin2 x = 3 cosec x - cosec x cot x.

Take f(x) = cosec x; then f'(x) = -cosec x cot x, so the bracket is 3 f(x) + f'(x).

Answer: e^(3x) cosec x + c.

Q5(v). Int e^(2x) [-sin x + 2 cos x] dx. Take f(x) = cos x; then f'(x) = -sin x, so the bracket is 2 f(x) + f'(x).

Answer: e^(2x) cos x + c.

Q5(vi). Int x e^x / (1 + x)2 dx. Write x/(1 + x)2 = 1/(1 + x) - 1/(1 + x)2.

Take f(x) = 1/(1 + x); then f'(x) = -1/(1 + x)2, so the integrand is e^x [f(x) + f'(x)].

Answer: e^x/(1 + x) + c.

Q5(vii). Int e^(-x) (cos x - sin x) dx. Take f(x) = sin x; then -f(x) + f'(x) = -sin x + cos x, matching the bracket with a = -1.

Answer: e^(-x) sin x + c.

Q5(viii). Int e^(m Tan^{-1} x) / (1 + x2) dx. Put u = Tan^{-1} x; then du = dx/(1 + x2).

The integral becomes Int e^(m u) du = e^(m u)/m.

Answer: e^(m Tan^{-1} x)/m + c.

Q5(ix). Int 2x / (1 - sin x) dx. Multiply top and bottom by (1 + sin x): 2x/(1 - sin x) = 2x(1 + sin x)/cos2 x = 2x sec2 x + 2x sec x tan x.

Int 2x sec2 x dx = 2x tan x + 2 ln|cos x|; Int 2x sec x tan x dx = 2x sec x - 2 ln|sec x + tan x|.

Since ln|cos x| - ln|sec x + tan x| = ln|1 - sin x|, the logs combine.

Answer: 2x (tan x + sec x) + 2 ln|1 - sin x| + c.

Q5(x). Int e^x (1 + x)/(2 + x)2 dx. Take f(x) = 1/(2 + x); then f(x) + f'(x) = 1/(2 + x) - 1/(2 + x)2 = (1 + x)/(2 + x)2.

Answer: e^x/(2 + x) + c.

Q5(xi). Int ((1 - sin x)/(1 - cos x)) e^x dx. Using half-angles, (1 - sin x)/(1 - cos x) = (1/2) cosec2(x/2) - cot(x/2).

Take f(x) = -cot(x/2); then f'(x) = (1/2) cosec2(x/2), so the integrand is e^x [f(x) + f'(x)].

Answer: -e^x cot(x/2) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate by parts: integral of x sin x dx
options: x cos x + sin x + c
x cos x - cos x + c
mcqs.why: Take u = x, dv = sin x dx, so du = dx, v = -cos x. By parts: -x cos x + integral of cos x dx = -x cos x + sin x + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate by parts: integral of ln x dx
mcqs.why: Take u = ln x, dv = dx, so du = dx/x, v = x. By parts: x ln x - integral of x (dx/x) = x ln x - integral of 1 dx = x ln x - x + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate by parts: integral of x ln x dx
mcqs.why: Take u = ln x, dv = x dx, so du = dx/x, v = x^2/2. By parts: (x^2/2) ln x - integral of (x/2) dx = (x^2/2) ln x - x^2/4 + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate by parts: integral of x^2 ln x dx
mcqs.why: Take u = ln x, dv = x^2 dx, so du = dx/x, v = x^3/3. By parts: (x^3/3) ln x - integral of (x^2/3) dx = (x^3/3) ln x - (x^3/9) + c, since integral of x^2/3 dx = x^3/9.

mcqs.q: Evaluate by parts: integral of Tan^(-1) x dx
options: x Tan^(-1) x - ln(1 + x^2) + c
mcqs.why: Take u = Tan^(-1) x, dv = dx, so du = dx/(1 + x^2), v = x. By parts: x Tan^(-1) x - integral of x dx/(1 + x^2) = x Tan^(-1) x - (1/2) ln(1 + x^2) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate by parts: integral of x^2 sin x dx
options: -x^2 cos x - 2x sin x + 2 cos x + c
x^2 cos x + 2x sin x + 2 cos x + c
-x^2 cos x + 2x sin x + 2 cos x + c
-x^2 cos x + 2x sin x - 2 cos x + c
mcqs.why: First parts with u = x^2, dv = sin x dx gives -x^2 cos x + integral of 2x cos x dx. Parts again: integral of 2x cos x dx = 2x sin x + 2 cos x. Total: -x^2 cos x + 2x sin x + 2 cos x + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate by parts: integral of Sin^(-1) x dx
options: x Sin^(-1) x - sqrt(1 - x^2) + c
x Sin^(-1) x + sqrt(1 - x^2) + c
x Sin^(-1) x + x sqrt(1 - x^2) + c
mcqs.why: Take u = Sin^(-1) x, dv = dx, so du = dx/sqrt(1 - x^2), v = x. By parts: x Sin^(-1) x - integral of x dx/sqrt(1 - x^2) = x Sin^(-1) x + sqrt(1 - x^2) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of tan^4 x dx
options: tan^3 x/3 + tan x - x + c
tan^3 x/3 - tan x - x + c
tan^3 x - tan x + x + c
tan^3 x/3 - tan x + x + c
mcqs.why: Write tan^4 x = tan^2 x (sec^2 x - 1) = tan^2 x sec^2 x - tan^2 x. Integral of tan^2 x sec^2 x dx = tan^3 x/3 and integral of tan^2 x dx = tan x - x, so the result is tan^3 x/3 - (tan x - x) = tan^3 x/3 - tan x + x + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of e^(2x) cos 3x dx
mcqs.why: Use integral of e^(a x) cos b x dx = e^(a x)(a cos b x + b sin b x)/(a^2 + b^2) with a = 2, b = 3: denominator 4 + 9 = 13, giving e^(2x)(2 cos 3x + 3 sin 3x)/13 + c. Differentiating this returns e^(2x) cos 3x.

mcqs.q: The correct closed form of integral of e^(a x) sin b x dx in amplitude form is:
options: (1/sqrt(a^2 + b^2)) e^(a x) sin(b x + Tan^(-1)(b/a)) + c
(1/sqrt(a^2 + b^2)) e^(a x) sin(b x - Tan^(-1)(b/a)) + c
sqrt(a^2 + b^2) e^(a x) sin(b x - Tan^(-1)(b/a)) + c
mcqs.why: Parts twice gives e^(a x)(a sin b x - b cos b x)/(a^2 + b^2). Write a sin b x - b cos b x = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) sin(b x - alpha) with alpha = Tan^(-1)(b/a), giving (1/sqrt(a^2 + b^2)) e^(a x) sin(b x - Tan^(-1)(b/a)) + c. The '+' sign printed in this copy is a misprint: only the minus form differentiates back to e^(a x) sin b x.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.5 — Evaluate the following integrals (partial fractions; c = constant of integration)
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Int (3x + 1)/(x2 - x - 6) dx.

Factor: x2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2).

Partial fractions: (3x + 1)/((x - 3)(x + 2)) = 2/(x - 3) + 1/(x + 2).

Answer: 2 ln|x - 3| + ln|x + 2| + c.

Q2. Int (5x + 8)/((x + 3)(2x - 1)) dx.

Partial fractions: (5x + 8)/((x + 3)(2x - 1)) = 1/(x + 3) + 3/(2x - 1).

Answer: ln|x + 3| + (3/2) ln|2x - 1| + c.

Q3. Int (x2 + 3x - 34)/(x2 + 2x - 15) dx.

Divide first: the quotient is 1 with remainder x - 19, and (x - 19)/((x + 5)(x - 3)) = 3/(x + 5) - 2/(x - 3).

Answer: x + 3 ln|x + 5| - 2 ln|x - 3| + c.

Q4. Int (a - b)x/((x - a)(x - b)) dx, a > b.

Partial fractions: (a - b)x/((x - a)(x - b)) = a/(x - a) - b/(x - b).

Answer: a ln|x - a| - b ln|x - b| + c.

Q5. Int (3 - x)/(1 - x - 6x2) dx.

Factor: 1 - x - 6x2 = (1 - 3x)(1 + 2x).

Partial fractions: (3 - x)/((1 - 3x)(1 + 2x)) = (8/5)/(1 - 3x) + (7/5)/(1 + 2x).

Answer: -(8/15) ln|1 - 3x| + (7/10) ln|1 + 2x| + c.

Q6. Int 2x/(x2 - a2) dx.

Partial fractions: 2x/((x - a)(x + a)) = 1/(x - a) + 1/(x + a).

Answer: ln|x2 - a2| + c.

Q7. Int dx/(6x2 + 5x - 4).

Factor: 6x2 + 5x - 4 = (3x + 4)(2x - 1).

Partial fractions: 1/((3x + 4)(2x - 1)) = (-3/11)/(3x + 4) + (2/11)/(2x - 1).

Answer: (1/11) ln|(2x - 1)/(3x + 4)| + c.

Q8. Int (2x3 - 3x2 - x - 7)/(2x2 - 3x - 2) dx.

Divide: the quotient is x with remainder x - 7, and (x - 7)/((2x + 1)(x - 2)) = 3/(2x + 1) - 1/(x - 2).

Answer: x2/2 + (3/2) ln|2x + 1| - ln|x - 2| + c.

Q9. Int (3x2 - 12x + 11)/((x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 1/(x - 1) + 1/(x - 2) + 1/(x - 3).

Answer: ln|(x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3)| + c.

Q10. Int (2x - 1)/(x(x - 1)(x - 3)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals (-1/3)/x - (1/2)/(x - 1) + (5/6)/(x - 3).

Answer: -(1/3) ln|x| - (1/2) ln|x - 1| + (5/6) ln|x - 3| + c.

Q11. Int (5x2 + 9x + 6)/((x2 - 1)(2x + 3)) dx.

Factor: (x2 - 1)(2x + 3) = (x - 1)(x + 1)(2x + 3).

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 2/(x - 1) - 1/(x + 1) + 3/(2x + 3).

Answer: 2 ln|x - 1| - ln|x + 1| + (3/2) ln|2x + 3| + c.

Q12. Int (4 + 7x)/((1 + x)2(2 + 3x)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 2/(1 + x) + 3/(1 + x)2 - 6/(2 + 3x).

Answer: 2 ln|1 + x| - 3/(1 + x) - 2 ln|2 + 3x| + c.

Q13. Int 2x2/((x - 1)2(x + 1)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals (3/2)/(x - 1) + 1/(x - 1)2 + (1/2)/(x + 1).

Answer: (3/2) ln|x - 1| - 1/(x - 1) + (1/2) ln|x + 1| + c.

Q14. Int dx/((x - 1)(x + 1)2).

Partial fractions: the integrand equals (1/4)/(x - 1) - (1/4)/(x + 1) - (1/2)/(x + 1)2.

Answer: (1/4) ln|(x - 1)/(x + 1)| + 1/(2(x + 1)) + c.

Q15. Int (x + 4)/(x3 - 3x2 + 4) dx.

Factor: x3 - 3x2 + 4 = (x + 1)(x - 2)2.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals (1/3)/(x + 1) - (1/3)/(x - 2) + 2/(x - 2)2.

Answer: (1/3) ln|x + 1| - (1/3) ln|x - 2| - 2/(x - 2) + c.

Q16. Int (x3 - 6x2 + 25)/((x + 1)2(x - 2)2) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 3/(x + 1) + 2/(x + 1)2 - 2/(x - 2) + 1/(x - 2)2.

Answer: 3 ln|x + 1| - 2/(x + 1) - 2 ln|x - 2| - 1/(x - 2) + c.

Q17. Int (x3 + 22x2 + 14x - 17)/((x - 3)(x + 2)3) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 2/(x - 3) - 1/(x + 2) + 11/(x + 2)2 - 7/(x + 2)3.

Answer: 2 ln|x - 3| - ln|x + 2| - 11/(x + 2) + 7/(2(x + 2)2) + c.

Q18. Int (x - 2)/((x + 1)(x2 + 1)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals (-3/2)/(x + 1) + ((3/2)x - 1/2)/(x2 + 1).

Answer: -(3/2) ln|x + 1| + (3/4) ln(x2 + 1) - (1/2) Tan^{-1} x + c.

Q19. Int x/((x - 1)(x2 + 1)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals (1/2)/(x - 1) + ((-1/2)x + 1/2)/(x2 + 1).

Answer: (1/2) ln|x - 1| - (1/4) ln(x2 + 1) + (1/2) Tan^{-1} x + c.

Q20. Int (9x - 7)/((x + 3)(x2 + 1)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals (-17/5)/(x + 3) + ((17/5)x - 6/5)/(x2 + 1).

Answer: -(17/5) ln|x + 3| + (17/10) ln(x2 + 1) - (6/5) Tan^{-1} x + c.

Q21. Int (1 + 4x)/((x - 3)(x2 + 4)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 1/(x - 3) + (-x + 1)/(x2 + 4).

Answer: ln|x - 3| - (1/2) ln(x2 + 4) + (1/2) Tan^{-1}(x/2) + c.

Q22. FLAGGED - Int 12/(?

+ 8) dx: denominator incomplete in the source copy; no answer given. As printed in this copy, Q22 reads 'Int 12/( + 8) dx' - the first term of the denominator is blank (not legible even at 300 DPI).

Without that term the integrand cannot be identified, so no partial-fraction decomposition is attempted.

Answer: NOT COMPUTED - the printed denominator is incomplete in the source copy; nothing has been invented here.

Q23. Int (9x + 6)/(x3 - 8) dx.

Factor: x3 - 8 = (x - 2)(x2 + 2x + 4).

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 2/(x - 2) + (-2x + 1)/(x2 + 2x + 4).

The second part gives -ln(x2 + 2x + 4) + sqrt(3) Tan^{-1}((x + 1)/sqrt(3)).

Answer: 2 ln|x - 2| - ln(x2 + 2x + 4) + sqrt(3) Tan^{-1}((x + 1)/sqrt(3)) + c.

Q24. Int (2x2 + 5x + 3)/((x - 1)2(x2 + 4)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 1/(x - 1) + 2/(x - 1)2 + (-x - 1)/(x2 + 4).

Answer: ln|x - 1| - 2/(x - 1) - (1/2) ln(x2 + 4) - (1/2) Tan^{-1}(x/2) + c.

Q25. Int (2x2 - x - 7)/((x + 2)2(x2 + x + 1)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals -2/(x + 2) + 1/(x + 2)2 + (2x - 1)/(x2 + x + 1).

The last part gives ln(x2 + x + 1) - (4/sqrt(3)) Tan^{-1}((2x + 1)/sqrt(3)).

Answer: -2 ln|x + 2| - 1/(x + 2) + ln(x2 + x + 1) - (4/sqrt(3)) Tan^{-1}((2x + 1)/sqrt(3)) + c.

Q26. Int (3x + 1)/((4x2 + 1)(x2 - x + 1)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 4x/(4x2 + 1) + 1/(x2 - x + 1).

Answer: (1/2) ln(4x2 + 1) + (2/sqrt(3)) Tan^{-1}((2x - 1)/sqrt(3)) + c.

Q27. Int (4x + 1)/((x2 + 4)(x2 + 4x + 5)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 1/(x2 + 4) - 1/(x2 + 4x + 5).

Since x2 + 4x + 5 = (x + 2)2 + 1, the second integral is Tan^{-1}(x + 2).

Answer: (1/2) Tan^{-1}(x/2) - Tan^{-1}(x + 2) + c.

Q28. Int 6a2/((x2 + a2)(x2 + 4a2)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 2/(x2 + a2) - 2/(x2 + 4a2).

Answer: (2/a) Tan^{-1}(x/a) - (1/a) Tan^{-1}(x/(2a)) + c.

Q29. Int (2x2 - 2)/(x4 + x2 + 1) dx.

Factor: x4 + x2 + 1 = (x2 + x + 1)(x2 - x + 1).

Partial fractions: the integrand equals (-2x - 1)/(x2 + x + 1) + (2x - 1)/(x2 - x + 1).

The first part gives -ln(x2 + x + 1) and the second gives ln(x2 - x + 1).

Answer: ln((x2 - x + 1)/(x2 + x + 1)) + c.

Q30. Int (3x - 8)/((x2 - x + 2)(x2 + x + 2)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals (2x - 1/2)/(x2 - x + 2) + (-2x - 7/2)/(x2 + x + 2).

The first part gives ln(x2 - x + 2) + (1/sqrt(7)) Tan^{-1}((2x - 1)/sqrt(7)); the second gives -ln(x2 + x + 2) - (5/sqrt(7)) Tan^{-1}((2x + 1)/sqrt(7)).

Answer: ln((x2 - x + 2)/(x2 + x + 2)) + (1/sqrt(7)) Tan^{-1}((2x - 1)/sqrt(7)) (5/sqrt(7)) Tan^{-1}((2x + 1)/sqrt(7)) + c.

Q31. Int (3x3 + 4x2 + 9x + 5)/((x2 + x + 1)(x2 + 2x + 3)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals (2x + 3)/(x2 + x + 1) + (x - 4)/(x2 + 2x + 3).

The first part gives ln(x2 + x + 1) + (4/sqrt(3)) Tan^{-1}((2x + 1)/sqrt(3)); the second gives (1/2) ln(x2 + 2x + 3) - (5/sqrt(2)) Tan^{-1}((x + 1)/sqrt(2)).

Answer: ln(x2 + x + 1) + (4/sqrt(3)) Tan^{-1}((2x + 1)/sqrt(3)) + (1/2) ln(x2 + 2x + 3) - (5/sqrt(2)) Tan^{-1}((x + 1)/sqrt(2)) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (3x + 1)/(x^2 - x - 6) dx
mcqs.why: Factor x^2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2). Partial fractions: (3x + 1)/((x - 3)(x + 2)) = 2/(x - 3) + 1/(x + 2). Integrate each: 2 ln|x - 3| + ln|x + 2| + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (5x + 8)/((x + 3)(2x - 1)) dx
Evaluate: integral of dx/(6x^2 + 5x - 4)
Evaluate: integral of (3x^2 - 12x + 11)/((x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3)) dx
mcqs.why: Partial fractions give exactly 1/(x - 1) + 1/(x - 2) + 1/(x - 3): check at the numerators, each residue is 1. Integrating gives ln|x - 1| + ln|x - 2| + ln|x - 3| = ln|(x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3)| + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of 2x/(x^2 - a^2) dx
mcqs.why: Partial fractions: 2x/((x - a)(x + a)) = 1/(x - a) + 1/(x + a). Integrate: ln|x - a| + ln|x + a| = ln|x^2 - a^2| + c. Equivalently the numerator is the derivative of x^2 - a^2.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (x - 2)/((x + 1)(x^2 + 1)) dx
Evaluate: integral of (1 + 4x)/((x - 3)(x^2 + 4)) dx
Evaluate: integral of 6a^2/((x^2 + a^2)(x^2 + 4a^2)) dx
Evaluate: integral of (2x^2 - 2)/(x^4 + x^2 + 1) dx
mcqs.why: Factor x^4 + x^2 + 1 = (x^2 + x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1). Partial fractions: (-2x - 1)/(x^2 + x + 1) + (2x - 1)/(x^2 - x + 1), whose integrals are -ln(x^2 + x + 1) and +ln(x^2 - x + 1). Result: ln((x^2 - x + 1)/(x^2 + x + 1)) + c.

mcqs.q: Evaluate: integral of (4x + 1)/((x^2 + 4)(x^2 + 4x + 5)) dx
mcqs.why: Partial fractions: the integrand equals 1/(x^2 + 4) - 1/(x^2 + 4x + 5). First integral = (1/2) Tan^(-1)(x/2). Since x^2 + 4x + 5 = (x + 2)^2 + 1, the second integral = Tan^(-1)(x + 2). Result: (1/2) Tan^(-1)(x/2) - Tan^(-1)(x + 2) + c.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.6 — Evaluate the following definite integrals
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Int from 1 to 2 of (x2 + 1) dx.

Antiderivative: x3/3 + x.

Evaluate: (8/3 + 2) - (1/3 + 1) = 14/3 - 4/3.

Answer: 10/3.

Q2. Int from -1 to 1 of (x^(1/3) + 1) dx.

The cube root is an odd function, so its integral over [-1, 1] is 0.

The integral of 1 over [-1, 1] is 2.

Answer: 2.

Q3. Int from -2 to 0 of dx/(2x - 1)2.

Antiderivative: -1/(2(2x - 1)).

Evaluate: -1/(2(-1)) - (-1/(2(-5))) = 1/2 - 1/10.

Answer: 2/5.

Q4. Int from -6 to 2 of sqrt(3 - x) dx.

Antiderivative: -(2/3)(3 - x)^(3/2).

Evaluate: -(2/3)(1)^(3/2) + (2/3)(9)^(3/2) = -2/3 + 18.

Answer: 52/3.

Q5. FLAGGED - Int from ?

to sqrt(?) of sqrt(2t ? 1) dt: limits and sign illegible in the source copy; no answer given. As printed in this copy, Q5 shows a blank lower limit, an upper limit consisting of a bare radical sign with no radicand, and an integrand 'sqrt(2t 1)' whose plus/minus sign is missing (not legible even at 300 DPI).

Without the limits and the sign, the integral cannot be identified, so no evaluation is attempted.

Answer: NOT COMPUTED - the printed item is incomplete in the source copy; nothing has been invented here.

Q6. Int from 2 to sqrt(5) of x sqrt(x2 - 1) dx.

Put u = x2 - 1; then du = 2x dx, so the antiderivative is (1/3)(x2 - 1)^(3/2).

Evaluate: (1/3)(4)^(3/2) - (1/3)(3)^(3/2) = 8/3 - sqrt(3).

Answer: 8/3 - sqrt(3).

Q7. Int from 1 to 2 of x/(x2 + 2) dx.

Antiderivative: (1/2) ln(x2 + 2).

Evaluate: (1/2)(ln 6 - ln 3) = (1/2) ln 2.

Answer: (1/2) ln 2.

Q8. Int from 2 to 3 of (x - 1/x)2 dx.

Expand: (x - 1/x)2 = x2 - 2 + 1/x2; antiderivative x3/3 - 2x - 1/x.

Evaluate: (9 - 6 - 1/3) - (8/3 - 4 - 1/2) = 8/3 + 7/6.

Answer: 23/6.

Q9. Int from -1 to 1 of (x + 1/2) sqrt(x2 + x + 1) dx.

Since x + 1/2 = (1/2)(2x + 1) and d/dx (x2 + x + 1) = 2x + 1, the antiderivative is (1/3)(x2 + x + 1)^(3/2).

Evaluate: (1/3)(3^(3/2) - 1) = sqrt(3) - 1/3.

Answer: sqrt(3) - 1/3.

Q10. Int from 0 to 3 of dx/(x2 + 9).

Antiderivative: (1/3) Tan^{-1}(x/3).

Evaluate: (1/3) Tan^{-1}(1) - 0 = (1/3)(pi/4).

Answer: pi/12.

Q11. Int from pi/6 to pi/3 of cos t dt.

Antiderivative: sin t.

Evaluate: sin(pi/3) - sin(pi/6) = sqrt(3)/2 - 1/2.

Answer: (sqrt(3) - 1)/2.

Q12. Int from 1 to 2 of (x + 1/x)^(1/2) (1 - 1/x2) dx.

Put u = x + 1/x; then du = (1 - 1/x2) dx, so the antiderivative is (2/3)(x + 1/x)^(3/2).

Evaluate: (2/3)[(5/2)^(3/2) - 2^(3/2)] = (5 sqrt(10))/6 - (4 sqrt(2))/3.

Answer: (5 sqrt(10))/6 - (4 sqrt(2))/3.

Q13. Int from 1 to 2 of ln x dx.

Antiderivative: x ln x - x.

Evaluate: (2 ln 2 - 2) - (0 - 1) = 2 ln 2 - 1.

Answer: 2 ln 2 - 1.

Q14. Int from 0 to 2 of (e^(x/2) - e^(-x/2)) dx.

Antiderivative: 2e^(x/2) + 2e^(-x/2).

Evaluate: (2e + 2/e) - 4.

Answer: 2e + 2/e - 4.

Q15. Int from 0 to pi/4 of (cos theta + sin theta)/(2 cos2 theta) d theta.

Split: (1/2) Int (sec theta + sin theta sec2 theta) d theta; antiderivative (1/2)(ln|sec theta + tan theta| + sec theta).

Evaluate: (1/2)[(ln(sqrt(2) + 1) + sqrt(2)) - 1].

Answer: (ln(sqrt(2) + 1) + sqrt(2) - 1)/2.

Q16. Int from 0 to pi/6 of cos3 theta d theta.

Write cos3 theta = (1 - sin2 theta) cos theta; antiderivative sin theta - sin3 theta/3.

Evaluate: 1/2 - (1/8)/3 = 1/2 - 1/24.

Answer: 11/24.

Q17. Int from pi/6 to pi/4 of cos2 theta cot2 theta d theta.

Since cos2 theta cot2 theta = cot2 theta - cos2 theta, the antiderivative is -cot theta - (3 theta/2) - sin 2 theta/4.

Evaluate at pi/4: -5/4 - 3pi/8; at pi/6: -(9 sqrt(3))/8 - pi/4.

Answer: (9 sqrt(3))/8 - 5/4 - pi/8.

Q18. Int from 0 to pi/4 of cos4 t dt.
