Use cos4 t = (3 + 4 cos 2t + cos 4t)/8; antiderivative 3t/8 + sin 2t/4 + sin 4t/32.

Evaluate: 3pi/32 + 1/4.

Answer: 3pi/32 + 1/4.

Q19. Int from 0 to pi/3 of cos2 theta sin theta d theta.

Put u = cos theta; antiderivative -cos3 theta/3.

Evaluate: -(1/8)/3 + 1/3 = 7/24.

Answer: 7/24.

Q20. Int from 0 to pi/4 of (1 + cos2 theta) tan2 theta d theta.

Since (1 + cos2 theta) tan2 theta = sec2 theta - cos2 theta, the antiderivative is tan theta - theta/2 - sin 2 theta/4.

Evaluate: 1 - pi/8 - 1/4.

Answer: 3/4 - pi/8.

Q21. Int from 0 to pi/4 of sec theta/(sin theta + cos theta) d theta.

Divide top and bottom by cos theta: the integrand becomes sec2 theta/(1 + tan theta).

Put u = tan theta: Int from 0 to 1 of du/(1 + u) = ln 2.

Answer: ln 2.

Q22. Int from -1 to 5 of |x - 3| dx.

Split at x = 3: Int from -1 to 3 of (3 - x) dx = 8; Int from 3 to 5 of (x - 3) dx = 2.

Answer: 10.

Q23. Int from 1/8 to 1 of (x^(1/3) + 2)2 / x^(2/3) dx.

Expand: the integrand equals 1 + 4x^(-1/3) + 4x^(-2/3); antiderivative x + 6x^(2/3) + 12x^(1/3).

Evaluate: 19 - (1/8 + 3/2 + 6) = 19 - 61/8.

Answer: 91/8.

Q24. Int from 1 to 3 of (x2 - 2)/(x + 1) dx.

Divide: (x2 - 2)/(x + 1) = x - 1 - 1/(x + 1); antiderivative x2/2 - x - ln|x + 1|.

Evaluate: (3/2 - ln 4) - (-1/2 - ln 2) = 2 - ln 2.

Answer: 2 - ln 2.

Q25. Int from 2 to 3 of (3x2 - 2x + 1)/((x - 1)(x2 + 1)) dx.

Partial fractions: the integrand equals 1/(x - 1) + (2x)/(x2 + 1); antiderivative ln|x 1| + ln(x2 + 1).

Evaluate: (ln 2 + ln 10) - (ln 1 + ln 5) = ln 4.

Answer: ln 4 = 2 ln 2.

Q26. Int from 0 to pi/4 of (sin x - 1)/cos2 x dx.

Write as sin x sec2 x - sec2 x; antiderivative sec x - tan x.

Evaluate: (sqrt(2) - 1) - (1 - 0) = sqrt(2) - 2.

Answer: sqrt(2) - 2.

Q27. Int from 0 to pi/4 of dx/(1 + sin x).

Multiply top and bottom by (1 - sin x): the integrand becomes sec2 x - sec x tan x; antiderivative tan x - sec x.

Evaluate: (1 - sqrt(2)) - (0 - 1) = 2 - sqrt(2).

Answer: 2 - sqrt(2).

Q28. Int from 0 to 1 of 3x/sqrt(4 - 3x) dx.

Put u = 4 - 3x; the integral becomes (1/3) Int from 1 to 4 of (4 - u)/sqrt(u) du.

Antiderivative (1/3)(8 sqrt(u) - (2/3) u^(3/2)); evaluate: (1/3)(32/3 - 22/3).

Answer: 10/9.

Q29. Int from pi/6 to pi/2 of cos x/(sin x (2 + sin x)) dx.

Put u = sin x: the integral becomes Int from 1/2 to 1 of du/(u(2 + u)) = (1/2)[ln(u/(2 + u))] from 1/2 to 1.

Evaluate: (1/2)(ln(1/3) - ln(1/5)) = (1/2) ln(5/3).

Answer: (1/2) ln(5/3).

Q30. Int from 0 to pi/2 of sin x/((1 + cos x)(2 + cos x)) dx.

Put u = cos x: the integral becomes Int from 0 to 1 of du/((1 + u)(2 + u)) = [ln((1 + u)/(2 + u))] from 0 to 1.

Evaluate: ln(2/3) - ln(1/2) = ln(4/3).

Answer: ln(4/3).

mcqs.q: Evaluate the definite integral from 1 to 2 of (x^2 + 1) dx
mcqs.why: Antiderivative is x^3/3 + x. Evaluate: at 2: 8/3 + 2 = 14/3; at 1: 1/3 + 1 = 4/3. Subtract: 14/3 - 4/3 = 10/3.

mcqs.q: Evaluate the definite integral from -1 to 1 of (x^(1/3) + 1) dx
mcqs.why: x^(1/3) is an odd function, so its integral over the symmetric interval [-1, 1] is 0. The integral of 1 from -1 to 1 is 1 - (-1) = 2. Total = 0 + 2 = 2.

mcqs.q: Evaluate the definite integral from -2 to 0 of dx/(2x - 1)^2
Evaluate the definite integral from -6 to 2 of sqrt(3 - x) dx
Evaluate the definite integral from 2 to sqrt(5) of x sqrt(x^2 - 1) dx
Evaluate the definite integral from 1 to 2 of x/(x^2 + 2) dx
mcqs.why: Antiderivative is (1/2) ln(x^2 + 2), since the numerator x is half the derivative of x^2 + 2. Evaluate: (1/2)(ln 6 - ln 3) = (1/2) ln(6/3) = (1/2) ln 2.

mcqs.q: Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 3 of dx/(x^2 + 9)
mcqs.why: Antiderivative is (1/3) Tan^(-1)(x/3). At 3: (1/3) Tan^(-1)(1) = (1/3)(pi/4) = pi/12. At 0 it is 0. Result: pi/12.

mcqs.q: Evaluate the definite integral from 1 to 2 of ln x dx
mcqs.why: Antiderivative is x ln x - x. At 2: 2 ln 2 - 2. At 1: 0 - 1 = -1. Subtract: (2 ln 2 - 2) - (-1) = 2 ln 2 - 1.

mcqs.q: Evaluate the definite integral from -1 to 5 of |x - 3| dx
mcqs.why: Split at x = 3 where the sign changes. From -1 to 3: integral of (3 - x) dx = [3x - x^2/2] = (9 - 9/2) - (-3 - 1/2) = 8. From 3 to 5: integral of (x - 3) dx = 2. Total = 8 + 2 = 10.

mcqs.q: Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/2 of sin x/((1 + cos x)(2 + cos x)) dx
mcqs.why: Put u = cos x, du = -sin x dx; limits become u = 1 to u = 0, flipping gives integral from 0 to 1 of du/((1 + u)(2 + u)) = [ln((1 + u)/(2 + u))] from 0 to 1 = ln(2/3) - ln(1/2) = ln(4/3).

lessons.title: Exercise 3.7 — Areas by definite integrals (answers in square units)
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Area between the x-axis and the curve y = x2 + 1 from x = 1 to x = 2.

Area = Int from 1 to 2 of (x2 + 1) dx = [x3/3 + x] from 1 to 2.

Evaluate: (8/3 + 2) - (1/3 + 1) = 10/3.

Answer: 10/3 square units.

Q2. Area above the x-axis and under the curve y = 5 - x2 from x = -1 to x = 2.

Area = Int from -1 to 2 of (5 - x2) dx = [5x - x3/3] from -1 to 2.

Evaluate: (10 - 8/3) - (-5 + 1/3) = 22/3 + 14/3 = 12.

Answer: 12 square units.

Q3. Area below the curve y = 3 sqrt(x) and above the x-axis between x = 1 and x = 4.

Area = Int from 1 to 4 of 3 sqrt(x) dx = 2[x^(3/2)] from 1 to 4.

Evaluate: 2(8 - 1) = 14.

Answer: 14 square units.

Q4. Area bounded by the cos function from x = -pi/2 to x = pi/2.

On [-pi/2, pi/2], cos x is non-negative, so area = Int from -pi/2 to pi/2 of cos x dx.

Evaluate: sin(pi/2) - sin(-pi/2) = 1 - (-1) = 2.

Answer: 2 square units.

Q5. Area between the x-axis and the curve y = 4x - x2.

The curve cuts the x-axis where 4x - x2 = 0, i.e. at x = 0 and x = 4; it is above the axis between them.

Area = Int from 0 to 4 of (4x - x2) dx = [2x2 - x3/3] from 0 to 4 = 32 - 64/3.

Answer: 32/3 square units.

Q6. Area bounded by the parabola y = x2 + 2x - 3 and the x-axis.

The parabola cuts the x-axis where (x + 3)(x - 1) = 0, i.e. at x = -3 and x = 1; it lies below the axis between them.

Area = -Int from -3 to 1 of (x2 + 2x - 3) dx = -[x3/3 + x2 - 3x] from -3 to 1.

Evaluate: -[(-5/3) - 9] = 32/3.

Answer: 32/3 square units.

Q7. Area bounded by the curve y = x3 + 1, the x-axis and the line x = 2.

The curve cuts the x-axis at x = -1, so the enclosed region runs from x = -1 to x = 2.

Area = Int from -1 to 2 of (x3 + 1) dx = [x4/4 + x] from -1 to 2.

Evaluate: 6 - (1/4 - 1) = 27/4.

Answer: 27/4 square units.

Q8. Area bounded by the curve y = x3 - 4x and the x-axis.

The curve cuts the x-axis at x = -2, 0, 2; the two lobes are symmetric in area.

Area = 2 Int from 0 to 2 of (4x - x3) dx = 2[2x2 - x4/4] from 0 to 2 = 2(8 - 4).

Answer: 8 square units.

Q9. Area between the curve y = x(x - 1)(x + 1) and the x-axis.

The curve is y = x3 - x, cutting the x-axis at x = -1, 0, 1; the two lobes are symmetric in area.

Area = 2 Int from 0 to 1 of (x - x3) dx = 2[1/2 - 1/4] = 1/2.

Answer: 1/2 square unit.

Q10. Area above the x-axis, bounded by the curve y2 = 3 - x, from x = -1 to x = 2.

Above the x-axis, y = sqrt(3 - x).

Area = Int from -1 to 2 of sqrt(3 - x) dx = [-(2/3)(3 - x)^(3/2)] from -1 to 2.

Evaluate: -(2/3)(1) + (2/3)(8) = 14/3.

Answer: 14/3 square units.

Q11. Area between the x-axis and the curve y = -cos(x/2) from x = -pi to x = pi.

On [-pi, pi], cos(x/2) is non-negative, so |y| = cos(x/2).

Area = Int from -pi to pi of cos(x/2) dx = [2 sin(x/2)] from -pi to pi = 2(1 - (-1)).

Answer: 4 square units.

Q12. Area between the x-axis and the curve y = sin 2x from x = 0 to x = pi/3.

On [0, pi/3], sin 2x is non-negative.

Area = Int from 0 to pi/3 of sin 2x dx = [-cos 2x/2] from 0 to pi/3 = (1/2 + 1)/2.

Answer: 3/4 square units.

Q13. Area between the x-axis and the curve y = sqrt(2a x - x2) when a > 0.

The curve is the upper semicircle of radius a centred at (a, 0), meeting the x-axis at x = 0 and x = 2a.

Area = Int from 0 to 2a of sqrt(2a x - x2) dx = (1/2) pi a2 (area of a semicircle of radius a).

Answer: (pi a2)/2 square units.

mcqs.q: The area between the x-axis and the curve y = x^2 + 1 from x = 1 to x = 2 is:
mcqs.why: Area = integral from 1 to 2 of (x^2 + 1) dx = [x^3/3 + x] from 1 to 2 = (8/3 + 2) - (1/3 + 1) = 14/3 - 4/3 = 10/3 square units.

mcqs.q: The area above the x-axis and under y = 5 - x^2 from x = -1 to x = 2 is:
mcqs.why: Area = integral from -1 to 2 of (5 - x^2) dx = [5x - x^3/3] from -1 to 2 = (10 - 8/3) - (-5 + 1/3) = 22/3 + 14/3 = 36/3 = 12 square units.

mcqs.q: The area below y = 3 sqrt(x) and above the x-axis between x = 1 and x = 4 is:
mcqs.why: Area = integral from 1 to 4 of 3 sqrt(x) dx = 3 x (2/3)[x^(3/2)] from 1 to 4 = 2(4^(3/2) - 1^(3/2)) = 2(8 - 1) = 14 square units.

mcqs.q: The area bounded by the cos function from x = -pi/2 to x = pi/2 is:
mcqs.why: On [-pi/2, pi/2], cos x is non-negative, so area = integral of cos x dx = [sin x] from -pi/2 to pi/2 = sin(pi/2) - sin(-pi/2) = 1 - (-1) = 2 square units.

mcqs.q: The area between the x-axis and the curve y = 4x - x^2 is:
mcqs.why: The curve cuts the axis where 4x - x^2 = x(4 - x) = 0, at x = 0 and x = 4, and is above the axis between them. Area = integral from 0 to 4 of (4x - x^2) dx = [2x^2 - x^3/3] from 0 to 4 = 32 - 64/3 = 32/3 square units.

mcqs.q: The area bounded by the parabola y = x^2 + 2x - 3 and the x-axis is:
mcqs.why: Roots: (x + 3)(x - 1) = 0 gives x = -3 and x = 1; the parabola is below the axis between them, so area = -integral from -3 to 1 of (x^2 + 2x - 3) dx = -[x^3/3 + x^2 - 3x] = -[(-5/3) - 9] = 32/3 square units.

mcqs.q: The area bounded by y = x^3 + 1, the x-axis and the line x = 2 is:
mcqs.why: The curve cuts the x-axis at x = -1 (since (-1)^3 + 1 = 0), so the region runs from -1 to 2. Area = integral from -1 to 2 of (x^3 + 1) dx = [x^4/4 + x] = (4 + 2) - (1/4 - 1) = 6 + 3/4 = 27/4 square units.

mcqs.q: The area bounded by the curve y = x^3 - 4x and the x-axis is:
mcqs.why: Roots are x = -2, 0, 2 and the two lobes have equal area. Area = 2 x integral from 0 to 2 of (4x - x^3) dx = 2[2x^2 - x^4/4] from 0 to 2 = 2(8 - 4) = 8 square units.

mcqs.q: The area between the curve y = x(x - 1)(x + 1) and the x-axis is:
mcqs.why: y = x^3 - x cuts the axis at -1, 0, 1 and the two lobes are symmetric. Area = 2 x integral from 0 to 1 of (x - x^3) dx = 2[x^2/2 - x^4/4] from 0 to 1 = 2(1/2 - 1/4) = 1/2 square unit.

mcqs.q: The area between the x-axis and y = sin 2x from x = 0 to x = pi/3 is:
mcqs.why: On [0, pi/3], sin 2x is non-negative. Area = integral from 0 to pi/3 of sin 2x dx = [-cos 2x/2] from 0 to pi/3 = (-cos(2pi/3))/2 - (-cos 0)/2 = (1/2)/2 + 1/2 = 1/4 + 1/2 = 3/4 square units.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.8
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Check that each of the following equations written against the differential equation is its solution

Q1(i). Equation x dy/dx = 1 + y; solution y = c x - 1. Differentiate the solution: dy/dx = c.

Left side: x dy/dx = c x. Right side: 1 + y = 1 + c x - 1 = c x.

Both sides agree, so the equation is satisfied.

Answer: verified.

Q1(ii). Equation x2(2y + 1) dy/dx - 1 = 0; solution y2 + y = c - 1/x. Differentiate the solution: (2y + 1) dy/dx = 1/x2.

Multiply by x2: x2(2y + 1) dy/dx = 1, i.e. x2(2y + 1) dy/dx - 1 = 0.

Answer: verified.

Q1(iii). Equation y dy/dx - e^(2x) = 1; solution y2 = e^(2x) + 2x + c. Differentiate the solution: 2y dy/dx = 2e^(2x) + 2.

Divide by 2: y dy/dx = e^(2x) + 1, i.e. y dy/dx - e^(2x) = 1.

Answer: verified.

Q1(iv). Equation (1/x) dy/dx - 2y = 0; solution y = c e^(x2). Differentiate the solution: dy/dx = 2x c e^(x2) = 2x y.

Then (1/x) dy/dx = 2y, i.e. (1/x) dy/dx - 2y = 0.

Answer: verified.

Q1(v). Equation dy/dx = (y2 + 1)/e^(-x); solution y = tan(e^x + c). Differentiate the solution: dy/dx = sec2(e^x + c) e^x = (1 + y2) e^x.

Since 1/e^(-x) = e^x, this is dy/dx = (y2 + 1)/e^(-x).

Answer: verified.

Q2. dy/dx = -y.

Exercise 3.8, Q2-Q18 - Solve the following differential equations (c = arbitrary constant)

Separate: dy/y = -dx.

Integrate: ln|y| = -x + c.

Answer: y = C e^(-x).

Q3. y dx + x dy = 0.

This is d(x y) = 0.

Integrate: x y = c.

Answer: x y = c.

Q4. dy/dx = (1 - x)/y.

Separate: y dy = (1 - x) dx.

Integrate: y2/2 = x - x2/2 + c.

Answer: y2 = 2x - x2 + C.

Q5. dy/dx = y/x2, y > 0.

Separate: dy/y = dx/x2.

Integrate: ln y = -1/x + c.

Answer: y = C e^(-1/x).

Q6. sin y cosec x dy/dx = 1.

Separate: sin y dy = sin x dx (since 1/cosec x = sin x).

Integrate: -cos y = -cos x + c.

Answer: cos y = cos x + C.

Q7. x dy + y(x - 1) dx = 0.

Separate: dy/y = -(x - 1)/x dx = (-1 + 1/x) dx.

Integrate: ln|y| = -x + ln|x| + c.

Answer: y = C x e^(-x).

Q8. (x2 + 1)/(y + 1) = (x/y) dy/dx, x, y > 0.

Rearrange: dy/dx = y(x2 + 1)/(x(y + 1)).

Separate: (y + 1)/y dy = (x2 + 1)/x dx, i.e. (1 + 1/y) dy = (x + 1/x) dx.

Integrate: y + ln y = x2/2 + ln x + c.

Answer: y + ln y = x2/2 + ln x + c.

Q9. (1/x) dy/dx = (1/2)(1 + y2).

Separate: dy/(1 + y2) = (x/2) dx.

Integrate: Tan^{-1} y = x2/4 + c.

Answer: Tan^{-1} y = x2/4 + c.

Q10. 2x2 y dy/dx = x2 - 1.

Separate: y dy = (x2 - 1)/(2x2) dx = (1/2 - 1/(2x2)) dx.

Integrate: y2/2 = x/2 + 1/(2x) + c.

Answer: y2 = x + 1/x + C.

Q11. dy/dx + 2x y/(2y + 1) = x.

Bring the fraction over: dy/dx = x - 2x y/(2y + 1) = x/(2y + 1).

Separate: (2y + 1) dy = x dx.

Integrate: y2 + y = x2/2 + c.

Answer: y2 + y = x2/2 + c.

Q12. (x2 - y x2) dy/dx + y2 + x y2 = 0.

Factor: x2(1 - y) dy/dx + y2(1 + x) = 0.

Separate: (1 - y)/y2 dy = -(1 + x)/x2 dx.

Integrate: -1/y - ln|y| = 1/x - ln|x| + c.

Answer: ln|x/y| = 1/x + 1/y + C.

Q13. sec2 x tan y dx + sec2 y tan x dy = 0.

Separate: tan x sec2 x dx = -tan y sec2 y dy.

Integrate: (1/2) tan2 x = -(1/2) tan2 y + c.

Answer: tan2 x + tan2 y = C.

Q14. (y - x dy/dx) = 2(y2 + dy/dx).

Expand: y - x dy/dx = 2y2 + 2 dy/dx, so (x + 2) dy/dx = y - 2y2.

Separate: dy/(y - 2y2) = dx/(x + 2).

Integrate: ln|y/(1 - 2y)| = ln|x + 2| + c.

Answer: y/(1 - 2y) = C(x + 2).

Q15. 1 + cos x tan y dy/dx = 0.

Separate: tan y dy = -dx/(1 + cos x).

Integrate: -ln|cos y| = -tan(x/2) + c, since Int dx/(1 + cos x) = tan(x/2).

Answer: cos y = C e^(tan(x/2)).

Q16. y - x dy/dx = 3(1 + x dy/dx).

Expand: y - x dy/dx = 3 + 3x dy/dx, so 4x dy/dx = y - 3.

Separate: dy/(y - 3) = dx/(4x).

Integrate: ln|y - 3| = (1/4) ln|x| + c.

Answer: y - 3 = C x^(1/4).

Q17. sec x + tan y dy/dx = 0.

Separate: tan y dy = -sec x dx.

Integrate: -ln|cos y| = -ln|sec x + tan x| + c.

Answer: cos y = C(sec x + tan x).

Q18. (e^x + e^(-x)) dy/dx = e^x - e^(-x).

(Print note: the RHS operator is faint in this copy; read as minus, the standard form.) Separate: dy = (e^x - e^(-x))/(e^x + e^(-x)) dx.

The numerator is the derivative of the denominator, so integrate: y = ln(e^x + e^(-x)) + c.

Answer: y = ln(e^x + e^(-x)) + c.

Separate: dy/(1 + y2) = x dx; integrate: Tan^{-1} y = x2/2 + c.

General solution: y = tan(x2/2 + c).

Particular: y = 1 at x = 0 gives c = pi/4.

Answer: y = tan(x2/2 + pi/4).

Q20. Solve dx/dt = 2x given that x = 4 when t = 0.

Exercise 3.8, Q19-Q23 - Differential equations and applications Q19. General solution of dy/dx - x = x y2; also the particular solution if y = 1 when x = 0. Rewrite: dy/dx = x(1 + y2).

Separate: dx/x = 2 dt; integrate: ln|x| = 2t + c, so x = C e^(2t).

Particular: x = 4 at t = 0 gives C = 4.

Answer: x = 4 e^(2t).

Q21. Solve ds/dt + 2s t = 0; also the particular solution if s = 4e when t = 0.

Separate: ds/s = -2t dt; integrate: ln|s| = -t2 + c, so s = C e^(-t2).

Particular: s = 4e at t = 0 gives C = 4e.

Answer: s = 4e^(1 - t2).

Q22. In a culture, bacteria increase at a rate proportional to the number present.

If there are 200 initially and they double in 2 hours, find the number present four hours later. Let N(t) be the number: dN/dt = k N, so N = 200 e^(k t).

Doubling in 2 hours: 400 = 200 e^(2k), so e^(2k) = 2.

After 4 hours: N = 200 e^(4k) = 200 (e^(2k))2 = 200 x 4.

Answer: 800 bacteria.

Q23. A ball is thrown vertically upward with a velocity of 2450 cm/sec.

Neglecting air resistance, find (i) velocity at any time t, (ii) distance traveled in any time t, (iii) maximum height attained by the ball. (Take g = 980 cm/sec2.) (i) dv/dt = -g gives v = 2450 - 980t.

(ii) Since v = dh/dt, h = 2450t - 490t2 (starting from h = 0 at t = 0).

(iii) Maximum height when v = 0, i.e. t = 2450/980 = 2.5 sec; h = 2450(2.5) 490(2.5)2 = 6125 - 3062.5.

Answer: (i) v = 2450 - 980t cm/sec; (ii) h = 2450t - 490t2 cm; (iii) maximum height 3062.5 cm.

mcqs.q: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = -y
mcqs.why: Separate variables: dy/y = -dx. Integrate both sides: ln|y| = -x + c. Exponentiating gives y = C e^(-x), and differentiating C e^(-x) gives -C e^(-x) = -y, confirming it.

mcqs.q: Solve the differential equation y dx + x dy = 0
mcqs.why: The left side is exactly d(x y) by the product rule: d(x y) = y dx + x dy. So d(x y) = 0, and integrating gives x y = c.

mcqs.q: Solve dy/dx = (1 - x)/y
mcqs.why: Separate: y dy = (1 - x) dx. Integrate: y^2/2 = x - x^2/2 + c. Multiply by 2 and absorb 2c into C: y^2 = 2x - x^2 + C.

mcqs.q: Solve dy/dx = y/x^2, for y > 0
mcqs.why: Separate: dy/y = dx/x^2. Integrate: ln y = -1/x + c, since integral of x^(-2) dx = -1/x. Exponentiating gives y = C e^(-1/x).

mcqs.q: Solve sin y cosec x dy/dx = 1
mcqs.why: Since 1/cosec x = sin x, separating gives sin y dy = sin x dx. Integrate: -cos y = -cos x + c, so cos y = cos x + C after absorbing the sign into the constant.

mcqs.q: Solve x dy + y(x - 1) dx = 0
mcqs.why: Divide by x y: dy/y = -(x - 1)/x dx = (-1 + 1/x) dx. Integrate: ln|y| = -x + ln|x| + c. Exponentiating: y = C x e^(-x).

mcqs.q: Find the particular solution of dy/dx - x = x y^2 with y = 1 when x = 0
mcqs.why: Rewrite dy/dx = x(1 + y^2). Separate: dy/(1 + y^2) = x dx. Integrate: Tan^(-1) y = x^2/2 + c, so y = tan(x^2/2 + c). At x = 0, y = 1 gives tan c = 1, c = pi/4. Particular solution: y = tan(x^2/2 + pi/4).

mcqs.q: Solve dx/dt = 2x given that x = 4 when t = 0
mcqs.why: Separate: dx/x = 2 dt. Integrate: ln|x| = 2t + c, so x = C e^(2t). At t = 0, x = 4 gives C = 4. Hence x = 4 e^(2t).

mcqs.q: Bacteria increase at a rate proportional to the number present. If there are 200 initially and they double in 2 hours, the number present after 4 hours is:
mcqs.why: dN/dt = kN gives N = 200 e^(k t). Doubling in 2 hours: 400 = 200 e^(2k), so e^(2k) = 2. After 4 hours: N = 200 e^(4k) = 200 (e^(2k))^2 = 200 x 4 = 800.

mcqs.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward at 2450 cm/sec (g = 980 cm/sec^2, no air resistance). The maximum height attained is:

lessons.title: Exercise 4.1 — Distance, midpoint and section formula
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Describe the location in the plane of the point P(x, y) for which (i) x > 0 (ii) x > 0 and y > 0 (iii) x = 0 (iv) y = 0 (v) x < 0 and y >= 0 (vi) x = y (vii) |x| = |y| (viii) |x| >= 3 (ix) x > 2 and y = 2 (x) x and y have opposite signs.

(i) x > 0 means P lies to the right of the y-axis: the right half-plane, y-axis excluded.

(ii) x > 0 and y > 0 means P lies in the interior of the first quadrant.

(iii) x = 0 means P lies on the y-axis; (iv) y = 0 means P lies on the x-axis.

(v) x < 0 and y >= 0 means P lies in the second quadrant together with the negative x-axis.

(vi) x = y means P lies on the line y = x, the bisector of the first and third quadrants.

(vii) |x| = |y| means y = x or y = -x: P lies on either bisector of the quadrants.

(viii) |x| >= 3 means P lies on or outside the vertical strip -3 < x < 3, i.e. on or to the left of x = -3, or on or to the right of x = 3.

(ix) x > 2 and y = 2 means P lies on the ray of the line y = 2 to the right of (2, 2), the point (2, 2) excluded.

Answer: (x) x and y of opposite signs means P lies in the interior of the second or the fourth quadrant.

Q2. Find in each case (i) the distance between the two given points (ii) the midpoint of the line segment joining them: (a) A(3, 1); B(-2, -4) (b) A(-8, 3); B(2, -1) (c) A(-sqrt(5), -1/3); B(-3 sqrt(5), 5).

Distance formula: d = sqrt[(x2 - x1)2 + (y2 - y1)2]; midpoint = ((x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2).

(a) Distance = sqrt[(-5)2 + (-5)2] = sqrt(50) = 5 sqrt(2); midpoint = ((3 - 2)/2, (1 4)/2) = (1/2, -3/2).

(b) Distance = sqrt[(10)2 + (-4)2] = sqrt(116) = 2 sqrt(29); midpoint = ((-8 + 2)/2, (3 - 1)/2) = (-3, 1).

(c) Distance = sqrt[(-2 sqrt(5))2 + (16/3)2] = sqrt(20 + 256/9) = sqrt(436/9) = 2 sqrt(109)/3.

Answer: (c) midpoint = ((-sqrt(5) - 3 sqrt(5))/2, (-1/3 + 5)/2) = (-2 sqrt(5), 7/3).

Q3. Which of the following points are at a distance of 15 units from the origin?

(a) (sqrt(176), 7) (b) (10, -10) (c) (1, 15) (d) (15/2, 15/2). A point (x, y) is 15 units from the origin exactly when x2 + y2 = 225.

(a) 176 + 49 = 225, so (sqrt(176), 7) is at distance 15.

(b) 100 + 100 = 200, not 225; (c) 1 + 225 = 226, not 225.

(d) 225/4 + 225/4 = 225/2, not 225.

Answer: only (a) is at a distance of 15 units from the origin.

Q4. Show that (i) A(0, 2), B(sqrt(3), 1) and C(0, -2) are vertices of a right triangle (ii) A(3, 1), B(-2, -3) and C(2, 2) are vertices of an isosceles triangle (iii) A(5, 2), B(-2, 3), C(-3, -4) and D(4, -5) are vertices of a parallelogram.

Is the parallelogram a square?

(i) AB2 = 3 + 1 = 4, BC2 = 3 + 9 = 12, AC2 = 0 + 16 = 16; AB2 + BC2 = AC2, so the triangle is right-angled at B.

(ii) AB2 = 25 + 16 = 41, BC2 = 16 + 25 = 41, AC2 = 1 + 1 = 2; AB = BC, so the triangle is isosceles with vertex B.

(iii) Midpoint of AC = (1, -1) and midpoint of BD = (1, -1); the diagonals bisect each other, so ABCD is a parallelogram.

Each side squared is 50: AB2 = 49 + 1, BC2 = 1 + 49, CD2 = 49 + 1, DA2 = 1 + 49, so all sides are equal; also AC2 = 64 + 36 = 100 and BD2 = 36 + 64 = 100, so the diagonals are equal.

Answer: a rhombus with equal diagonals is a square, so yes, the parallelogram is a square.

Q5. The midpoints of the sides of a triangle are (1, -1), (-4, -3) and (-1, 1).

Find the coordinates of the vertices of the triangle. Let the midpoints of BC, CA, AB be (1, -1), (-4, -3), (-1, 1) respectively.

A vertex is the sum of the two adjacent midpoints minus the opposite midpoint: A = (-4, -3) + (-1, 1) - (1, -1) = (-6, -1).

Similarly B = (-1, 1) + (1, -1) - (-4, -3) = (4, 3), and C = (1, -1) + (-4, -3) - (-1, 1) = (-2, -5).

Check: midpoint of BC = (1, -1), of CA = (-4, -3), of AB = (-1, 1), as given.

Answer: the vertices are (-6, -1), (4, 3) and (-2, -5).

Q6. Find h such that A(sqrt(3), -1), B(0, 2) and C(h, -2) are vertices of a right triangle with right angle at the vertex A.

At A, vectors AB = (-sqrt(3), 3) and AC = (h - sqrt(3), -1) must be perpendicular, so their dot product is 0.

Dot product: -sqrt(3)(h - sqrt(3)) + 3(-1) = -sqrt(3) h + 3 - 3 = -sqrt(3) h.

Setting this to 0 gives h = 0.

Answer: h = 0.

Q7. Find h such that A(-1, h), B(3, 2) and C(7, 3) are collinear.

Collinear points have equal slopes: slope AB = slope BC.

Slope AB = (2 - h)/(3 - (-1)) = (2 - h)/4; slope BC = (3 - 2)/(7 - 3) = 1/4.

Equating: (2 - h)/4 = 1/4, so 2 - h = 1.

Answer: h = 1.

Q8. The points A(-5, -2) and B(5, -4) are ends of a diameter of a circle.

Find the centre and radius of the circle. The centre is the midpoint of the diameter: ((-5 + 5)/2, (-2 - 4)/2) = (0, -3).

AB2 = (10)2 + (-2)2 = 104, so AB = sqrt(104) = 2 sqrt(26); the radius is half the diameter.

Answer: centre (0, -3), radius sqrt(26).

Q9. Find h such that A(h, 1), B(2, 7) and C(-6, -7) are vertices of a right triangle with right angle at the vertex A.

At A, vectors AB = (2 - h, 6) and AC = (-6 - h, -8) must be perpendicular, so their dot product is 0.

Dot product: (2 - h)(-6 - h) + 6(-8) = (h2 + 4h - 12) - 48 = h2 + 4h - 60.

h2 + 4h - 60 = 0 gives (h + 10)(h - 6) = 0.

Answer: h = 6 or h = -10.

Q10. A quadrilateral has vertices A(9, 3), B(-7, 7), C(-3, -7) and D(5, -5).

Find the midpoints of its sides. Show that the figure formed by joining the midpoints consecutively is a parallelogram. Midpoints: AB = (1, 5), BC = (-5, 0), CD = (1, -6), DA = (7, -1).

Joining them consecutively gives a quadrilateral; its diagonals join (1, 5) to (1, -6) and (-5, 0) to (7, -1).

Midpoint of the first diagonal = (1, -1/2); midpoint of the second diagonal = (1, -1/2).

The diagonals of the midpoint figure bisect each other, so it is a parallelogram.

Answer: midpoints (1, 5), (-5, 0), (1, -6), (7, -1); the midpoint figure is a parallelogram.

Q11. Find h such that the quadrilateral with vertices A(-3, 0), B(1, -2), C(5, 0) and D(1, h) is a parallelogram.

Is it a square? For a parallelogram the diagonals bisect each other: midpoint of AC = (1, 0) must equal midpoint of BD = (1, (h - 2)/2).

So (h - 2)/2 = 0, giving h = 2.

With h = 2, each side squared is 20 (AB2 = 16 + 4, and likewise for the others), so it is a rhombus; but diagonal AC = 8 while diagonal BD = 4, so the diagonals are not equal.

Answer: h = 2; it is a rhombus but not a square.

Q12. If two vertices of an equilateral triangle are A(-3, 0) and B(3, 0), find the third vertex.

How many of these triangles are possible? AB = 6, so the third vertex lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, the line x = 0, at height equal to the altitude of an equilateral triangle of side 6.

Altitude = (sqrt(3)/2) x 6 = 3 sqrt(3).

The third vertex is (0, 3 sqrt(3)) above AB or (0, -3 sqrt(3)) below AB.

Answer: two triangles are possible, with third vertex (0, 3 sqrt(3)) or (0, -3 sqrt(3)).

Q13. Find the points trisecting the join of A(-1, 4) and B(6, 2).

Trisection points divide AB in the ratios 1:2 and 2:1.

First point (ratio 1:2) = ((2(-1) + 6)/3, (2(4) + 2)/3) = (4/3, 10/3).

Second point (ratio 2:1) = ((-1 + 2(6))/3, (4 + 2(2))/3) = (11/3, 8/3).

Answer: (4/3, 10/3) and (11/3, 8/3).

Q14. Find the point three-fifth of the way along the line segment from A(-5, 8) to B(5, 3).

Three-fifth of the way means the point divides AB in the ratio 3:2.

Point = ((2(-5) + 3(5))/5, (2(8) + 3(3))/5) = (5/5, 25/5).

Answer: (1, 5).

Q15. Find the point P on the join of A(1, 4) and B(5, 6) that is twice as far from A as B is from A and lies (i) on the same side of A as B does (ii) on the opposite side of A as B does.

AP = 2 AB, so P = A + 2(B - A) on the same side, and P = A - 2(B - A) on the opposite side; B - A = (4, 2).

(i) P = (1, 4) + 2(4, 2) = (9, 8).

(ii) P = (1, 4) - 2(4, 2) = (-7, 0).

Answer: (i) (9, 8); (ii) (-7, 0).

Q16. Find the point which is equidistant from A(5, 3), B(-2, 2) and C(4, 2).

What is the radius of the circumcircle of triangle ABC? B and C have the same y-coordinate, so the perpendicular bisector of BC is x = (-2 + 4)/2 = 1; let the centre be (1, k).

Equate squared distances to B and A: (1 + 2)2 + (k - 2)2 = (1 - 5)2 + (k - 3)2.

That is 9 + (k - 2)2 = 16 + (k - 3)2, giving 13 - 4k = 25 - 6k, so 2k = 12 and k = 6.

Radius = distance from (1, 6) to B(-2, 2) = sqrt(9 + 16) = 5.

Answer: the equidistant point is (1, 6); circumradius 5.

Q17. The points (4, -2), (-2, 4) and (5, 5) are the vertices of a triangle.

Find the in-centre of the triangle. Side lengths: a = BC = sqrt(49 + 1) = 5 sqrt(2); b = CA = sqrt(1 + 49) = 5 sqrt(2); c = AB = sqrt(36 + 36) = 6 sqrt(2).

In-centre = (aA + bB + cC)/(a + b + c), with a + b + c = 16 sqrt(2).

x-coordinate = (5 sqrt(2)(4) + 5 sqrt(2)(-2) + 6 sqrt(2)(5))/(16 sqrt(2)) = 40/16 = 5/2.

y-coordinate = (5 sqrt(2)(-2) + 5 sqrt(2)(4) + 6 sqrt(2)(5))/(16 sqrt(2)) = 40/16 = 5/2.

Answer: in-centre (5/2, 5/2).

Q18. Find the points that divide the line segment joining A(x1, y1) and B(x2, y2) into four equal parts.

The division points divide AB in the ratios 1:3, 1:1 and 3:1.

Ratio 1:3: ((3x1 + x2)/4, (3y1 + y2)/4).

Ratio 1:1 (midpoint): ((x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2).

Ratio 3:1: ((x1 + 3x2)/4, (y1 + 3y2)/4).

Answer: the three points above, in order from A to B.

mcqs.q: What is the distance between A(3, 1) and B(-2, -4)?
What is the midpoint of the segment joining A(-8, 3) and B(2, -1)?
Which point is at a distance of 15 units from the origin?
mcqs.why: A point is 15 from the origin when x^2+y^2=225. For (sqrt(176),7): 176+49=225, so distance = sqrt(225)=15. The others give 200, 226 and 225/2.

mcqs.q: A(-5, -2) and B(5, -4) are ends of a diameter of a circle. What are its centre and radius?
mcqs.why: Centre is midpoint of diameter: ((-5+5)/2, (-2-4)/2) = (0, -3). AB = sqrt[(10)^2+(-2)^2]=sqrt(104)=2 sqrt(26), so radius = AB/2 = sqrt(26).

mcqs.q: What is the point three-fifth of the way along the segment from A(-5, 8) to B(5, 3)?
What is the point equidistant from A(5, 3), B(-2, 2) and C(4, 2)?
mcqs.why: Perpendicular bisector of BC (same y) is x = (-2+4)/2 = 1. Let centre (1,k): (1+2)^2+(k-2)^2 = (1-5)^2+(k-3)^2 gives 9+(k-2)^2=16+(k-3)^2, so 13-4k=25-6k, 2k=12, k=6. Point is (1,6).

mcqs.q: Find h so that A(h, 1), B(2, 7) and C(-6, -7) form a right triangle with right angle at A.
Find h so that A(-1, h), B(3, 2) and C(7, 3) are collinear.
mcqs.why: Collinear means slope AB = slope BC. Slope AB = (2-h)/(3-(-1)) = (2-h)/4. Slope BC = (3-2)/(7-3)=1/4. So (2-h)/4=1/4, 2-h=1, h=1.

mcqs.q: Two vertices of an equilateral triangle are A(-3, 0) and B(3, 0). What are the possible third vertices?
mcqs.why: AB=6. Third vertex is on perpendicular bisector x=0 at altitude height (sqrt(3)/2) x 6 = 3 sqrt(3) above or below AB, giving (0, 3 sqrt(3)) or (0, -3 sqrt(3)); two triangles are possible.

mcqs.q: Where does the point P(x, y) lie when x < 0 and y >= 0?
options: In the second quadrant together with the negative x-axis
mcqs.why: x < 0 is left of the y-axis and y >= 0 is on or above the x-axis. The notes state this is the second quadrant together with the negative x-axis (where y=0 and x<0).

lessons.title: Exercise 4.2 — Translation and rotation of axes
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. The two points P and O' are given in the xy-coordinate system.

Find the XY-coordinates of P referred to the translated axes O'X and O'Y: (i) P(3, 2); O'(1, 3) (ii) P(-2, 6); O'(-3, 2) (iii) P(-6, -8); O'(-4, -6) (iv) P(3/2, 5/2); O'(-1/2, 7/2). For translation through O'(h, k): X = x - h, Y = y - k.

(i) X = 3 - 1 = 2, Y = 2 - 3 = -1, so P = (2, -1).

(ii) X = -2 - (-3) = 1, Y = 6 - 2 = 4, so P = (1, 4).

(iii) X = -6 - (-4) = -2, Y = -8 - (-6) = -2, so P = (-2, -2).

Answer: (iv) X = 3/2 - (-1/2) = 2, Y = 5/2 - 7/2 = -1, so P = (2, -1).

Q2. The xy-coordinate axes are translated through the point whose coordinates are given in the xy-coordinate system.

The coordinates of P are given in the XY-coordinate system. Find the coordinates of P in the xy-coordinate system: (i) P(8, 10); O'(3, 4) (ii) P(-5, -3); O'(-2, -6) (iii) P(-3/4, -7/6); O'(1/4, -1/6) (iv) P(4, -3); O'(-2, 3). For translation through O'(h, k): x = X + h, y = Y + k.

(i) x = 8 + 3 = 11, y = 10 + 4 = 14, so P = (11, 14).

(ii) x = -5 + (-2) = -7, y = -3 + (-6) = -9, so P = (-7, -9).

(iii) x = -3/4 + 1/4 = -1/2, y = -7/6 + (-1/6) = -4/3, so P = (-1/2, -4/3).

Answer: (iv) x = 4 + (-2) = 2, y = -3 + 3 = 0, so P = (2, 0).

Q3. The xy-coordinate axes are rotated about the origin through the indicated angle.

The new axes are OX and OY. Find the XY-coordinates of the point P with the given xy-coordinates: (i) P(5, 3); theta = 45 degrees (ii) P(3, -7); theta = 30 degrees (iii) P(11, -15); theta = 60 degrees (iv) P(15, 10); theta = arctan(1/3). For rotation through theta: X = x cos theta + y sin theta, Y = y cos theta - x sin theta.

(i) theta = 45 degrees: X = (5 + 3)(sqrt(2)/2) = 4 sqrt(2); Y = (3 - 5)(sqrt(2)/2) = -sqrt(2).

(ii) theta = 30 degrees: X = 3(sqrt(3)/2) - 7(1/2) = (3 sqrt(3) - 7)/2; Y = -7(sqrt(3)/2) - 3(1/2) = (-7 sqrt(3) - 3)/2.

(iii) theta = 60 degrees: X = 11(1/2) - 15(sqrt(3)/2) = (11 - 15 sqrt(3))/2; Y = -15(1/2) - 11(sqrt(3)/2) = (-15 - 11 sqrt(3))/2.

Answer: (iv) theta = arctan(1/3) gives sin theta = 1/sqrt(10), cos theta = 3/sqrt(10): X = 45/sqrt(10) + 10/sqrt(10) = 55/sqrt(10) = 11 sqrt(10)/2; Y = 30/sqrt(10) 15/sqrt(10) = 15/sqrt(10) = 3 sqrt(10)/2.

Q4. The xy-coordinate axes are rotated about the origin through the indicated angle and the new axes are OX and OY.

Find the xy-coordinates of P with the given XY-coordinates: (i) P(-5, 3); theta = 30 degrees (ii) P(-7 sqrt(2), 5 sqrt(2)); theta = 45 degrees. For the inverse rotation: x = X cos theta - Y sin theta, y = X sin theta + Y cos theta.

(i) theta = 30 degrees: x = -5(sqrt(3)/2) - 3(1/2) = (-5 sqrt(3) - 3)/2; y = -5(1/2) + 3(sqrt(3)/2) = (-5 + 3 sqrt(3))/2.

Answer: (ii) theta = 45 degrees: x = (-7 sqrt(2) - 5 sqrt(2))(sqrt(2)/2) = -12; y = (-7 sqrt(2) + 5 sqrt(2))(sqrt(2)/2) = -2; so P = (-12, -2).

mcqs.q: For translation through O'(1, 3), what are the XY-coordinates of P(3, 2)?
mcqs.why: For translation through O'(h,k): X = x-h, Y = y-k. So X = 3-1 = 2 and Y = 2-3 = -1, giving P = (2, -1) in XY-coordinates.

mcqs.q: For translation through O'(-3, 2), what are the XY-coordinates of P(-2, 6)?
mcqs.why: X = x-h = -2-(-3) = -2+3 = 1. Y = y-k = 6-2 = 4. So the translated coordinates are P = (1, 4).

mcqs.q: For translation through O'(-4, -6), what are the XY-coordinates of P(-6, -8)?
Axes are translated through O'(3, 4). If P has XY-coordinates (8, 10), what are its xy-coordinates?
mcqs.why: For inverse translation: x = X+h, y = Y+k. So x = 8+3 = 11 and y = 10+4 = 14, giving P = (11, 14) in xy-coordinates.

mcqs.q: Axes are translated through O'(-2, -6). If P has XY-coordinates (-5, -3), what are its xy-coordinates?
mcqs.why: x = X+h = -5+(-2) = -7. y = Y+k = -3+(-6) = -9. So P = (-7, -9) in the original xy-coordinate system.

mcqs.q: Axes are translated through O'(-2, 3). If P has XY-coordinates (4, -3), what are its xy-coordinates?
mcqs.why: x = X+h = 4+(-2) = 2. y = Y+k = -3+3 = 0. So the xy-coordinates are P = (2, 0), as given in the notes.

mcqs.q: Axes are rotated through 45 degrees. What are the XY-coordinates of P(5, 3)?
mcqs.why: X = x cos45 + y sin45 = (5+3)(sqrt(2)/2) = 8 sqrt(2)/2 = 4 sqrt(2). Y = y cos45 - x sin45 = (3-5)(sqrt(2)/2) = -2 sqrt(2)/2 = -sqrt(2). So (4 sqrt(2), -sqrt(2)).

mcqs.q: Axes are rotated through 30 degrees. What are the XY-coordinates of P(3, -7)?
Axes are rotated through 45 degrees. If P has XY-coordinates (-7 sqrt(2), 5 sqrt(2)), what are its xy-coordinates?
mcqs.why: Inverse rotation: x = X cos45 - Y sin45 = (-7 sqrt(2)-5 sqrt(2))(sqrt(2)/2) = (-12 sqrt(2))(sqrt(2)/2) = -12. y = X sin45 + Y cos45 = (-7 sqrt(2)+5 sqrt(2))(sqrt(2)/2) = -2. So (-12,-2).

mcqs.q: In a translation of axes through O'(h, k), how are the new coordinates X and Y obtained from (x, y)?
options: X = x - h, Y = y - k
X = x + h, Y = y + k
X = x - k, Y = y - h
X = h - x, Y = k - y
mcqs.why: The notes give for translation through O'(h,k): X = x - h and Y = y - k. For example P(3,2) with O'(1,3) gives X=3-1=2, Y=2-3=-1.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.3 — Equations of straight lines
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find the slope and inclination of the line joining the points, and sketch each line

in the plane: (i) (-2, 4); (5, 11) (ii) (3, -2); (2, 7) (iii) (4, 6); (4, 8).

Slope m = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1); inclination alpha satisfies tan alpha = m, with 0 degrees < alpha < 180 degrees.

(i) m = (11 - 4)/(5 + 2) = 7/7 = 1, so alpha = 45 degrees. Sketch: join (-2, 4) to (5, 11).

(ii) m = (7 + 2)/(2 - 3) = 9/(-1) = -9, so alpha = 180 degrees - arctan 9 = approx. 96.3 degrees. Sketch: join (3, -2) to (2, 7).

Answer: (iii) x2 = x1, so the line is vertical: slope undefined, alpha = 90 degrees. Sketch: the vertical line x = 4 through (4, 6) and (4, 8).

Q2. In the triangle A(8, 6), B(-4, 2), C(-2, -6), find the slope of (i) each side of the triangle (ii) each median of the triangle (iii) each altitude of the triangle.

(i) Sides: AB: (2 - 6)/(-4 - 8) = 1/3; BC: (-6 - 2)/(-2 + 4) = -4; CA: (6 + 6)/(8 + 2) = 6/5.

(ii) Midpoints: BC (-3, -2), CA (3, 0), AB (2, 4). Medians: from A: (-2 - 6)/(-3 - 8) = 8/11; from B: (0 - 2)/(3 + 4) = -2/7; from C: (4 + 6)/(2 + 2) = 5/2.

Answer: (iii) Altitudes are perpendicular to the sides, so their slopes are the negative reciprocals: from A (perpendicular to BC): 1/4; from B (perpendicular to CA): -5/6; from C (perpendicular to AB): -3.

Q3. By means of slopes, show that the following points lie on the same line: (a) (-1, -3); (1, 5); (2, 9) (b) (4, -5); (7, 5); (10, 15) (c) (-4, 6); (3, 8); (10, 10) (d) (a, 2b); (c, a

+ b); (2c - a, 2a).

Three points are collinear when the slope of the first pair equals the slope of the second pair.

(a) Slopes: (5 + 3)/(1 + 1) = 4 and (9 - 5)/(2 - 1) = 4, equal, so collinear.

(b) Slopes: (5 + 5)/(7 - 4) = 10/3 and (15 - 5)/(10 - 7) = 10/3, equal, so collinear.

(c) Slopes: (8 - 6)/(3 + 4) = 2/7 and (10 - 8)/(10 - 3) = 2/7, equal, so collinear.

Answer: (d) Slopes: (a + b - 2b)/(c - a) = (a - b)/(c - a) and (2a - (a + b))/(2c - a - c) = (a - b)/(c - a), equal, so collinear.

Q4. Find k so that the line joining A(7, 3); B(k, -6) and the line joining C(-4, 5); D(-6, 4) are (i) parallel (ii) perpendicular.

Slope of AB = (-6 - 3)/(k - 7) = -9/(k - 7); slope of CD = (4 - 5)/(-6 + 4) = 1/2.

(i) Parallel: slopes equal, so -9/(k - 7) = 1/2, giving k - 7 = -18.

Answer: (i) k = -11. (ii) Perpendicular: product of slopes = -1, so -9/(k - 7) = -2, giving k - 7 = 9/2, so k = 23/2.

Q5. Using slopes, show that the triangle with vertices A(6, 1), B(2, 7) and C(-6, -7) is a right triangle.

Slopes: AB = (7 - 1)/(2 - 6) = -3/2; BC = (-7 - 7)/(-6 - 2) = 7/4; CA = (1 + 7)/(6 + 6) = 2/3.

The product of the slopes of AB and AC is (-3/2)(2/3) = -1, so AB is perpendicular to AC.

Answer: the triangle is right-angled at A, hence a right triangle.

Q6. The three points A(7, -1), B(-2, 2) and C(1, 4) are consecutive vertices of a parallelogram.

Find the fourth vertex. In a parallelogram the diagonals bisect each other, so the fourth vertex D satisfies D = A + C - B.

D = (7 + 1 - (-2), -1 + 4 - 2) = (10, 1).

Answer: the fourth vertex is (10, 1).

Q7. The points A(-1, 2), B(3, -1) and C(6, 3) are consecutive vertices of a rhombus.

Find the fourth vertex and show that the diagonals of the rhombus are perpendicular to each other. Fourth vertex D = A + C - B = (-1 + 6 - 3, 2 + 3 + 1) = (2, 6).

Diagonal AC has direction (7, 1); diagonal BD has direction D - B = (-1, 7).

Their dot product is 7(-1) + 1(7) = 0, so the diagonals are perpendicular.

Answer: fourth vertex (2, 6); diagonals AC and BD are perpendicular.

Q8. Two pairs of points are given.

Find whether the two lines determined by these points are (i) parallel (ii) perpendicular (iii) none: (a) (1, -2), (2, 4) and (4, 1), (-8, 2)

(b) (-3, 4), (6, 2) and (4, 5), (-2, -7).

(a) Slopes: (4 + 2)/(2 - 1) = 6 and (2 - 1)/(-8 - 4) = -1/12; product = -1/2, and the slopes are not equal.

Answer: (a) none. (b) Slopes: (2 - 4)/(6 + 3) = -2/9 and (-7 - 5)/(-2 - 4) = 2; product = -4/9, and the slopes are not equal, so (b) none.

Q9. Find an equation of (a) the horizontal line through (7, -9) (b) the vertical line through (-5, 3) (c) the line bisecting the first and third quadrants (d) the line bisecting the second and fourth quadrants.

(a) A horizontal line has equation y = constant: y = -9.

(b) A vertical line has equation x = constant: x = -5.

(c) The bisector of the first and third quadrants is the line y = x.

Answer: (d) The bisector of the second and fourth quadrants is the line y = -x.

Q10. Find an equation of the line (a) through A(-6, 5) having slope 7 (b) through (8, -3) having slope 0 (c) through (-8, 5) having slope undefined (d) through (-5, -3) and (9, -1) (e) y-intercept -7 and slope -5 (f) x-intercept -3 and y-intercept 4 (g) x-intercept -9 and slope -4.

(a) Point-slope: y - 5 = 7(x + 6), i.e. 7x - y + 47 = 0.

(b) Slope 0: y = -3. (c) Slope undefined: x = -8.

(d) Slope = (-1 + 3)/(9 + 5) = 1/7, so y + 3 = (1/7)(x + 5), i.e. x - 7y - 16 = 0.

(e) Slope-intercept: y = -5x - 7. (f) Two-intercept: x/(-3) + y/4 = 1, i.e. 4x - 3y + 12 = 0.

Answer: (g) y = -4(x + 9), i.e. 4x + y + 36 = 0.

Q11. Find an equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining A(3, 5) and B(9, 8).

Midpoint of AB = (6, 13/2); slope of AB = (8 - 5)/(9 - 3) = 1/2, so the perpendicular slope is -2.

Equation: y - 13/2 = -2(x - 6), i.e. y = -2x + 37/2.

Answer: 4x + 2y - 37 = 0.

Q12. Find equations of the sides, altitudes and medians of the triangle whose vertices are A(-3, 2), B(5, 4) and C(3, -8).

Sides: BC: slope 6, y - 4 = 6(x - 5), i.e. 6x - y - 26 = 0; CA: slope -5/3, y + 8 = (-5/3)(x - 3), i.e. 5x + 3y + 9 = 0; AB: slope 1/4, y - 2 = (1/4)(x + 3), i.e. x - 4y + 11 = 0.

Altitudes: from A (perpendicular to BC, slope -1/6): y - 2 = (-1/6)(x + 3), i.e. x + 6y 9 = 0; from B (perpendicular to CA, slope 3/5): y - 4 = (3/5)(x - 5), i.e. 3x - 5y + 5 = 0; from C (perpendicular to AB, slope -4): y + 8 = -4(x - 3), i.e. 4x + y - 4 = 0.

Midpoints: BC (4, -2), CA (0, -3), AB (1, 3). Medians: from A: y - 2 = (-4/7)(x + 3), i.e. 4x + 7y - 2 = 0; from B: y - 4 = (7/5)(x - 5), i.e. 7x - 5y - 15 = 0.

Answer: median from C: y + 8 = (-11/2)(x - 3), i.e. 11x + 2y - 17 = 0.

Q13. Find an equation of the line through (-4, -6) and perpendicular to a line having slope -3/2.

The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal of -3/2, i.e. 2/3.

Equation: y + 6 = (2/3)(x + 4).

Answer: 2x - 3y - 10 = 0.

Q14. Find an equation of the line through (11, -5) and parallel to a line with slope -24.

A parallel line has the same slope, -24.

Equation: y + 5 = -24(x - 11), i.e. y = -24x + 259.

Answer: 24x + y - 259 = 0.

Q15. The points A(-1, 2), B(6, 3) and C(2, -4) are vertices of a triangle.

Show that the line joining the midpoint D of AB and the midpoint E of AC is parallel to BC and DE = (1/2) BC. D = midpoint of AB = (5/2, 5/2); E = midpoint of AC = (1/2, -1).

Slope of DE = (-1 - 5/2)/(1/2 - 5/2) = (-7/2)/(-2) = 7/4; slope of BC = (-4 - 3)/(2 - 6) = 7/4, so DE is parallel to BC.

DE = sqrt[(2)2 + (7/2)2] = sqrt(65)/2; BC = sqrt[(4)2 + (7)2] = sqrt(65).

Answer: DE is parallel to BC and DE = (1/2) BC, as required.

Q16. A milkman can sell 560 litres of milk at Rs.

12.50 per litre and 700 litres of milk at Rs. 12.00 per litre. Assuming the graph of the sale price and the milk sold to be a straight line, find the number of litres of milk that the milkman can sell at Rs. 12.25 per litre. Take price as x and litres sold as y: the points are (12.50, 560) and (12.00, 700).

Slope = (700 - 560)/(12.00 - 12.50) = 140/(-0.50) = -280 litres per rupee.

At price 12.25, the change from 12.50 is -0.25, so litres = 560 + (-280)(-0.25) = 560 + 70.

Answer: 630 litres.

Q17. The population of Pakistan to the nearest million was 60 million in 1961 and 95 million in 1981.

Using t as the number of years after 1961, find an equation of the line that gives the population in terms of t. Use this equation to find the population in (a) 1947 (b) 1997. Points (t, P): (0, 60) and (20, 95), in millions; slope = (95 - 60)/20 = 7/4.

Equation: P = 60 + (7/4) t million.

(a) 1947 gives t = -14: P = 60 - (7/4)(14) = 60 - 24.5 = 35.5 million.

Answer: (b) 1997 gives t = 36: P = 60 + (7/4)(36) = 60 + 63 = 123 million.

Q18. A house was purchased for Rs.

1 million in 1980. It is worth Rs. 4 million in 1996. Assuming that the value increased by the same amount each year, find an equation that gives the value of the house after t years of the date of purchase. What was its value in 1990?

Points (t, V): (0, 1) and (16, 4), in millions of rupees; slope = (4 - 1)/16 = 3/16.

Equation: V = 1 + (3/16) t million rupees.

In 1990, t = 10: V = 1 + 30/16 = 1 + 1.875 = 2.875 million.

Answer: V = 1 + (3/16) t million rupees; value in 1990 = Rs. 2,875,000.

Q19. Plot the Celsius (C) and Fahrenheit (F) temperature scales on the horizontal axis and the vertical axis respectively.

Draw the line joining the freezing point and the boiling point of water. Find an equation giving F temperature in terms of C. Freezing point: (C, F) = (0, 32); boiling point: (100, 212).

Slope = (212 - 32)/(100 - 0) = 180/100 = 9/5.

With F-intercept 32, the equation is F = 32 + (9/5) C.

Answer: F = (9/5) C + 32.

Q20. The average entry test score of engineering candidates was 592 in the year 1998 while the score was 564 in 2002.

Assuming that the relationship between time and score is linear, find the average score for 2006. Points (year, score): (1998, 592) and (2002, 564); slope = (564 - 592)/4 = -7 per

year.

Let t be years after 1998: score S = 592 - 7t.

For 2006, t = 8: S = 592 - 56.

Answer: average score 536.

Q21. Convert each of the following equations into (i) slope-intercept form (ii) two-intercept form (iii) normal form: (a) 2x - 4y + 11 = 0 (b) 4x + 7y - 2 = 0 (c) 15y - 8x + 13 = 0.

Also find the length of the perpendicular from (0, 0) to each line. (a) Slope-intercept: y = (1/2) x + 11/4. Two-intercept: x/(-11/2) + y/(11/4) = 1. Normal: (-x + 2y)/sqrt(5) = 11/(2 sqrt(5)). Perpendicular from origin: |11|/sqrt(20) = 11 sqrt(5)/10.

(b) Slope-intercept: y = (-4/7) x + 2/7. Two-intercept: x/(1/2) + y/(2/7) = 1. Normal: (4x + 7y)/sqrt(65) = 2/sqrt(65). Perpendicular from origin: 2/sqrt(65).

Answer: (c) Slope-intercept: y = (8/15) x - 13/15. Two-intercept: x/(13/8) + y/(-13/15) = 1. Normal: (8x - 15y)/17 = 13/17. Perpendicular from origin: 13/17.

Q22. In each of the following check whether the two lines are (i) parallel (ii) perpendicular (iii) neither parallel nor perpendicular: (a) 2x + y - 3 = 0; 4x + 2y + 5 = 0 (b) 3y = 2x + 5; 3x + 2y - 8 = 0 (Print note: the operators in the second line of (b) render faintly in this copy; the form 3x + 2y - 8 = 0 is confirmed by the book's text layer.) (c) 4y + 2x - 1 = 0; x - 2y - 7 = 0 (d) 4x - y + 2 = 0; 12x - 3y + 1 = 0 (Print note: the operators in the second line of (d) render faintly in this copy; the form 12x - 3y + 1 = 0 is confirmed by the book's text layer.) (e) 12x + 35y - 7 = 0; 105x - 36y + 11 = 0.

Slopes: (a) -2 and -2, equal, so parallel. (b) 2/3 and -3/2, product -1, so perpendicular.

(c) -1/2 and 1/2, product -1/4, neither equal nor product -1, so neither.

(d) 4 and 4, equal, so parallel. (e) -12/35 and 105/36 = 35/12, product -1, so perpendicular.

Answer: (a) parallel; (b) perpendicular; (c) neither; (d) parallel; (e) perpendicular.

Q23. Find the distance between the given parallel lines.

Sketch the lines. Also find an equation of the parallel line lying midway between them: (a) 3x - 4y + 3 = 0; 3x - 4y + 7 = 0 (b) 12x + 5y - 6 = 0; 12x + 5y + 13 = 0 (c) x + 2y - 5 = 0; 2x + 4y + 1 = 0 (Print note: the operators of the second line of (c) render faintly in this copy; the form 2x + 4y + 1 = 0 is confirmed by the book's text layer.) (a) Distance = |7 - 3|/sqrt(9 + 16) = 4/5; midway line: 3x - 4y + 5 = 0. Sketch: two parallel lines with the midway line between them.

(b) Distance = |13 - (-6)|/sqrt(144 + 25) = 19/13; midway line: 12x + 5y + 7/2 = 0, i.e. 24x + 10y + 7 = 0.

Answer: (c) Second line divided by 2 is x + 2y + 1/2 = 0; distance = |-5 1/2|/sqrt(5) = 11/(2 sqrt(5)) = 11 sqrt(5)/10; midway line: x + 2y - 9/4 = 0, i.e. 4x + 8y - 9 = 0.

Q24. Find an equation of the line through (-4, 7) and parallel to the line 2x - 7y + 4 = 0.

The given line has slope 2/7, so the parallel line has slope 2/7.

Equation: y - 7 = (2/7)(x + 4).

Answer: 2x - 7y + 57 = 0.

Q25. Find an equation of the line through (5, -8) and perpendicular to the join of A(-15, -8), B(10, 7).

Slope of AB = (7 + 8)/(10 + 15) = 15/25 = 3/5, so the perpendicular slope is -5/3.

Equation: y + 8 = (-5/3)(x - 5).

Answer: 5x + 3y - 1 = 0.

Q26. Find equations of two parallel lines perpendicular to 2x - y + 3 = 0 such that the product of the x- and y-intercepts of each is 3.

The given line has slope 2, so the required lines have slope -1/2; write a line as x + 2y + k = 0.

Its intercepts are x = -k and y = -k/2, whose product is k2/2.

Setting k2/2 = 3 gives k2 = 6, so k = sqrt(6) or k = -sqrt(6).

Answer: x + 2y + sqrt(6) = 0 and x + 2y - sqrt(6) = 0.

Q27. One vertex of a parallelogram is (1, 4); the diagonals intersect at (2, 1) and the sides have slopes 1 and -1/7.

Find the other three vertices.

The vertex opposite (1, 4) is the reflection in the diagonal centre (2, 1): (3, -2).

Let an adjacent vertex B lie on the slope-1 line through (1, 4): B = (x, x + 3); the other adjacent vertex is its reflection in (2, 1): (4 - x, -x - 1).

This vertex lies on the slope -1/7 line through (1, 4): -x - 1 - 4 = (-1/7)(4 - x - 1), giving 7x + 35 = 3 - x, so x = -4.

Then B = (-4, -1) and the other adjacent vertex is (8, 3).

Answer: the other vertices are (3, -2), (-4, -1) and (8, 3).

Q28. Find whether the given point lies above or below the given line: (a) (5, 8); 2x 3y + 6 = 0 (b) (-7, 6); 4x + 3y - 9 = 0.

(a) On the line 2x - 3y + 6 = 0, at x = 5, y = (2(5) + 6)/3 = 16/3, which is less than 8, so the point lies above the line.

Answer: (b) On the line 4x + 3y - 9 = 0, at x = -7, y = (9 - 4(-7))/3 = 37/3, which is greater than 6, so the point lies below the line.

Q29. Check whether the given points are on the same or opposite sides of the given line: (a) (0, 0) and (-4, 7); 6x - 7y + 70 = 0 (b) (2, 3) and (-2, 3); 3x - 5y + 8 = 0.

(a) Values of 6x - 7y + 70: at (0, 0) it is 70 (positive); at (-4, 7) it is -24 - 49 + 70 = -3 (negative); opposite signs mean opposite sides.

Answer: (b) Values of 3x - 5y + 8: at (2, 3) it is 6 - 15 + 8 = -1 (negative); at (-2, 3) it is -6 - 15 + 8 = -13 (negative); same sign means the same side.

Q30. Find the distance from the point P(6, -1) to the line 6x - 4y + 9 = 0.

Distance = |6(6) - 4(-1) + 9|/sqrt(36 + 16) = |36 + 4 + 9|/sqrt(52).

That is 49/(2 sqrt(13)) = 49 sqrt(13)/26.

Answer: 49 sqrt(13)/26 units.

Q31. Find the area of the triangular region whose vertices are A(5, 3), B(-2, 2), C(4, 2).

BC is horizontal (y = 2) with length 4 - (-2) = 6; the height from A to BC is 3 - 2 = 1.

Area = (1/2) x base x height = (1/2)(6)(1).

Answer: 3 square units.

Q32. The coordinates of three points are A(2, 3), B(-1, 1) and C(4, -5).

By computing the area bounded by ABC check whether the points are collinear. Area = (1/2)|2(1 + 5) + (-1)(-5 - 3) + 4(3 - 1)| = (1/2)|12 + 8 + 8| = 14.

The area is not zero, so the points do not lie on one line.

Answer: the points are not collinear.

mcqs.q: What are the slope and inclination of the line joining (-2, 4) and (5, 11)?
mcqs.why: Slope m = (y2-y1)/(x2-x1) = (11-4)/(5-(-2)) = 7/7 = 1. Inclination alpha has tan alpha = m = 1, so alpha = 45 degrees.

mcqs.q: What are the slope and inclination of the line joining (4, 6) and (4, 8)?
mcqs.why: Here x2 = x1 = 4, so the denominator x2-x1 = 0 and the line is vertical. The notes state slope is undefined and inclination alpha = 90 degrees for this line x = 4.

mcqs.q: In triangle A(8, 6), B(-4, 2), C(-2, -6), what is the slope of the median from A?
Find k so that the line joining A(7, 3), B(k, -6) is parallel to the line joining C(-4, 5), D(-6, 4).
Using slopes, the triangle A(6, 1), B(2, 7), C(-6, -7) is right-angled at which vertex?
mcqs.why: Slope AB = (7-1)/(2-6)=6/(-4)=-3/2. Slope AC = (1+7)/(6+6)=8/12=2/3. Product (-3/2)(2/3) = -1, so AB is perpendicular to AC, hence right-angled at A.

mcqs.q: A(-1, 2), B(3, -1) and C(6, 3) are consecutive vertices of a rhombus. What is the fourth vertex?
mcqs.why: Fourth vertex D = A + C - B = (-1+6-3, 2+3-(-1)) = (2, 6). Check: this is the point given in the notes, and diagonals AC and BD are then perpendicular.

mcqs.q: What is an equation of the line with y-intercept -7 and slope -5?
mcqs.why: Slope-intercept form is y = mx + c with m = -5 and c = -7. Substituting gives y = -5x - 7, exactly as in the notes for this case.

mcqs.q: What is an equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining A(3, 5) and B(9, 8)?
mcqs.why: Midpoint = ((3+9)/2, (5+8)/2) = (6, 13/2). Slope AB = (8-5)/(9-3)=3/6=1/2, so perpendicular slope = -2. Equation y-13/2 = -2(x-6) gives 4x+2y-37=0.

mcqs.q: What is the distance from P(6, -1) to the line 6x - 4y + 9 = 0?
A milkman sells 560 litres at Rs. 12.50 per litre and 700 litres at Rs. 12.00 per litre. Assuming a straight-line relation, how many litres can he sell at Rs. 12.25 per litre?

lessons.title: Exercise 4.4 — Angle between lines, concurrency and centres of a triangle
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find the point of intersection of the lines (Print note: the operators of the second line of each pair render blank in this copy; the forms below are recovered from the book's text layer and cross-checked against the legible first lines.): (i) x - 2y + 1 = 0 and 2x - y + 2 = 0 (ii) 3x + y + 12 = 0 and x + 2y - 1 = 0 (iii) x + 4y - 12 = 0 and x - 3y + 3 = 0.

(i) From the first line x = 2y - 1; putting this in the second: 2(2y - 1) - y + 2 = 0, so 3y = 0 and y = 0, x = -1.

(ii) From the second line x = 1 - 2y; putting this in the first: 3(1 - 2y) + y + 12 = 0, so -5y + 15 = 0, y = 3, x = -5.

Answer: (i) (-1, 0); (ii) (-5, 3); (iii) subtracting the two lines gives 7y - 15 = 0, so y = 15/7 and x = 3y - 3 = 24/7, i.e. (24/7, 15/7).

Q2. Find an equation of the line through (Print note: the operators of the second lines render blank in this copy; the forms below are recovered from the book's text layer.): (i) the point (2, -9) and the intersection of the lines 2x + 5y - 8 = 0 and 3x 4y - 6 = 0 (ii) the intersection of the lines x - y - 4 = 0 and 7x + y + 20 = 0 and (a) parallel (b) perpendicular to the line 6x + y - 14 = 0 (iii) the intersection of the lines x + 2y + 3 = 0, 3x + 4y + 7 = 0 and making equal intercepts on the axes.

(i) Intersection: 6x + 15y = 24 and 6x - 8y = 12 give 23y = 12, so the point is (62/23, 12/23).

Slope from (2, -9) to (62/23, 12/23) is (12/23 + 9)/(62/23 - 2) = 219/16, so the line is y + 9 = (219/16)(x - 2), i.e. 219x - 16y - 582 = 0.

(ii) Intersection: adding the lines gives 8x + 16 = 0, so the point is (-2, -6). (a) Parallel to 6x + y - 14 = 0 (slope -6): y + 6 = -6(x + 2), i.e. 6x + y + 18 = 0. (b) Perpendicular (slope 1/6): y + 6 = (1/6)(x + 2), i.e. x - 6y - 34 = 0.

Answer: (iii) Intersection: doubling the first line and subtracting from the second gives x = -1, y = -1. A line with equal intercepts a has equation x + y = a; through (-1, -1) this gives a = -2, i.e. x + y + 2 = 0.

Q3. Find an equation of the line through the intersection of 16x - 10y - 33 = 0; 12x 14y - 29 = 0 and the intersection of x - y + 4 = 0; x - 7y + 2 = 0.

First intersection: 7 times the first line minus 5 times the second gives 52x = 86, so x = 43/26; then 10y = 16x - 33 = -170/26, so y = -17/26.

Second intersection: subtracting the lines gives 6y + 2 = 0, so y = -1/3 and x = y 4 = -13/3.

Slope between the points: (-1/3 + 17/26)/(-13/3 - 43/26) = (25/78)/(-467/78) = -25/467.

Equation through (-13/3, -1/3): y + 1/3 = (-25/467)(x + 13/3).

Answer: 25x + 467y + 264 = 0.

Q4. Find the condition that the lines y = m1 x + c1; y = m2 x + c2 and y = m3 x + c3 are concurrent.

Write the lines as m1 x - y + c1 = 0, m2 x - y + c2 = 0, m3 x - y + c3 = 0.

Three lines are concurrent exactly when the determinant of their coefficients is zero.

Expanding the determinant gives m1(c2 - c3) + m2(c3 - c1) + m3(c1 - c2) = 0.

Answer: the required condition is m1(c2 - c3) + m2(c3 - c1) + m3(c1 - c2) = 0.

Q5. FLAGGED - Determine the value of p such that the lines 2x - 3y - 1 = 0, 3x - y 5 = 0 and 3x + 4y + 8 = 0 meet at a point.

(Print note: as printed in this copy, no line contains p, and the three lines are not concurrent, so no value of p can be determined from the printed question; no value is invented here.) Intersection of the first two lines: from 3x - y - 5 = 0, y = 3x - 5; putting this in 2x 3y - 1 = 0 gives 2x - 9x + 15 - 1 = 0, so x = 2 and y = 1.

Check the third line at (2, 1): 3(2) + 4(1) + 8 = 18, not 0, so the third line does not pass through the intersection of the first two.

Answer: FLAGGED - the question as printed has no determinable value of p; the three printed lines do not meet at a point.

Q6. Show that the lines 4x - 3y - 8 = 0, 3x - 4y - 6 = 0 and x - y - 2 = 0 are concurrent and the third line bisects the angle formed by the first two lines.

Intersection of the first two: 4 times the first minus 3 times the second gives 7x = 14, so x = 2 and y = 0; the third line gives 2 - 0 - 2 = 0, so all three pass through (2, 0) and are concurrent.

Angle bisectors of the first two lines: (4x - 3y - 8)/5 + (3x - 4y - 6)/5 = 0 gives (7x 7y - 14)/5 = 0, i.e. x - y - 2 = 0.

Answer: the third line is one of the angle bisectors of the first two lines, as required.

Q7. The vertices of a triangle are A(-2, 3), B(-4, 1) and C(3, 5).

Find coordinates of the (i) centroid (ii) orthocentre (iii) circumcentre of the triangle. Are these three points collinear? (i) Centroid = ((-2 - 4 + 3)/3, (3 + 1 + 5)/3) = (-1, 3).

(ii) Altitude from A (perpendicular to BC, slope 4/7): 7x + 4y + 2 = 0. Altitude from B (perpendicular to AC, slope 2/5): 5x + 2y + 18 = 0. Solving gives x = -34/3, y = 58/3; this also satisfies the third altitude x + y - 8 = 0.

(iii) Perpendicular bisector of AB: x + y + 1 = 0. Perpendicular bisector of AC: 5x + 2y - 21/2 = 0. Solving gives x = 25/6, y = -31/6; this point is equidistant from A, B and C.

Answer: centroid (-1, 3), orthocentre (-34/3, 58/3), circumcentre (25/6, -31/6). Slope from orthocentre to centroid is -49/31, and slope from centroid to circumcentre is also -49/31, so the three points are collinear (the Euler line).

Q8. Check whether the lines 4x - 3y - 8 = 0; 3x - 4y - 6 = 0; x - y - 2 = 0 are concurrent.

If so, find the point where they meet. Intersection of the first two lines: 4 times the first minus 3 times the second gives 7x = 14, so x = 2; then 8 - 3y - 8 = 0 gives y = 0.

Check the third line at (2, 0): 2 - 0 - 2 = 0, satisfied.

Answer: yes, concurrent at (2, 0).

Q9. Find the coordinates of the vertices of the triangle formed by the lines x - 2y - 6 = 0; 3x - y + 3 = 0; 2x + y - 4 = 0.

Also find measures of the angles of the triangle. Vertices: first and second lines meet where x - 2y = 6 and 3x - y = -3, giving (-12/5, -21/5). Second and third meet where 3x - y = -3 and 2x + y = 4, giving (1/5, 18/5). First and third meet where x - 2y = 6 and 2x + y = 4, giving (14/5, -8/5).

Slopes: first line 1/2, second line 3, third line -2. Angle between first and second: tan = (3 - 1/2)/(1 + 3/2) = 1, so 45 degrees. Angle between second and third: tan = (-2 - 3)/(1 - 6) = 1, so 45 degrees.

Answer: vertices (-12/5, -21/5), (1/5, 18/5), (14/5, -8/5); angles 45 degrees, 45 degrees and 90 degrees (the third angle, between slopes -2 and 1/2, has denominator 1 + (-2)(1/2) = 0).

Q10. Find the angle measured from the line l1 to the line l2 where (a) l1 joining (2, 7) and (7, 10); l2 joining (1, 1) and (-5, 3) (b) l1 joining (3, -1) and (5, 7); l2 joining (2, 4) and (-8, 2) (c) l1 joining (1, -7) and (6, -4); l2 joining (-1, 2) and (-6, -1) (d) l1 joining (-9, -1) and (3, -5); l2 joining (2, 7) and (-6, -7).

Also find the acute angle in each case. Use tan theta = (m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2). (a) m1 = 3/5, m2 = -1/3: tan theta = -7/6, so theta = 180 degrees - 49.4 degrees = 130.6 degrees; acute angle 49.4 degrees.

(b) m1 = 4, m2 = 1/5: tan theta = -19/9, so theta = 180 degrees - 64.7 degrees = 115.3 degrees; acute angle 64.7 degrees.

(c) m1 = 3/5, m2 = 3/5: the slopes are equal, so the lines are parallel; angle 0 degrees, acute angle 0 degrees.

Answer: (d) m1 = -1/3, m2 = 7/4: tan theta = 5, so theta = 78.7 degrees, already acute.

Q11. Find the interior angles of the triangle whose vertices are (a) A(-2, 11), B(-6, -3), C(4, -9) (b) A(6, 1), B(2, 7), C(-6, -7) (c) A(2, -5), B(-4, -3), C(-1, 5) (d) A(2, 8), B(-5, 4), C(4, -9).

Use cos of the angle between the two side vectors at each vertex. (a) At A: cos = 64/sqrt(5777), angle approx. 32.6 degrees; at B: cos = -44/sqrt(28832), angle 105.0 degrees; at C: angle approx. 42.3 degrees.

(b) At A the side slopes are -3/2 and 2/3, whose product is -1, so angle A = 90 degrees; at B: cos approx. 0.447, angle 63.4 degrees; at C: angle 26.6 degrees.

(c) Angles: at A approx. 54.9 degrees; at B approx. 87.9 degrees; at C approx. 37.3 degrees.

Answer: (d) Angles: at A approx. 67.0 degrees; at B approx. 85.0 degrees; at C approx. 28.0 degrees. Each set sums to 180 degrees.

Q12. Find the interior angles of the quadrilateral whose vertices are A(5, 2), B(-2, 3), C(-3, -4) and D(4, -5).

At A, vectors AB = (-7, 1) and AD = (-1, -7) have dot product 7 - 7 = 0, so angle A = 90 degrees.

At B, vectors BA = (7, -1) and BC = (-1, -7) have dot product -7 + 7 = 0, so angle B = 90 degrees.

At C, vectors CB = (1, 7) and CD = (7, -1) have dot product 7 - 7 = 0, so angle C = 90 degrees; similarly angle D = 90 degrees.

Answer: all interior angles are 90 degrees; in fact all sides equal sqrt(50), so the quadrilateral is a square.

Q13. Show that the points A(0, 0), B(2, 1), C(3, 3), D(1, 2) are the vertices of a rhombus.

Find its interior angles. Side lengths: AB = sqrt(5), BC = sqrt(5), CD = sqrt(5), DA = sqrt(5); all sides equal, so ABCD is a rhombus.

At A, vectors AB = (2, 1) and AD = (1, 2) give cos A = 4/5, so angle A = approx. 36.9 degrees.

At B, vectors BA = (-2, -1) and BC = (1, 2) give cos B = -4/5, so angle B = approx. 143.1 degrees.

Answer: interior angles 36.9 degrees, 143.1 degrees, 36.9 degrees, 143.1 degrees.

Q14. Find the area of the region bounded by the triangle whose sides are 7x - y - 10 = 0; 10x + y - 14 = 0; 3x + 2y + 3 = 0.

Vertices: first and second lines meet at (24/17, 2/17); second and third at (31/17, -72/17); first and third at (1, -3).

Area = (1/2)|24/17(-72/17 + 3) + 31/17(-3 - 2/17) + 1(2/17 + 72/17)| = (1/2)(889/289).

Answer: 889/578 square units (approx. 1.54).

Q15. The vertices of a triangle are A(-2, 3), B(-4, 1) and C(3, 5).

Find the centre of the circumcircle of the triangle. This is the triangle of Q7. Its perpendicular bisector of AB is x + y + 1 = 0 and of AC is 5x + 2y - 21/2 = 0.

Solving gives x = 25/6 and y = -31/6.

Answer: circumcentre (25/6, -31/6).

Q16. Express the given system of equations in matrix form.

Find in each case whether the lines are concurrent: (a) x + 3y - 2 = 0; 2x - y + 4 = 0; x - 11y + 14 = 0 (b) 2x + 3y + 4 = 0; x - 2y - 3 = 0; 3x + y - 8 = 0 (c) 3x - 4y - 2 = 0; x + 2y - 4 = 0; 3x - 2y + 5 = 0. Concurrency holds exactly when the determinant of the coefficient matrix (columns x, y, constant) is zero.

(a) Matrix [[1, 3, -2], [2, -1, 4], [1, -11, 14]] times [x, y, 1] = 0; determinant = 30 72 + 42 = 0, so concurrent.

(b) Matrix [[2, 3, 4], [1, -2, -3], [3, 1, -8]]; determinant = 38 - 3 + 28 = 63, not zero, so not concurrent.

Answer: (c) Matrix [[3, -4, -2], [1, 2, -4], [3, -2, 5]]; determinant = 6 + 68 + 16 = 90, not zero, so not concurrent.

Q17. Find a system of linear equations corresponding to the given matrix form.

Check whether the lines represented by the system are concurrent: (a) [[1, 0, -1], [2, 0, 1], [0, -1, 6]] [x, y, 1] = 0 (b) [[1, 1, 2], [2, 4, -3], [3, 6, -5]] [x, y, 1] = 0.

(a) Equations: x - 1 = 0; 2x + 1 = 0; -y + 6 = 0. The first two give x = 1 and x = -1/2, which cannot both hold, so the lines are not concurrent (determinant -1, not zero).

Answer: (b) Equations: x + y + 2 = 0; 2x + 4y - 3 = 0; 3x + 6y - 5 = 0. The last two are parallel (2x + 4y = 3 and 3x + 6y = 5), so the lines are not concurrent (determinant -1, not zero).

mcqs.q: What is the point of intersection of x - 2y + 1 = 0 and 2x - y + 2 = 0?
mcqs.why: From first line x = 2y-1. Put in second: 2(2y-1)-y+2=0 gives 4y-2-y+2=0, so 3y=0, y=0, and x=2(0)-1=-1. Intersection is (-1, 0).

mcqs.q: What is the point of intersection of 3x + y + 12 = 0 and x + 2y - 1 = 0?
mcqs.why: From second line x = 1-2y. Put in first: 3(1-2y)+y+12=0 gives 3-6y+y+12=0, so -5y+15=0, y=3, and x=1-2(3)=-5. Intersection is (-5, 3).

mcqs.q: For triangle A(-2, 3), B(-4, 1), C(3, 5), what is the centroid?
For triangle A(-2, 3), B(-4, 1), C(3, 5), what is the circumcentre?
mcqs.why: Perpendicular bisector of AB is x+y+1=0 and of AC is 5x+2y-21/2=0. Solving these two equations together gives x=25/6 and y=-31/6, the circumcentre equidistant from A, B and C.

mcqs.q: For triangle A(-2, 3), B(-4, 1), C(3, 5), what is the orthocentre?
mcqs.why: Altitude from A is 7x+4y+2=0 and altitude from B is 5x+2y+18=0. Solving: from the system, x=-34/3 and y=58/3, which also satisfies the third altitude x+y-8=0.

mcqs.q: The lines 4x - 3y - 8 = 0, 3x - 4y - 6 = 0 and x - y - 2 = 0 are concurrent at which point?
mcqs.why: First two: 4 times first minus 3 times second gives 7x=14, so x=2, then 8-3y-8=0 gives y=0. Check third at (2,0): 2-0-2=0, satisfied. So concurrent at (2, 0).

mcqs.q: The lines x - 2y - 6 = 0, 3x - y + 3 = 0 and 2x + y - 4 = 0 form a triangle. Which point is the vertex where the second and third lines meet?
mcqs.why: Solve 3x-y=-3 and 2x+y=4. Adding: 5x=1, so x=1/5. Then y=4-2x=4-2/5=18/5. So the second and third lines meet at (1/5, 18/5).

mcqs.q: l1 joins (2, 7) to (7, 10) and l2 joins (1, 1) to (-5, 3). What is the acute angle between them?
In triangle A(6, 1), B(2, 7), C(-6, -7), what is the interior angle at A?
mcqs.why: Slopes at A: AB slope = (7-1)/(2-6)=-3/2 and AC slope = (1+7)/(6+6)=2/3. Product (-3/2)(2/3)=-1, so the sides at A are perpendicular and angle A = 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the area of the region bounded by 7x - y - 10 = 0, 10x + y - 14 = 0 and 3x + 2y + 3 = 0?

lessons.title: Exercise 4.5 — Homogeneous equation of the second degree (pair of lines through the origin)
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find the lines represented by 10x2 - 23xy - 5y2 = 0 and also find the measure of the angle between them.

(Problems 1-6.) Factor: 10x2 - 23xy - 5y2 = (5x + y)(2x - 5y) = 0.

Lines: 5x + y = 0 (slope -5) and 2x - 5y = 0 (slope 2/5).

Angle: with a = 10, h = -23/2, b = -5: tan theta = 2 sqrt(h2 - ab)/(a + b) = 27/5, so the acute angle is arctan(27/5) = approx. 79.5 degrees.

Answer: lines y = -5x and y = (2/5)x; acute angle approx. 79.5 degrees.

Q2. Find the lines represented by 3x2 + 7xy + 2y2 = 0 and also find the measure of the angle between them.

Factor: 3x2 + 7xy + 2y2 = (3x + y)(x + 2y) = 0.

Lines: 3x + y = 0 and x + 2y = 0.

Angle: with a = 3, h = 7/2, b = 2: tan theta = 2 sqrt(h2 - ab)/(a + b) = 5/5 = 1.

Answer: lines y = -3x and y = -x/2; angle 45 degrees.

Q3. Find the lines represented by 9x2 + 24xy + 16y2 = 0 and also find the measure of the angle between them.

Factor: 9x2 + 24xy + 16y2 = (3x + 4y)2 = 0.

The two lines coincide: 3x + 4y = 0 (a double line).

Answer: coincident lines 3x + 4y = 0; angle between them 0 degrees.

Q4. Find the lines represented by 2x2 + 3xy - 5y2 = 0 and also find the measure of the angle between them.

Factor: 2x2 + 3xy - 5y2 = (2x + 5y)(x - y) = 0.

Lines: 2x + 5y = 0 (slope -2/5) and x - y = 0 (slope 1).

Angle: with a = 2, h = 3/2, b = -5: tan theta = 2 sqrt(h2 - ab)/(a + b) = 7/(-3), so the acute angle is arctan(7/3) = approx. 66.8 degrees.

Answer: lines y = -(2/5)x and y = x; acute angle approx. 66.8 degrees.

Q5. Find the lines represented by 6x2 - 19xy + 15y2 = 0 and also find the measure of the angle between them.

Factor: 6x2 - 19xy + 15y2 = (3x - 5y)(2x - 3y) = 0.

Lines: 3x - 5y = 0 (slope 3/5) and 2x - 3y = 0 (slope 2/3).

Angle: with a = 6, h = -19/2, b = 15: tan theta = 2 sqrt(h2 - ab)/(a + b) = 1/21.

Answer: lines y = (3/5)x and y = (2/3)x; angle approx. 2.7 degrees.

Q6. Find the lines represented by x2 + 2xy sec(alpha) + y2 = 0 and also find the measure of the angle between them.

Here a = 1, h = sec(alpha), b = 1. Dividing by y2 and solving for x/y gives x/y = -sec(alpha) + tan(alpha) or x/y = -sec(alpha) - tan(alpha).

Lines: x = (-sec(alpha) + tan(alpha)) y and x = (-sec(alpha) - tan(alpha)) y.

Angle: tan theta = 2 sqrt(h2 - ab)/(a + b) = 2 tan(alpha)/2 = tan(alpha).

Answer: angle theta = alpha (for alpha acute).

Q7. Find a joint equation of the lines through the origin and perpendicular to the lines: x2 - 2xy tan(alpha) - y2 = 0.

For the given pair, the slopes satisfy -m2 - 2 tan(alpha) m + 1 = 0, so the product of the slopes is -1: the two given lines are already perpendicular to each other.

Hence the lines through the origin perpendicular to them are the same pair of lines.

Answer: the joint equation is unchanged: x2 - 2xy tan(alpha) - y2 = 0.

Q8. Find a joint equation of the lines through the origin and perpendicular to the lines: ax2 + 2hxy + by2 = 0.

Let the given lines be y = m1 x and y = m2 x, with m1 + m2 = -2h/b and m1 m2 = a/b.

The perpendiculars through the origin are x + m1 y = 0 and x + m2 y = 0.

Their joint equation is (x + m1 y)(x + m2 y) = x2 + (m1 + m2) xy + m1 m2 y2 = x2 - (2h/b) xy + (a/b) y2 = 0.

Answer: bx2 - 2hxy + ay2 = 0.

Q9. Find the area of the region bounded by: 10x2 - xy - 21y2 = 0 and x + y + 1 = 0.

Factor: 10x2 - xy - 21y2 = (5x + 7y)(2x - 3y) = 0, two lines through the origin.

Intersection with x + y + 1 = 0: with 5x + 7y = 0, the point is (-7/2, 5/2); with 2x 3y = 0, the point is (-3/5, -2/5).

The region is the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (-7/2, 5/2), (-3/5, -2/5).

Area = (1/2)|(-7/2)(-2/5) - (-3/5)(5/2)| = (1/2)(7/5 + 3/2) = 29/20.

Answer: 29/20 square units.

mcqs.q: What are the lines represented by 10x^2 - 23xy - 5y^2 = 0?
mcqs.why: Factorising: 10x^2-23xy-5y^2 = (5x+y)(2x-5y) = 0. Setting each factor to zero gives the two lines 5x+y=0 and 2x-5y=0 through the origin.

mcqs.q: What is the acute angle between the lines represented by 10x^2 - 23xy - 5y^2 = 0?
mcqs.why: a=10, h=-23/2, b=-5. tan theta = 2 sqrt(h^2-ab)/(a+b) = 2 sqrt(529/4+50)/5 = 27/5. So theta = arctan(27/5) = approx. 79.5 degrees.

mcqs.q: What are the lines represented by 3x^2 + 7xy + 2y^2 = 0?
mcqs.why: Factorising: 3x^2+7xy+2y^2 = (3x+y)(x+2y) = 0. So 3x+y=0 gives y=-3x, and x+2y=0 gives 2y=-x, y=-x/2.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the lines represented by 3x^2 + 7xy + 2y^2 = 0?
mcqs.why: a=3, h=7/2, b=2. tan theta = 2 sqrt(h^2-ab)/(a+b) = 2 sqrt(49/4-6)/5 = 2(5/2)/5 = 5/5 = 1. So theta = arctan(1) = 45 degrees.

mcqs.q: What are the lines represented by 9x^2 + 24xy + 16y^2 = 0, and what is the angle between them?
options: Lines y = -3x and y = -x/2, angle 45 degrees
mcqs.why: Factorising: 9x^2+24xy+16y^2 = (3x+4y)^2 = 0, a perfect square. Both factors are the same line 3x+4y=0, so the lines coincide and the angle between them is 0 degrees.

mcqs.q: What are the lines represented by 2x^2 + 3xy - 5y^2 = 0?
mcqs.why: Factorising: 2x^2+3xy-5y^2 = (2x+5y)(x-y) = 0. So 2x+5y=0 gives y=-(2/5)x, and x-y=0 gives y=x.

mcqs.q: What is the angle between the lines represented by 6x^2 - 19xy + 15y^2 = 0?
mcqs.why: a=6, h=-19/2, b=15. tan theta = 2 sqrt(h^2-ab)/(a+b) = 2 sqrt(361/4-90)/21 = 2(1/2)/21 = 1/21. So theta = arctan(1/21) = approx. 2.7 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is a joint equation of the lines through the origin perpendicular to the lines ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0?
mcqs.why: Perpendiculars are x+m1 y=0 and x+m2 y=0 with m1+m2=-2h/b and m1 m2=a/b. Joint equation x^2+(m1+m2)xy+m1 m2 y^2=0 becomes x^2-(2h/b)xy+(a/b)y^2=0, i.e. bx^2-2hxy+ay^2=0.

mcqs.q: What is the area of the region bounded by 10x^2 - xy - 21y^2 = 0 and x + y + 1 = 0?
What is a joint equation of the lines through the origin perpendicular to the lines x^2 - 2xy tan(alpha) - y^2 = 0?
mcqs.why: For the given pair the slopes satisfy -m^2-2 tan(alpha) m+1=0 in product form, giving product of slopes -1, so the two given lines are already perpendicular to each other. Hence the perpendicular pair is the same pair, equation unchanged.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Linear Inequalities and Linear Programming

lessons.title: Exercise 5.1 — Graphs of linear inequalities
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Graph the solution set of each of the following linear inequalities in the xy-plane: (i) 2x + y <= 6 (ii) 3x + 7y >= 21 (iii) 3x - 2y >= 6 (iv) 5x - 4y <= 20 (v) 2x + 1 >= 0 (vi) 3y - 4 <= 0.

Draw the boundary line and test the origin (0, 0); shade the side that satisfies the inequality.

(i) Line 2x + y = 6 through (3, 0) and (0, 6); origin satisfies 0 <= 6, so shade the origin side (below the line).

(ii) Line 3x + 7y = 21 through (7, 0) and (0, 3); origin fails 0 >= 21, so shade the side away from the origin (above the line).

(iii) Line 3x - 2y = 6 through (2, 0) and (0, -3); origin fails 0 >= 6, so shade the side away from the origin.

(iv) Line 5x - 4y = 20 through (4, 0) and (0, -5); origin satisfies 0 <= 20, so shade the origin side.

Answer: (v) 2x + 1 >= 0 gives x >= -1/2: shade the vertical half-plane to the right of the line x = -1/2. (vi) 3y - 4 <= 0 gives y <= 4/3: shade the horizontal half-plane below the line y = 4/3.

Q2. Indicate the solution set of the following systems of linear inequalities by shading: (i) 2x - 3y <= 6; 2x + 3y <= 12 (ii) x + y >= 5; x - y <= 1 (iii) 3x + 7y >= 21; x - y <= 2 (iv) 4x - 3y <= 12 (v) 3x + 7y >= 21; x >= -3/2; y <= 4.

Shade the intersection of the half-planes. (i) The two lines meet at (9/2, 1); both inequalities hold at the origin, so the region is the wedge on the origin side of both lines, with vertex (9/2, 1), unbounded to the left.

(ii) The lines x + y = 5 and x - y = 1 meet at (3, 2); the region is above both lines (y >= 5 - x and y >= x - 1), with vertex (3, 2), unbounded upward.

(iii) The lines meet at (7/2, 3/2); the region is above 3x + 7y = 21 and above x - y = 2 in the sense y >= x - 2, with vertex (7/2, 3/2), unbounded upward.

(iv) A single half-plane: the line 4x - 3y = 12 through (3, 0) and (0, -4); the origin satisfies 0 <= 12, so shade the origin side.

Answer: (v) The region is bounded on the left by x = -3/2 and above by y = 4, and lies above 3x + 7y = 21; its vertices are (-3/2, 51/14) and (-3/2, 4), and it extends unbounded to the right.

Q3. Indicate the solution region of the following systems of linear inequalities by shading: (i) 2x - 3y <= 6; 2x + 3y <= 12; y >= 0 (ii) x + y <= 5; y - 2x <= 2; x >= 0 (iii) x + y >= 5; x - y >= 1; y >= 0 (iv) 3x + 7y <= 21; x - y <= 2; x >= 0 (v) 3x + 7y <= 21; x - y <= 2; y >= 0 (vi) 3x + 7y <= 21; 2x - y >= -3; x >= 0.

(i) Between the lines, above y = 0: vertices (3, 0) and (9/2, 1); the region extends unbounded to the left along y = 0.

(ii) Below both lines, x >= 0: vertices (0, 2) and (1, 4); the region extends unbounded downward.

(iii) Between y = 5 - x (below) and y = x - 1 (above), y >= 0: vertices (3, 2) and (5, 0); the region extends unbounded to the right.

(iv) Triangle with vertices (0, -2), (0, 3) and (7/2, 3/2), bounded.

(v) Vertices (2, 0) and (7/2, 3/2); the region extends unbounded to the left along y = 0.

Answer: (vi) The three lines are concurrent at (0, 3); the region is x >= 0, below both lines, with the single corner (0, 3), extending unbounded downward.

Q4. Graph the solution region of the following system of linear inequalities and find the corner points in each case: (i) 2x - 3y <= 6; 2x + 3y <= 12; x >= 0 (ii) x + y <= 5; -2x + y <= 2; y >= 0 (iii) 3x + 7y <= 21; 2x - y <= -3; y >= 0 (iv) 3x + 2y >= 6; x + 3y <= 6; y >= 0 (v) 5x + 7y <= 35; -x + 3y <= 3; x >= 0 (vi) 5x + 7y <= 35; x - 2y <= 2; x >= 0.

(i) Triangle with corner points (0, -2), (0, 4) and (9/2, 1).

(ii) Triangle with corner points (-1, 0), (5, 0) and (1, 4).

(iii) Corner points (0, 3) and (-3/2, 0); the region is unbounded (the wedge between y = 2x + 3 and 3x + 7y = 21, y >= 0, opening to the left).

(iv) Triangle with corner points (2, 0), (6, 0) and (6/7, 12/7).

(v) Corner points (0, 1) and (42/11, 25/11); the region is unbounded downward (no y >= 0 constraint).

Answer: (vi) Triangle with corner points (0, -1), (0, 5) and (84/17, 25/17).

Q5. Graph the solution region of the following system of linear inequalities by shading: (i) 3x - 4y <= 12; 3x + 2y >= 3; x + 2y <= 9 (ii) 3x - 4y <= 12; x + 2y <= 6; x + y >= 1 (iii) 2x + y <= 4; 2x - 3y >= 12; x + 2y <= 6 (iv) 2x + y <= 10; x + y <= 7; -2x + y <= 4 (v) 2x + 3y <= 18; 2x + y <= 10; -2x + y <= 2 (vi) 3x - 2y >= 3; x + 4y <= 12; 3x + y <= 12.

(i) Triangle with vertices (-3, 6), (2, -3/2) and (6, 3/2).

(ii) Triangle with vertices (-4, 5), (16/7, -9/7) and (24/5, 3/5).

(iii) The lines 2x + y = 4 and 2x - 3y = 12 meet at the single corner (3, -2); the region lies below all three lines and extends unbounded downward.

(iv) Corner points (1, 6) and (3, 4); the region lies below all three lines and extends unbounded downward.

(v) Corner points (3/2, 5) and (3, 4); the region lies below all three lines and extends unbounded downward.

Answer: (vi) Corner points (18/7, 33/14) and (36/11, 24/11); the region lies below x + 4y = 12 and 3x + y = 12 and above 3x - 2y = 3, extending unbounded downward.

mcqs.q: For the inequality 2x + y <= 6, through which pair of points does the boundary line 2x + y = 6 pass?
mcqs.why: Set y = 0: 2x = 6 so x = 3, giving (3, 0). Set x = 0: y = 6, giving (0, 6). These are the two intercepts stated in the notes.

mcqs.q: For 3x + 7y >= 21, what does testing the origin (0, 0) show, and which side is shaded?
options: Origin satisfies it, so the origin side is shaded
Origin fails it, so the side away from the origin is shaded
Origin lies on the line, so both sides are shaded
Origin fails it, so the origin side is shaded
mcqs.why: At (0, 0): 3(0) + 7(0) = 0, and 0 >= 21 is false. Since the origin fails, the notes shade the side away from the origin, above the line through (7, 0) and (0, 3).

mcqs.q: The inequality 2x + 1 >= 0 is equivalent to which half-plane description?
options: x <= -1/2, to the left of x = -1/2
x >= -1/2, to the right of x = -1/2
x >= 1/2, to the right of x = 1/2
mcqs.why: 2x + 1 >= 0 gives 2x >= -1, so dividing by 2 gives x >= -1/2. This is the vertical half-plane to the right of the line x = -1/2, as in the notes.

mcqs.q: The inequality 3y - 4 <= 0 is equivalent to which condition?
mcqs.why: 3y - 4 <= 0 gives 3y <= 4, so dividing by 3 gives y <= 4/3. The notes shade the horizontal half-plane below the line y = 4/3.

mcqs.q: At what point do the lines 2x - 3y = 6 and 2x + 3y = 12 meet in Exercise 5.1 Q2(i)?
mcqs.why: Add the equations: (2x - 3y) + (2x + 3y) = 6 + 12, so 4x = 18 and x = 9/2. Then 2(9/2) + 3y = 12 gives 9 + 3y = 12, so y = 1. The vertex is (9/2, 1).

mcqs.q: The lines x + y = 5 and x - y = 1 meet at which vertex of their solution region?
mcqs.why: Add the equations: (x + y) + (x - y) = 5 + 1, so 2x = 6 and x = 3. Then 3 + y = 5 gives y = 2. The notes give the vertex as (3, 2), with the region unbounded upward.

mcqs.q: Which set gives the vertices of the bounded triangle for 3x + 7y <= 21, x - y <= 2, x >= 0 in Q3(iv)?
mcqs.why: On x = 0, x - y = 2 gives y = -2, giving (0, -2), and 3x + 7y = 21 gives y = 3, giving (0, 3). Solving 3x + 7y = 21 with x - y = 2 gives x = 7/2, y = 3/2. These three points form the bounded triangle in the notes.

mcqs.q: Which set gives the corner points of the triangle for 2x - 3y <= 6, 2x + 3y <= 12, x >= 0 in Q4(i)?
mcqs.why: On x = 0, 2x - 3y = 6 gives y = -2 and 2x + 3y = 12 gives y = 4, so (0, -2) and (0, 4). The two slanted lines meet at (9/2, 1): 4x = 18 gives x = 9/2 and then y = 1. Hence the triangle corners are as listed.

mcqs.q: For the system 3x + 2y >= 6, x + 3y <= 6, y >= 0 in Q4(iv), what is the corner point where the two slanted lines meet?
mcqs.why: Solve 3x + 2y = 6 and x + 3y = 6. From the second, x = 6 - 3y, so 3(6 - 3y) + 2y = 6 gives 18 - 7y = 6, so y = 12/7 and x = 6 - 36/7 = 6/7. The meeting corner is (6/7, 12/7), with the other corners (2, 0) and (6, 0).

mcqs.q: Which point is a vertex of the triangle for 3x - 4y <= 12, 3x + 2y >= 3, x + 2y <= 9 in Q5(i), in addition to (2, -3/2) and (6, 3/2)?
mcqs.why: The notes list the triangle vertices as (-3, 6), (2, -3/2) and (6, 3/2). Check (-3, 6): 3(-3) + 2(6) = 3 satisfies 3x + 2y >= 3 as equality, and -3 + 2(6) = 9 satisfies x + 2y <= 9 as equality, so it is the intersection of those two lines.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.2 — Feasible regions and corner points
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Graph the feasible region of the following system of linear inequalities and find

the corner points in each case: (i) 2x - 3y <= 6; 2x + 3y <= 12; x >= 0, y >= 0 (ii) x + y <= 5; -2x + y <= 2; x >= 0, y >= 0 (iii) x + y <= 5; -2x + y >= 2; x >= 0 (iv) 3x + 7y <= 21; x - y <= 3; x >= 0, y >= 0 (v) 3x + 2y > 6; x + y <= 4; x >= 0, y >= 0 (vi) 5x + 7y <= 35; x - 2y <= 4; x >= 0, y >= 0.

(i) Corner points (0, 0), (3, 0), (9/2, 1), (0, 4).
