(ii) Corner points (0, 0), (5, 0), (1, 4), (0, 2).

(iii) Triangle with corner points (0, 2), (1, 4), (0, 5).

(iv) Corner points (0, 0), (3, 0), (21/5, 6/5), (0, 3).

(v) Corner points (4, 0), (0, 4), (0, 3), (2, 0); the boundary 3x + 2y = 6 is open (strict inequality) and is not included.

Answer: (vi) Corner points (0, 0), (4, 0), (98/17, 15/17), (0, 5).

Q2. Graph the feasible region of the following system of linear inequalities and find the corner points in each case: (i) 2x + y <= 10; x + 4y <= 12; x + 2y <= 10; x >= 0, y >= 0 (ii) 2x + 3y <= 18; 2x + y <= 10; x + 4y <= 12; x >= 0, y >= 0 (iii) 2x + 3y <= 18; x + 4y <= 12; 3x + y <= 12; x >= 0, y >= 0 (iv) x + 2y <= 14; 3x + 4y <= 36; 2x + y <= 10; x >= 0, y >= 0 (v) x + 3y <= 15; 2x + y <= 12; 4x + 3y <= 24; x >= 0, y >= 0 (vi) 2x + y <= 20; 8x + 15y <= 120; x + y <= 11; x >= 0, y >= 0.

(i) Corner points (0, 0), (5, 0), (4, 2), (0, 3).

(ii) Corner points (0, 0), (5, 0), (4, 2), (0, 3).

(iii) Corner points (0, 0), (4, 0), (36/11, 24/11), (0, 3).

(iv) Corner points (0, 0), (5, 0), (2, 6), (0, 7).

(v) Corner points (0, 0), (6, 0), (3, 4), (0, 5).

Answer: (vi) Corner points (0, 0), (10, 0), (9, 2), (45/7, 32/7), (0, 8).

mcqs.q: Which set gives the corner points of the feasible region for 2x - 3y <= 6, 2x + 3y <= 12, x >= 0, y >= 0?
mcqs.why: With x >= 0, y >= 0 the region includes (0, 0). On y = 0, 2x = 6 gives (3, 0). On x = 0, 3y = 12 gives (0, 4). The two lines meet at (9/2, 1) since 4x = 18 and then y = 1. These are the four corners in the notes.

mcqs.q: For x + y <= 5, -2x + y >= 2, x >= 0, the feasible triangle has which corner points?
mcqs.why: On x = 0, -2x + y = 2 gives (0, 2) and x + y = 5 gives (0, 5). Solving x + y = 5 with -2x + y = 2: subtract to get 3x = 3, so x = 1 and y = 4, giving (1, 4). Hence the triangle is (0, 2), (1, 4), (0, 5).

mcqs.q: At what point do 3x + 7y = 21 and x - y = 3 meet in Q1(iv), giving a corner of the feasible region?
mcqs.why: From x - y = 3, x = y + 3. Substitute in 3x + 7y = 21: 3(y + 3) + 7y = 21 gives 10y + 9 = 21, so y = 12/10 = 6/5 and x = 6/5 + 3 = 21/5. The corner is (21/5, 6/5).

mcqs.q: In Q1(v), with 3x + 2y > 6, x + y <= 4, x >= 0, y >= 0, why is the boundary 3x + 2y = 6 treated differently?
options: It is not a straight line
It is included because the inequality is weak
It is open and not included because the inequality is strict
mcqs.why: The constraint uses the strict symbol > in 3x + 2y > 6. The notes state the boundary 3x + 2y = 6 is open (strict inequality) and is not included, while the corner points are (4, 0), (0, 4), (0, 3) and (2, 0).

mcqs.q: What is the intersection corner of 5x + 7y = 35 and x - 2y = 4 in Q1(vi)?
mcqs.why: From x - 2y = 4, x = 4 + 2y. Substitute in 5x + 7y = 35: 5(4 + 2y) + 7y = 35 gives 20 + 17y = 35, so y = 15/17 and x = 4 + 30/17 = 98/17. The corner is (98/17, 15/17).

mcqs.q: In Q2(i), the corner (4, 2) is the intersection of which two lines?
mcqs.why: Check (4, 2): 2(4) + 2 = 10 satisfies 2x + y = 10, and 4 + 4(2) = 12 satisfies x + 4y = 12. Also 4 + 2(2) = 8 <= 10, so the binding pair at this corner is 2x + y = 10 and x + 4y = 12, as in the feasible region (0, 0), (5, 0), (4, 2), (0, 3).

mcqs.q: What is the non-axis corner in Q2(iii) for 2x + 3y <= 18, x + 4y <= 12, 3x + y <= 12, x >= 0, y >= 0, besides (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 3)?
mcqs.why: The corner is the intersection of x + 4y = 12 and 3x + y = 12. From the second, y = 12 - 3x, so x + 4(12 - 3x) = 12 gives x + 48 - 11x = 12, so -11x = -36, x = 36/11 and y = 12 - 108/11 = 24/11. Hence (36/11, 24/11).

mcqs.q: In Q2(iv), the corner (2, 6) lies on which pair of boundary lines?
mcqs.why: Check (2, 6): x + 2y = 2 + 12 = 14, so it lies on x + 2y = 14, and 2x + y = 4 + 6 = 10, so it lies on 2x + y = 10. By contrast 3x + 4y = 6 + 24 = 30, not 36, so that line is not binding there.

mcqs.q: Which point is a corner of the feasible region in Q2(v) for x + 3y <= 15, 2x + y <= 12, 4x + 3y <= 24, x >= 0, y >= 0, lying on both x + 3y = 15 and 4x + 3y = 24?
mcqs.why: Check (3, 4): x + 3y = 3 + 12 = 15, so it lies on x + 3y = 15, and 4x + 3y = 12 + 12 = 24, so it lies on 4x + 3y = 24, while 2x + y = 6 + 4 = 10 <= 12 is satisfied. Hence (3, 4) is the intersection corner listed in the notes, with the other corners (0, 0), (6, 0) and (0, 5).

mcqs.q: In Q2(vi), which list gives all the corner points of the feasible region?
mcqs.why: The notes list five corners: (0, 0), (10, 0), (9, 2), (45/7, 32/7) and (0, 8). Check (9, 2): 2(9) + 2 = 20 meets 2x + y = 20 and 9 + 2 = 11 meets x + y = 11, confirming it as their intersection corner.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.3 — Linear programming problems
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Maximize f(x, y) = 2x + 5y subject to the constraints 2y - x <= 8; x - y <= 4; x >= 0; y >= 0.

Feasible corner points: (0, 0), (0, 4), (16, 12), (4, 0).

Values of f: f(0, 0) = 0; f(0, 4) = 20; f(16, 12) = 32 + 60 = 92; f(4, 0) = 8.

Answer: maximum value 92 at (16, 12).

Q2. Maximize f(x, y) = x + 3y subject to the constraints 2x + 5y <= 30; 5x + 4y <= 20; x >= 0; y >= 0.

The two lines meet outside the first quadrant (at negative x), so in the first quadrant the second constraint dominates: the feasible region is the triangle (0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 5).

Values of f: f(0, 0) = 0; f(4, 0) = 4; f(0, 5) = 15.

Answer: maximum value 15 at (0, 5).

Q3. Maximize z = 2x + 3y subject to the constraints 3x + 4y <= 12; 2x + y <= 4; 4x - y <= 4; x >= 0; y >= 0.

Feasible corner points: (0, 0), (0, 3), (4/5, 12/5), (4/3, 4/3), (1, 0).

Values of z: z(0, 3) = 9; z(4/5, 12/5) = 44/5 = 8.8; z(4/3, 4/3) = 20/3; z(1, 0) = 2.

Answer: maximum value 9 at (0, 3).

Q4. Minimize z = 2x + y subject to the constraints x + y >= 3; 7x + 5y <= 35; x >= 0; y >= 0.

Feasible corner points: (0, 3), (0, 7), (5, 0), (3, 0).

Values of z: z(0, 3) = 3; z(0, 7) = 7; z(5, 0) = 10; z(3, 0) = 6.

Answer: minimum value 3 at (0, 3).

Q5. Maximize the function defined as f(x, y) = 2x + 3y subject to the constraints 2x + y <= 8; x + 2y <= 14; x >= 0; y >= 0.

Feasible corner points: (0, 0), (4, 0), (2/3, 20/3), (0, 7).

Values of f: f(4, 0) = 8; f(2/3, 20/3) = 4/3 + 20 = 64/3; f(0, 7) = 21.

Answer: maximum value 64/3 at (2/3, 20/3).

Q6. Minimize z = 3x + y subject to the constraints 3x + 5y >= 15; x + 6y >= 9; x >= 0; y >= 0.

Feasible corner points: (0, 3), (45/13, 12/13), (9, 0); the region is unbounded, but z

has positive coefficients so its minimum occurs at a corner.

Values of z: z(0, 3) = 3; z(45/13, 12/13) = 147/13; z(9, 0) = 27.

Answer: minimum value 3 at (0, 3).

Q7. Each unit of food X costs Rs.

25 and contains 2 units of protein and 4 units of iron while each unit of food Y costs Rs. 30 and contains 3 units of protein and 2 units of iron. Each animal must receive at least 12 units of protein and 16 units of iron each day. How many units of each food should be fed to each animal at the smallest possible cost? Let x units of X and y units of Y be fed. Minimize cost C = 25x + 30y subject to 2x + 3y >= 12 (protein), 4x + 2y >= 16 (iron), x >= 0, y >= 0.

Feasible corner points: (6, 0) (satisfies both: protein 12, iron 24), (3, 2) (intersection: protein 12, iron 16), (0, 8) (protein 24, iron 16).

Costs: C(6, 0) = 150; C(3, 2) = 75 + 60 = 135; C(0, 8) = 240.

Answer: smallest cost Rs. 135 with 3 units of food X and 2 units of food Y per animal per day.

Q8. A dealer wishes to purchase a number of fans and sewing machines.

He has only Rs. 5760 to invest and has space at most for 20 items. A fan costs him Rs. 360 and a sewing machine costs Rs. 240. His expectation is that he can sell a fan at a profit of Rs. 22 and a sewing machine at a profit of Rs. 18. Assuming that he can sell all the items that he can buy, how should he invest his money in order to maximize

his profit?

Let x fans and y sewing machines be bought. Maximize profit P = 22x + 18y subject to 360x + 240y <= 5760 (money), x + y <= 20 (space), x >= 0, y >= 0.

Feasible corner points: (0, 0), (16, 0), (8, 12) (intersection of 3x + 2y = 48 and x + y = 20), (0, 20).

Profits: P(16, 0) = 352; P(8, 12) = 176 + 216 = 392; P(0, 20) = 360.

Answer: maximum profit Rs. 392 by buying 8 fans and 12 sewing machines.

Q9. A machine can produce product A by using 2 units of chemical and 1 unit of a compound or can produce product B by using 1 unit of chemical and 2 units of the compound.

Only 800 units of chemical and 1000 units of the compound are available. The profits per unit of A and B are Rs. 30 and Rs. 20 respectively, maximize the profit function. Let x units of A and y units of B be produced. Maximize profit P = 30x + 20y subject to 2x + y <= 800 (chemical), x + 2y <= 1000 (compound), x >= 0, y >= 0.

Feasible corner points: (0, 0), (400, 0), (200, 400) (intersection), (0, 500).

Profits: P(400, 0) = 12000; P(200, 400) = 6000 + 8000 = 14000; P(0, 500) = 10000.

Answer: maximum profit Rs. 14000 by producing 200 units of A and 400 units of B.

mcqs.q: Maximize f(x, y) = 2x + 5y subject to 2y - x <= 8, x - y <= 4, x >= 0, y >= 0. What is the maximum?
Maximize f(x, y) = x + 3y subject to 2x + 5y <= 30, 5x + 4y <= 20, x >= 0, y >= 0. What is the maximum?
mcqs.why: The two lines meet outside the first quadrant, so the feasible triangle is (0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 5). Values: f(0, 0) = 0; f(4, 0) = 4 + 0 = 4; f(0, 5) = 0 + 3(5) = 15. The maximum is 15 at (0, 5).

mcqs.q: Maximize z = 2x + 3y subject to 3x + 4y <= 12, 2x + y <= 4, 4x - y <= 4, x >= 0, y >= 0. What is the maximum?
For the same maximization of z = 2x + 3y in Q3, what is z at the corner (4/5, 12/5)?
mcqs.why: z(4/5, 12/5) = 2(4/5) + 3(12/5) = 8/5 + 36/5 = 44/5 = 8.8. This is less than the maximum 9 at (0, 3), so (4/5, 12/5) is not the maximizer.

mcqs.q: Minimize z = 2x + y subject to x + y >= 3, 7x + 5y <= 35, x >= 0, y >= 0. What is the minimum?
Maximize f(x, y) = 2x + 3y subject to 2x + y <= 8, x + 2y <= 14, x >= 0, y >= 0. What is the maximum?
Minimize z = 3x + y subject to 3x + 5y >= 15, x + 6y >= 9, x >= 0, y >= 0. What is the minimum?
mcqs.why: Corner values: z(0, 3) = 3(0) + 3 = 3; z(45/13, 12/13) = 3(45/13) + 12/13 = 135/13 + 12/13 = 147/13; z(9, 0) = 3(9) + 0 = 27. The region is unbounded but the smallest corner value, 3 at (0, 3), is the minimum.

mcqs.q: Food X costs Rs. 25 and food Y costs Rs. 30, with protein and iron requirements 2x + 3y >= 12 and 4x + 2y >= 16. What feeding gives the smallest cost?
options: 6 units of X, 0 of Y, cost Rs. 150
0 of X, 8 units of Y, cost Rs. 240
2 units of X, 3 units of Y, cost Rs. 140
3 units of X, 2 units of Y, cost Rs. 135
mcqs.why: Minimize C = 25x + 30y. Costs: C(6, 0) = 25(6) + 0 = 150; C(3, 2) = 25(3) + 30(2) = 75 + 60 = 135; C(0, 8) = 0 + 30(8) = 240. The smallest cost is Rs. 135 with 3 units of X and 2 units of Y.

mcqs.q: A dealer with Rs. 5760 and space for at most 20 items buys fans (Rs. 360, profit Rs. 22) and sewing machines (Rs. 240, profit Rs. 18). How should he invest to maximize profit?
mcqs.why: Maximize P = 22x + 18y. Profits: P(16, 0) = 22(16) = 352; P(8, 12) = 22(8) + 18(12) = 176 + 216 = 392; P(0, 20) = 18(20) = 360. The point (12, 8) costs 360(12) + 240(8) = 6240 > 5760, so it is infeasible. The maximum feasible profit is Rs. 392 with 8 fans and 12 machines.

mcqs.q: Products A and B give profits Rs. 30 and Rs. 20, with 2x + y <= 800 and x + 2y <= 1000. What production maximizes profit?
options: 400 of A, 0 of B, profit Rs. 12000
0 of A, 500 of B, profit Rs. 10000
200 of A, 400 of B, profit Rs. 14000
400 of A, 400 of B, profit Rs. 20000

lessons.title: Exercise 6.1 — The circle
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. In each of the following, find an equation of the circle with (a) centre at (5, -2) and radius 4 (b) centre at (sqrt(2), -3 sqrt(3)) and radius 2 sqrt(2) (c) ends of a diameter at (-3, 2) and (5, -6).

(a) (x - 5)2 + (y + 2)2 = 16, i.e. x2 + y2 - 10x + 4y + 13 = 0.

(b) (x - sqrt(2))2 + (y + 3 sqrt(3))2 = 8, i.e. x2 + y2 - 2 sqrt(2) x + 6 sqrt(3) y + 21 = 0.

Answer: (c) Centre is the midpoint (1, -2); radius is half the distance between the ends, sqrt(128)/2 = 4 sqrt(2). Equation: (x - 1)2 + (y + 2)2 = 32, i.e. x2 + y2 - 2x + 4y - 27 = 0.

Q2. Find the centre and radius of the circle with the given equation (a) x2 + y2 + 12x - 10y = 0 (b) 5x2 + 5y2 + 14x + 12y - 10 = 0 (c) x2 + y2 - 6x + 4y + 13 = 0 (d) 4x2 + 4y2 - 8x + 12y - 25 = 0.

Complete the squares. (a) (x + 6)2 + (y - 5)2 = 61: centre (-6, 5), radius sqrt(61).

(b) Dividing by 5: x2 + y2 + (14/5)x + (12/5)y - 2 = 0, so (x + 7/5)2 + (y + 6/5)2 = 27/5: centre (-7/5, -6/5), radius 3 sqrt(15)/5.

(c) (x - 3)2 + (y + 2)2 = 0: centre (3, -2), radius 0, a degenerate point circle.

Answer: (d) Dividing by 4: x2 + y2 - 2x + 3y - 25/4 = 0, so (x - 1)2 + (y + 3/2)2 = 19/2: centre (1, -3/2), radius sqrt(38)/2.

Q3. Write an equation of the circle that passes through the given points (a) A(4, 5), B(-4, -3), C(8, -3) (b) A(-7, 7), B(5, -1), C(10, 0) (c) A(a, 0), B(0, b), C(0, 0) (d) A(5, 6), B(-3, 2), C(3, -4).

Use x2 + y2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 and solve for g, f, c. (a) Subtracting the equations in pairs gives g = -2, f = 1, c = -35: x2 + y2 - 4x + 2y - 35 = 0.

(b) Solving gives g = -5, f = -12, c = 0: x2 + y2 - 10x - 24y = 0.

(c) Through the origin c = 0; through (a, 0) gives g = -a/2; through (0, b) gives f = -b/2: x2 + y2 - ax - by = 0.

Answer: (d) Solving gives g = -7/3, f = -4/3, c = -65/3: 3x2 + 3y2 - 14x - 8y - 65 = 0.

Q4. In each of the following, find an equation of the circle passing through (a) A(3, -1), B(0, 1) and having centre at 4x - 3y - 3 = 0 (b) A(-3, 1) with radius 2 and centre at 2x - 3y + 3 = 0 (c) A(5, 1) and tangent to the line 2x - y - 10 = 0 at B(3, -4) (d) A(1, 4), B(-1, 8) and tangent to the line x + 3y - 3 = 0.

(a) Equidistance from A and B gives 3h - 2k = 9/2; with 4h - 3k = 3 this gives centre (15/2, 9) and radius squared 481/4: x2 + y2 - 15x - 18y + 17 = 0.

(b) Centre (h, k) on 2x - 3y + 3 = 0 at distance 2 from (-3, 1) gives 13k2 + 10k - 3 = 0, so k = 3/13 or k = -1: circles (x + 3)2 + (y + 1)2 = 4 and (x + 15/13)2 + (y 3/13)2 = 4.

(c) The centre lies on the perpendicular to 2x - y - 10 = 0 at B, i.e. x + 2y + 5 = 0, and is equidistant from A and B, giving centre (-26, 21/2): x2 + y2 + 52x - 21y - 265 = 0.

Answer: (d) Equidistance from A and B gives h = 2k - 12; equating distance to the line with distance to A gives k2 - 18k + 65 = 0, so k = 5 or 13: circles x2 + y2 + 4x 10y + 19 = 0 (centre (-2, 5)) and x2 + y2 - 28x - 26y + 115 = 0 (centre (14, 13)).

Q5. Find an equation of a circle of radius a and lying in the second quadrant such that it is tangent to both the axes.

A circle in the second quadrant tangent to both axes has centre (-a, a) and radius a.

Answer: (x + a)2 + (y - a)2 = a2, i.e. x2 + y2 + 2ax - 2ay + a2 = 0.

Q6. Show that the lines 3x - 2y = 0 and 2x + 3y - 13 = 0 are tangents to the circle x2 + y2 + 6x - 4y = 0.

The circle has centre (-3, 2) and radius sqrt(9 + 4) = sqrt(13).

Distance from (-3, 2) to 3x - 2y = 0 is |-9 - 4|/sqrt(13) = sqrt(13), equal to the radius.

Answer: distance from (-3, 2) to 2x + 3y - 13 = 0 is |-6 + 6 - 13|/sqrt(13) = sqrt(13), equal to the radius; so both lines are tangents.

Q7. Show that the circles x2 + y2 + 2x - 2y - 7 = 0 and x2 + y2 - 6x + 4y + 9 = 0 touch externally.

First circle: centre (-1, 1), radius sqrt(1 + 1 + 7) = 3. Second circle: centre (3, -2), radius sqrt(9 + 4 - 9) = 2.

Distance between centres = sqrt(16 + 9) = 5 = 3 + 2, the sum of the radii.

Answer: the circles touch externally.

Q8. Show that the circles x2 + y2 + 2x - 8 = 0 and x2 + y2 - 6x + 6y - 46 = 0 touch internally.

First circle: centre (-1, 0), radius sqrt(1 + 8) = 3. Second circle: centre (3, -3), radius sqrt(9 + 9 + 46) = 8.

Distance between centres = sqrt(16 + 9) = 5 = 8 - 3, the difference of the radii.

Answer: the circles touch internally.

Q9. Find equations of the circles of radius 2 and tangent to the line x - y - 4 = 0 at A(1, -3).

The centre lies on the perpendicular to x - y - 4 = 0 through A(1, -3), i.e. x + y + 2 = 0, at distance 2 from A.

This gives (h - 1)2 + (k + 3)2 = 4 with k = -h - 2, i.e. 2(h - 1)2 = 4, so h = 1 + sqrt(2) or h = 1 - sqrt(2).

Answer: centres (1 + sqrt(2), -3 - sqrt(2)) and (1 - sqrt(2), -3 + sqrt(2)); equations x2 + y2 - 2(1 + sqrt(2))x + 2(3 + sqrt(2))y + 10 + 8 sqrt(2) = 0 and x2 + y2 - 2(1 sqrt(2))x + 2(3 - sqrt(2))y + 10 - 8 sqrt(2) = 0.

mcqs.q: What is the equation of the circle with centre (5, -2) and radius 4, in general form?
What is the equation of the circle with centre (sqrt(2), -3 sqrt(3)) and radius 2 sqrt(2), in general form?
mcqs.why: (x - sqrt(2))^2 + (y + 3 sqrt(3))^2 = (2 sqrt(2))^2 = 8. Expanding: x^2 - 2 sqrt(2) x + 2 + y^2 + 6 sqrt(3) y + 27 = 8, so x^2 + y^2 - 2 sqrt(2) x + 6 sqrt(3) y + (2 + 27 - 8) = 0, i.e. the constant term is 21.

mcqs.q: A circle has the ends of a diameter at (-3, 2) and (5, -6). What is its centre?
mcqs.why: The centre is the midpoint of the diameter: ((-3 + 5)/2, (2 + (-6))/2) = (2/2, -4/2) = (1, -2).

mcqs.q: For the circle with ends of a diameter at (-3, 2) and (5, -6), what is the radius?
mcqs.why: Distance between the ends: sqrt((5 - (-3))^2 + (-6 - 2)^2) = sqrt(64 + 64) = sqrt(128) = 8 sqrt(2). The radius is half of this: 8 sqrt(2)/2 = 4 sqrt(2), and indeed the equation is (x - 1)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 32.

mcqs.q: Find the centre and radius of the circle x^2 + y^2 + 12x - 10y = 0.
mcqs.why: Completing the squares: (x + 6)^2 - 36 + (y - 5)^2 - 25 = 0, so (x + 6)^2 + (y - 5)^2 = 36 + 25 = 61. Hence centre (-6, 5) and radius sqrt(61).

mcqs.q: Find the centre of the circle 5x^2 + 5y^2 + 14x + 12y - 10 = 0.
mcqs.why: Divide by 5: x^2 + y^2 + (14/5)x + (12/5)y - 2 = 0. Comparing with x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 gives g = 7/5 and f = 6/5, so the centre is (-g, -f) = (-7/5, -6/5). (Completing squares gives radius 3 sqrt(15)/5.)

mcqs.q: What is the radius of the circle x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 4y + 13 = 0?
options: 0; it is a degenerate point circle at (3, -2)
mcqs.why: Completing the squares: (x - 3)^2 - 9 + (y + 2)^2 - 4 + 13 = 0, so (x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 9 + 4 - 13 = 0. Radius squared is 0, so the radius is 0: a degenerate point circle at (3, -2).

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the circle passing through A(4, 5), B(-4, -3) and C(8, -3).
mcqs.why: Substitute the three points into x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 and subtract the equations in pairs; solving gives g = -2, f = 1, c = -35. Hence 2g = -4, 2f = 2 and the equation is x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 2y - 35 = 0.

mcqs.q: A circle of radius a lies in the second quadrant and is tangent to both axes. What is its centre?
mcqs.why: Tangency to both axes means the distance from the centre to each axis equals the radius a, so the centre is a units from each axis. In the second quadrant x is negative and y is positive, giving centre (-a, a) and equation (x + a)^2 + (y - a)^2 = a^2.

mcqs.q: For the circle x^2 + y^2 + 6x - 4y = 0, which statement about the line 3x - 2y = 0 is correct?
options: The radius is 13 and the line is not a tangent
The radius is sqrt(13) and the line is a tangent
The radius is sqrt(13) and the line is not a tangent
The radius is 5 and the line is a tangent
mcqs.why: Centre is (-3, 2) and radius = sqrt(3^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(13) (from g = 3, f = -2: r = sqrt(g^2 + f^2 - c) = sqrt(9 + 4 - 0)). Distance from (-3, 2) to 3x - 2y = 0 is |3(-3) - 2(2)|/sqrt(9 + 4) = 13/sqrt(13) = sqrt(13), equal to the radius, so the line is a tangent.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.2 — Tangents and normals to a circle
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Write down equations of the tangent and normal to the circle (i) x2 + y2 = 25 at (4, 3) and at (5 cos(theta), 5 sin(theta)) (ii) 3x2 + 3y2 + 5x - 13y + 2 = 0 at (1, 10/3).

(i) At (4, 3): tangent 4x + 3y = 25; normal (through the origin and the point) 3x - 4y = 0.

At (5 cos(theta), 5 sin(theta)): tangent x cos(theta) + y sin(theta) = 5; normal x sin(theta) - y cos(theta) = 0.

Answer: (ii) In standard form x2 + y2 + (5/3)x - (13/3)y + 2/3 = 0, so g = 5/6, f = -13/6. Tangent T = 0: 33x + 21y - 103 = 0. Normal: (y - 10/3)(11/6) = (x - 1)(7/6), i.e. 21x - 33y + 89 = 0.

Q2. Write down equations of the tangent and normal to the circle 4x2 + 4y2 - 16x + 24y - 117 = 0 at the points on the circle whose abscissa is -4.

In standard form x2 + y2 - 4x + 6y - 117/4 = 0. Putting x = -4 gives y2 + 6y + 11/4 = 0, so y = -1/2 or y = -11/2.

At (-4, -1/2): tangent -24x + 10y - 91 = 0; normal 5x + 12y + 26 = 0.

Answer: at (-4, -11/2): tangent 24x + 10y + 151 = 0; normal 5x - 12y - 46 = 0.

Q3. Check the position of the point (5, 6) with respect to the circle (i) x2 + y2 = 81 (ii) 2x2 + 2y2 + 12x - 8y + 1 = 0.

(i) Substituting: 25 + 36 = 61 < 81, so the point lies inside the circle.

Answer: (ii) Dividing by 2: x2 + y2 + 6x - 4y + 1/2 = 0; substituting gives 25 + 36 + 30 - 24 + 1/2 = 135/2 > 0, so the point lies outside the circle.

Q4. Find the length of the tangent drawn from the point (-5, 4) to the circle 5x2 + 5y2 - 10x + 15y - 131 = 0.

In standard form x2 + y2 - 2x + 3y - 131/5 = 0.

Substituting (-5, 4): 25 + 16 + 10 + 12 - 131/5 = 184/5.

Answer: length of the tangent = sqrt(184/5) = 2 sqrt(230)/5.

Q5. Find the length of the chord cut off from the line 2x + 3y = 13 by the circle x2 + y2 = 26.

Centre (0, 0), radius sqrt(26). Distance from the centre to the line = 13/sqrt(13) = sqrt(13).

Half the chord = sqrt(26 - 13) = sqrt(13).

Answer: length of the chord = 2 sqrt(13).

Q6. Find the coordinates of the points of intersection of the line x + 2y = 6 with the circle x2 + y2 - 2x - 2y - 39 = 0.

Putting x = 6 - 2y in the circle gives 5y2 - 22y - 15 = 0, so y = 5 or y = -3/5.

Answer: points of intersection (-4, 5) and (36/5, -3/5).

Q7. Find equations of the tangents to the circle x2 + y2 = 2 (i) parallel to the line x 2y + 1 = 0 (ii) perpendicular to the line 3x + 2y = 6.

(i) Tangents parallel to x - 2y + 1 = 0 have the form x - 2y + c = 0; distance from the origin equal to the radius sqrt(2) gives |c|/sqrt(5) = sqrt(2), so c = + sqrt(10) or

- sqrt(10).

Answer: (i) x - 2y + sqrt(10) = 0 and x - 2y - sqrt(10) = 0. (ii) Tangents perpendicular to 3x + 2y = 6 have slope 2/3, i.e. form 2x - 3y + c = 0; |c|/sqrt(13) = sqrt(2) gives c = + sqrt(26) or - sqrt(26): 2x - 3y + sqrt(26) = 0 and 2x - 3y sqrt(26) = 0.

Q8. Find equations of the tangents drawn from (i) (0, 5) to x2 + y2 = 16 (ii) (-1, 2) to x2 + y2 + 4x + 2y = 0 (iii) (-7, -2) to (x + 1)2 + (y - 2)2 = 26.

Also find the points of contact. (i) Chord of contact: 5y = 16, i.e. y = 16/5; with the circle this gives x = + 12/5 or 12/5. Tangents: 3x + 4y = 20 and -3x + 4y = 20; points of contact (12/5, 16/5) and (-12/5, 16/5).

(ii) Chord of contact: x + 3y = 0; with the circle this gives (0, 0) and (-3, 1). Tangents: 2x + y = 0 and x - 2y + 5 = 0.

Answer: (iii) Chord of contact: 3x + 2y + 12 = 0; with the circle this gives (-2, -3) and (-6, 3). Tangents: x + 5y + 17 = 0 and 5x - y + 33 = 0.

Q9. Find an equation of the chord of contact of the tangents drawn from (4, 5) to the circle 2x2 + 2y2 - 8x + 12y + 21 = 0.

In standard form x2 + y2 - 4x + 6y + 21/2 = 0.

Chord of contact T = 0: 4x + 5y - 2(x + 4) + 3(y + 5) + 21/2 = 0.

Answer: 4x + 16y + 35 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the tangent to the circle x^2 + y^2 = 25 at the point (4, 3).
mcqs.why: For x^2 + y^2 = r^2 the tangent at (x1, y1) is x x1 + y y1 = r^2 (T = 0). With (x1, y1) = (4, 3): 4x + 3y = 25. Check: 4(4) + 3(3) = 25, so the point lies on it.

mcqs.q: Find the normal to the circle x^2 + y^2 = 25 at the point (4, 3).
mcqs.why: The normal at a point of a circle passes through the centre (0, 0) and the point (4, 3), so its slope is 3/4 and its equation is y = (3/4)x, i.e. 3x - 4y = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the tangent to x^2 + y^2 = 25 at the point (5 cos(theta), 5 sin(theta)).
mcqs.why: Tangent T = 0: x x1 + y y1 = 25 with x1 = 5 cos(theta), y1 = 5 sin(theta) gives 5x cos(theta) + 5y sin(theta) = 25; dividing by 5: x cos(theta) + y sin(theta) = 5.

mcqs.q: What is the position of the point (5, 6) with respect to the circle x^2 + y^2 = 81?
mcqs.why: Substitute (5, 6): 5^2 + 6^2 = 25 + 36 = 61. Since 61 < 81, the value of x^2 + y^2 - 81 is negative, so the point lies inside the circle.

mcqs.q: What is the position of the point (5, 6) with respect to the circle 2x^2 + 2y^2 + 12x - 8y + 1 = 0?
options: At the centre of the circle
mcqs.why: Divide by 2: x^2 + y^2 + 6x - 4y + 1/2 = 0. Substituting (5, 6): 25 + 36 + 30 - 24 + 1/2 = 135/2, which is greater than 0, so the point lies outside the circle.

mcqs.q: Find the length of the tangent drawn from (-5, 4) to the circle 5x^2 + 5y^2 - 10x + 15y - 131 = 0.
Find the length of the chord cut off from the line 2x + 3y = 13 by the circle x^2 + y^2 = 26.
mcqs.why: Centre (0, 0), radius sqrt(26). Perpendicular distance from the centre to the line: 13/sqrt(2^2 + 3^2) = 13/sqrt(13) = sqrt(13). Half the chord = sqrt(r^2 - d^2) = sqrt(26 - 13) = sqrt(13), so the chord length is 2 sqrt(13).

mcqs.q: Find the points of intersection of the line x + 2y = 6 with the circle x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 2y - 39 = 0.
mcqs.why: Put x = 6 - 2y into the circle; simplifying gives 5y^2 - 22y - 15 = 0, i.e. (5y + 3)(y - 5) = 0, so y = 5 or y = -3/5. Then x = 6 - 2(5) = -4 and x = 6 - 2(-3/5) = 36/5, giving (-4, 5) and (36/5, -3/5).

mcqs.q: Find the tangents drawn from (0, 5) to the circle x^2 + y^2 = 16.
Find the chord of contact of the tangents drawn from (4, 5) to the circle 2x^2 + 2y^2 - 8x + 12y + 21 = 0.
mcqs.why: Divide by 2: x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 6y + 21/2 = 0. Chord of contact T = 0 from (4, 5): 4x + 5y - 2(x + 4) + 3(y + 5) + 21/2 = 0, i.e. 2x + 8y + 35/2 = 0; multiplying by 2: 4x + 16y + 35 = 0.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.3 — Analytic proofs of properties of a circle
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Prove that normal lines of a circle pass through the centre of the circle.

For the circle x2 + y2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0, the normal at P(x1, y1) is (y - y1)(x1 + g) = (x - x1)(y1 + f).

The centre is (-g, -f). Putting x = -g and y = -f gives left side (-f - y1)(x1 + g) = -(y1 + f)(x1 + g) and right side (-g - x1)(y1 + f) = -(x1 + g)(y1 + f).

Answer: both sides are equal, so the centre lies on the normal; hence every normal passes through the centre.

Q2. Prove that the straight line drawn from the centre of a circle perpendicular to a tangent passes through the point of tangency.

Let P(x1, y1) be the point of tangency on x2 + y2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0, whose centre is C(-g, -f).

The tangent at P has slope -(x1 + g)/(y1 + f), so the line through C perpendicular to it has slope (y1 + f)/(x1 + g) and equation y + f = ((y1 + f)/(x1 + g))(x + g).

Answer: putting x = x1 gives y + f = y1 + f, i.e. y = y1, so the line passes through P(x1, y1), the point of tangency.

Q3. Prove that the mid point of the hypotenuse of a right triangle is the circumcentre of the triangle.

Place the right angle at the origin: let the triangle have vertices C(0, 0), A(a, 0) and B(0, b), with hypotenuse AB.

The midpoint of AB is M(a/2, b/2). Then MA = MB = sqrt(a2 + b2)/2.

Answer: also MC = sqrt((a/2)2 + (b/2)2) = sqrt(a2 + b2)/2, so M is equidistant from A, B and C; hence M is the circumcentre.

Q4. Prove that the perpendicular dropped from a point of a circle on a diameter is a mean proportional between the segments into which it divides the diameter.

Take the diameter AB on the x-axis with A(-a, 0), B(a, 0), so the circle is x2 + y2 = a2. Let P(x1, y1) be a point on the circle and M(x1, 0) the foot of the perpendicular from P to AB.

Then PM = y1, AM = x1 + a and MB = a - x1, so AM times MB = (a + x1)(a - x1) = a2 - x12.

Answer: since P lies on the circle, y12 = a2 - x12, so PM2 = AM times MB, i.e. PM is the mean proportional between AM and MB.

mcqs.q: In the proof that normals of a circle pass through its centre, the circle is taken as x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0. What is its centre?
mcqs.why: Completing the squares: (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c, so the centre is (-g, -f) and the radius is sqrt(g^2 + f^2 - c). This centre is used throughout the proof.

mcqs.q: For the circle x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0, the normal at P(x1, y1) has which equation?
options: x x1 + y y1 + g(x + x1) + f(y + y1) + c = 0
mcqs.why: The normal at P(x1, y1) is (y - y1)(x1 + g) = (x - x1)(y1 + f), as used in the proof. (The third option is the tangent T = 0, not the normal.)

mcqs.q: To prove the centre (-g, -f) lies on the normal (y - y1)(x1 + g) = (x - x1)(y1 + f), substituting x = -g, y = -f makes the two sides:
mcqs.why: Left side: (-f - y1)(x1 + g) = -(y1 + f)(x1 + g). Right side: (-g - x1)(y1 + f) = -(x1 + g)(y1 + f). The two products are identical, so both sides equal -(x1 + g)(y1 + f); hence the centre lies on the normal.

mcqs.q: In the proof about the line from the centre perpendicular to a tangent, the tangent at P(x1, y1) on x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 has slope:
mcqs.why: From the tangent equation, its slope is -(x1 + g)/(y1 + f). The line through the centre C(-g, -f) perpendicular to the tangent therefore has the negative-reciprocal slope (y1 + f)/(x1 + g).

mcqs.q: The line through the centre C(-g, -f) perpendicular to the tangent at P(x1, y1) is y + f = ((y1 + f)/(x1 + g))(x + g). Why does it pass through P?
options: Putting x = x1 gives y + f = y1 + f, i.e. y = y1, so the point (x1, y1) = P satisfies it
P is the centre of the circle
The line is the tangent itself
mcqs.why: Substitute x = x1: y + f = ((y1 + f)/(x1 + g))(x1 + g) = y1 + f, so y = y1. Thus (x1, y1), the point of tangency P, lies on the line, which proves the statement.

mcqs.q: In the circumcentre proof, the right triangle is placed with vertices C(0, 0), A(a, 0), B(0, b). The midpoint M of the hypotenuse AB is:
mcqs.why: Midpoint of A(a, 0) and B(0, b): ((a + 0)/2, (0 + b)/2) = (a/2, b/2). The right angle is at C(0, 0), so AB is the hypotenuse.

mcqs.q: With M(a/2, b/2) as above, the distance MA equals:
mcqs.why: MA = sqrt((a - a/2)^2 + (0 - b/2)^2) = sqrt((a/2)^2 + (b/2)^2) = sqrt(a^2 + b^2)/2. The same computation gives MB = sqrt(a^2 + b^2)/2.

mcqs.q: Why is M(a/2, b/2) the circumcentre of the right triangle with vertices C(0, 0), A(a, 0), B(0, b)?
options: Because MA = MB = MC = sqrt(a^2 + b^2)/2, so M is equidistant from all three vertices
Because M lies on the hypotenuse AB only
mcqs.why: MC = sqrt((a/2)^2 + (b/2)^2) = sqrt(a^2 + b^2)/2, and MA = MB = sqrt(a^2 + b^2)/2 as well. A point equidistant from all three vertices is the circumcentre, so M is the circumcentre.

mcqs.q: In the mean-proportional proof, the diameter AB lies on the x-axis with A(-a, 0), B(a, 0), P(x1, y1) is on x^2 + y^2 = a^2, and M is the foot of the perpendicular from P to AB. Then M is:
mcqs.why: The perpendicular from P(x1, y1) to the x-axis meets it at the point with the same x-coordinate and y = 0, i.e. M(x1, 0). Hence PM = y1, AM = x1 + a and MB = a - x1.

mcqs.q: In the same proof, PM is the mean proportional between AM and MB because:
mcqs.why: AM x MB = (a + x1)(a - x1) = a^2 - x1^2. Since P(x1, y1) lies on x^2 + y^2 = a^2, y1^2 = a^2 - x1^2, and PM = y1, so PM^2 = a^2 - x1^2 = AM x MB; i.e. PM is the mean proportional between AM and MB.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.4 — Parabola
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find the focus, vertex and directrix of the parabola.

Sketch its graph. (i) y2 = 8x (ii) x2 = -16y (iii) x2 = 5y (iv) y2 = -12x (v) x2 = 4(y - 1) (vi) y2 = -8(x - 3) (vii) (x 1)2 = 8(y + 2) (viii) y = 6x2 - 1 (ix) x + 8 - y2 + 2y = 0 (x) x2 - 4x - 8y + 4 = 0. (i) 4a = 8, a = 2: vertex (0, 0), focus (2, 0), directrix x = -2, opening right. (ii) 4a = 16, a = 4: vertex (0, 0), focus (0, -4), directrix y = 4, opening downward.

(iii) 4a = 5, a = 5/4: vertex (0, 0), focus (0, 5/4), directrix y = -5/4, opening upward. (iv) 4a = 12, a = 3: vertex (0, 0), focus (-3, 0), directrix x = 3, opening left.

(v) Vertex (0, 1), a = 1: focus (0, 2), directrix y = 0. (vi) Vertex (3, 0), a = 2: focus (1, 0), directrix x = 5.

(vii) Vertex (1, -2), a = 2: focus (1, 0), directrix y = -4. (viii) x2 = (1/6)(y + 1), a = 1/24: vertex (0, -1), focus (0, -23/24), directrix y = -25/24.

Answer: (ix) (y - 1)2 = x + 9, a = 1/4: vertex (-9, 1), focus (-35/4, 1), directrix x = -37/4. (x) (x - 2)2 = 8y, a = 2: vertex (2, 0), focus (2, 2), directrix y = -2.

Q2. Write an equation of the parabola with given elements.

(i) Focus (-3, 1); directrix x = 3 (ii) Focus (2, 5); directrix y = 1 (iii) Focus (-3, 1); directrix x - 2y - 3 = 0 (iv) Focus (1, 2); vertex (3, 2) (v) Focus (-1, 0); vertex (-1, 2) (vi) Directrix x = -2; Focus (2, 2) (vii) Directrix y = 3; vertex (2, 2) (viii) Directrix y = 1, length of latus rectum is 8. Opens downward. (ix) Axis y = 0, through (2, 1) and (11, -2) (x) Axis parallel to y-axis, the points (0, 3), (3, 4) and (4, 11) lie on the graph. (i) Vertex is the midpoint (0, 1) of focus and foot of perpendicular, a = 3, opening left: (y - 1)2 = -12x. (ii) Vertex (2, 3), a = 2, opening upward: (x - 2)2 = 8(y - 3).

(iii) By definition (x + 3)2 + (y - 1)2 = (x - 2y - 3)2/5, i.e. 4x2 + y2 + 4xy + 36x 22y + 41 = 0.

(iv) Vertex (3, 2), a = 2, focus to the left of the vertex, opening left: (y - 2)2 = -8(x 3). (v) Vertex (-1, 2), a = 2, focus below the vertex, opening downward: (x + 1)2 = -8(y - 2).

(vi) Vertex (0, 2), a = 2, opening right: (y - 2)2 = 8x. (vii) Focus (2, 1), a = 1, opening downward: (x - 2)2 = -4(y - 2).

(viii) Note: the printed data do not fix the position of the axis. With latus rectum 8, a = 2, and the vertex 2 units below the directrix y = 1, the general equation is (x - h)2 = -8(y + 1); with the axis taken as the y-axis (h = 0) this is x2 = -8(y + 1).

(ix) With axis y = 0, y2 = 4a(x - h): from the two points, 1 = 8a - 4ah and 4 = 44a 4ah, giving a = 1/12 and h = -1: 3y2 = x + 1.

Answer: (x) y = Ax2 + Bx + C through the three points gives C = 3, A = 5/3, B = -14/3: 5x2 - 14x - 3y + 9 = 0.

Q3. Find an equation of the parabola having its focus at the origin and directrix, parallel to the (i) x-axis (ii) y-axis.

(i) Let the directrix parallel to the x-axis be y = k. By definition, distance from P(x, y) to (0, 0) equals distance to the line: x2 + y2 = (y - k)2, i.e. x2 = -2ky + k2.

Answer: (ii) Let the directrix parallel to the y-axis be x = k. Then x2 + y2 = (x - k)2, i.e. y2 = -2kx + k2. (In particular, with the directrix at distance 2a from the focus, these are x2 = 4ay and y2 = 4ax up to the sign of the side on which the directrix lies.)

Q4. Show that an equation of the parabola with focus at (a cos(alpha), a sin(alpha)) and directrix x cos(alpha) + y sin(alpha) + a = 0 is (x sin(alpha) - y cos(alpha))2 = 4a(x cos(alpha) + y sin(alpha)).

By definition, PF2 = PM2: (x - a cos(alpha))2 + (y - a sin(alpha))2 = (x cos(alpha) + y sin(alpha) + a)2.

Expanding the left side gives x2 + y2 - 2a(x cos(alpha) + y sin(alpha)) + a2; expanding the right side gives x2 cos2(alpha) + y2 sin2(alpha) + 2xy sin(alpha) cos(alpha) + 2a(x cos(alpha) + y sin(alpha)) + a2.

Answer: subtracting gives x2 sin2(alpha) + y2 cos2(alpha) - 2xy sin(alpha) cos(alpha) = 4a(x cos(alpha) + y sin(alpha)), i.e. (x sin(alpha) - y cos(alpha))2 = 4a(x cos(alpha) + y sin(alpha)).

Q5. Show that the ordinate at any point P of the parabola is a mean proportional between the length of the latus rectum and the abscissa of P.

Let P = (at2, 2at) be a point on y2 = 4ax. Its ordinate is 2at and its abscissa is at2; the length of the latus rectum is 4a.

Answer: the mean proportional between 4a and at2 is sqrt(4a times at2) = 2at, which is the ordinate of P.

Q6. A comet has a parabolic orbit with the earth at the focus.

When the comet is 150,000 km from the earth, the line joining the comet and the earth makes an angle of 30 degrees with the axis of the parabola. How close will the comet come to the earth? For the parabola y2 = 4ax with focus (a, 0), the distance from the focus to a point P is r = x + a, and the angle condition gives y = r sin(30 degrees) = 75,000 km.

Then y2 = 4a(r - a) gives 75,0002 = 4a(150,000 - a), i.e. a2 - 150,000a + 1,406,250,000 = 0, so a = 10,048 km or a = 139,952 km.

Answer: the perihelion (closest approach) is a = approx. 10,048 km; the second root corresponds to the supplementary angle on the other side of the focus.

Q7. Find an equation of the parabola formed by the cables of a suspension bridge whose span is a m and the vertical height of the supporting towers is b m.

Take the vertex at the centre of the bridge on the road surface, with the axis vertical: x2 = 4Ay. The towers stand at x = + a/2 and x = - a/2 with height b, so (a/2)2 = 4Ab, giving 4A = a2/(4b).

Answer: x2 = (a2/(4b)) y, with y measured upward from the road surface at the centre of the span.

Q8. A parabolic arch has a 100 m base and height 25 m.

Find the height of the arch at the point 30 m from the centre of the base. Take the vertex at the top (0, 25) with the axis vertical, opening downward: x2 = -4a(y - 25). The base ends (+-50, 0) lie on the arch, so 2500 = 100a, giving a = 25.

At x = 30: 900 = -100(y - 25), so y - 25 = -9 and y = 16.

Answer: height of the arch 30 m from the centre is 16 m.

Q9. Show that tangent at any point P of a parabola makes equal angles with the line PF and the line through P parallel to the axis of the parabola, F being focus.

(These angles are called respectively angle of incidence and angle of reflection). Let P = (at2, 2at) on y2 = 4ax. The tangent at P is ty = x + at2, which meets the axis at T(-at2, 0).

Then TF = a + at2, and PF = at2 + a (distance from focus equals distance from directrix), so triangle TPF is isosceles with TF = PF.

Answer: hence the angle at T (equal, by parallel lines, to the angle between the tangent and the line through P parallel to the axis) equals the angle at P between PF and the tangent.

mcqs.q: Find the focus and directrix of the parabola y^2 = 8x.
mcqs.why: Compare with y^2 = 4ax: 4a = 8, so a = 2. Vertex is (0, 0); the parabola opens right, focus is (a, 0) = (2, 0) and directrix is x = -a = -2.

mcqs.q: Find the focus and directrix of the parabola x^2 = -16y.
mcqs.why: Compare with x^2 = -4ay: 4a = 16, so a = 4. The negative sign means it opens downward; vertex (0, 0), focus (0, -a) = (0, -4) and directrix y = a = 4.

mcqs.q: Find the focus of the parabola x^2 = 5y.
mcqs.why: Compare with x^2 = 4ay: 4a = 5, so a = 5/4. It opens upward, so the focus is (0, a) = (0, 5/4) and the directrix is y = -5/4.

mcqs.q: Find the directrix of the parabola y^2 = -12x.
mcqs.why: Compare with y^2 = -4ax: 4a = 12, so a = 3. It opens left, focus (-3, 0); the directrix is the vertical line x = +a = 3.

mcqs.q: Find the vertex and directrix of the parabola x^2 = 4(y - 1).
mcqs.why: In the form x^2 = 4a(y - k) with a = 1 and k = 1: vertex (0, 1). It opens upward, focus (0, 1 + 1) = (0, 2), and directrix y = k - a = 1 - 1 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the focus of the parabola y^2 = -8(x - 3).
mcqs.why: In the form y^2 = -4a(x - h): 4a = 8, a = 2, vertex (3, 0). It opens left, so the focus is (h - a, 0) = (3 - 2, 0) = (1, 0) and the directrix is x = 5.

mcqs.q: Find the vertex of the parabola (x - 1)^2 = 8(y + 2).
mcqs.why: In the form (x - h)^2 = 4a(y - k) the vertex is (h, k) = (1, -2). Here 4a = 8, a = 2, so the focus is (1, -2 + 2) = (1, 0) and the directrix is y = -4.

mcqs.q: Find the focus of the parabola y = 6x^2 - 1.
mcqs.why: Rewrite: x^2 = (1/6)(y + 1), so 4a = 1/6 and a = 1/24. Vertex is (0, -1); opening upward, the focus is (0, -1 + 1/24) = (0, -23/24) and the directrix is y = -25/24.

mcqs.q: The equation x + 8 - y^2 + 2y = 0 represents a parabola. Find its vertex and focus.
mcqs.why: Rearrange: y^2 - 2y = x + 8; completing the square, (y - 1)^2 = x + 9. So vertex is (-9, 1), 4a = 1 gives a = 1/4, it opens right, focus = (-9 + 1/4, 1) = (-35/4, 1), directrix x = -37/4.

mcqs.q: A parabolic arch has a 100 m base and height 25 m. What is the height of the arch at a point 30 m from the centre of the base?
mcqs.why: Take the vertex at the top (0, 25), opening downward: x^2 = -4a(y - 25). The base ends (+/-50, 0) lie on it: 2500 = -4a(0 - 25) = 100a, so a = 25. At x = 30: 900 = -100(y - 25), so y - 25 = -9 and y = 16 m.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.5 — Ellipse
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find an equation of the ellipse with given data and sketch its graph: (i) Foci (+-3, 0) and minor axis of length 10 (ii) Foci (0, -1) and (0, -5) and major axis of length 6 (iii) Foci (+-3 sqrt(3), 0) and vertices (+-6, 0) (iv) Vertices (-1, 1), (5, 1); foci (4, 1) and (0, 1) (v) Foci (+-sqrt(5), 0) and passing through the point (3/2, sqrt(3)) (vi) Vertices (0, +-5), eccentricity 3/5 (vii) Centre (0, 0), focus (0, -3), vertex (0, 4) (viii) Centre (2, 2), major axis parallel to y-axis and of length 8 units, minor axis parallel to x-axis and of length 6 units (ix) Centre (0, 0), symmetric with respect to both the axes and passing through the points (2, 3) and (6, 1) (x) Centre (0, 0), major axis horizontal, the points (3, 1), (4, 0) lie on the graph.

(i) c = 3, b = 5, a2 = 25 + 9 = 34: x2/34 + y2/25 = 1. (ii) Centre (0, -3), c = 2, a = 3, b2 = 5, major axis vertical: x2/5 + (y + 3)2/9 = 1.

(iii) a = 6, c = 3 sqrt(3), b2 = 36 - 27 = 9: x2/36 + y2/9 = 1. (iv) Centre (2, 1), a = 3, c = 2, b2 = 5: (x - 2)2/9 + (y - 1)2/5 = 1.

(v) c = sqrt(5); putting (3/2, sqrt(3)) in x2/a2 + y2/(a2 - 5) = 1 gives a2 = 9 (the other root 5/4 is rejected since a2 > c2): x2/9 + y2/4 = 1.

(vi) a = 5, e = 3/5, c = 3, b2 = 16, major axis vertical: x2/16 + y2/25 = 1. (vii) a = 4, c = 3, b2 = 7, major axis vertical: x2/7 + y2/16 = 1.

(viii) Centre (2, 2), a = 4, b = 3: (x - 2)2/9 + (y - 2)2/16 = 1. (ix) With x2/A + y2/B = 1 through (2, 3) and (6, 1): A = 40, B = 10: x2/40 + y2/10 = 1.

Answer: (x) (4, 0) is a vertex, so a = 4; (3, 1) gives 9/16 + 1/b2 = 1, so b2 = 16/7: x2 + 7y2 = 16.

Q2. Find the centre, foci, eccentricity, vertices and directrices of the ellipse, whose equation is given: (i) x2 + 4y2 = 16 (ii) 9x2 + y2 = 18 (iii) 25x2 + 9y2 = 225 (iv) (2x - 1)2/4 + (y + 2)2/16 = 1 (v) x2 + 16x + 4y2 - 16y + 76 = 0 (vi) 25x2 + 4y2 250x - 16y + 541 = 0.

(i) x2/16 + y2/4 = 1: centre (0, 0), a = 4, b = 2, c = 2 sqrt(3), e = sqrt(3)/2, vertices (+-4, 0), foci (+-2 sqrt(3), 0), directrices x = +-8 sqrt(3)/3.

(ii) x2/2 + y2/18 = 1: centre (0, 0), a = 3 sqrt(2), b = sqrt(2), c = 4, e = 2 sqrt(2)/3, vertices (0, +-3 sqrt(2)), foci (0, +-4), directrices y = +-9/2.

(iii) x2/9 + y2/25 = 1: centre (0, 0), a = 5, b = 3, c = 4, e = 4/5, vertices (0, +-5), foci (0, +-4), directrices y = +-25/4.

(iv) (x - 1/2)2 + (y + 2)2/4 = 1: centre (1/2, -2), a = 2, b = 1, c = sqrt(3), e = sqrt(3)/2, vertices (1/2, 0), (1/2, -4), foci (1/2, -2 +- sqrt(3)), directrices y = -2 +4/sqrt(3).

(v) (x + 8)2/4 + (y - 2)2 = 1: centre (-8, 2), a = 2, b = 1, c = sqrt(3), e = sqrt(3)/2, vertices (-6, 2), (-10, 2), foci (-8 +- sqrt(3), 2), directrices x = -8 +- 4/sqrt(3).

Answer: (vi) (x - 5)2/4 + (y - 2)2/25 = 1: centre (5, 2), a = 5, b = 2, c = sqrt(21), e = sqrt(21)/5, vertices (5, 7), (5, -3), foci (5, 2 +- sqrt(21)), directrices y = 2 +25/sqrt(21).

Q3. Let a be a positive number and 0 < c < a.

Let F(-c, 0) and F'(c, 0) be two given points. Prove that the locus of points P(x, y) such that |PF| + |PF'| = 2a, is an ellipse. The condition is sqrt((x + c)2 + y2) + sqrt((x - c)2 + y2) = 2a, i.e. sqrt((x + c)2 + y2) = 2a - sqrt((x - c)2 + y2).

Squaring and simplifying gives (a2 - c2)x2 + a2y2 = a2(a2 - c2).

Answer: since 0 < c < a, b2 = a2 - c2 > 0, and dividing gives x2/a2 + y2/b2 = 1, an ellipse with foci (+-c, 0).

Q4. Use problem 3 to find equation of the ellipse as locus of points P(x, y) such that the sum of the distances from P to the points (0, 0) and (1, 1) is 2.

The foci are (0, 0) and (1, 1), so the centre is (1/2, 1/2), 2c = sqrt(2) (c = 1/sqrt(2)) and 2a = 2 (a = 1); hence b2 = 1 - 1/2 = 1/2.

With u = (x + y - 1)/sqrt(2) along the major axis and v = (x - y)/sqrt(2) perpendicular to it, the equation is u2 + v2/(1/2) = 1.

Answer: (x + y - 1)2 + 2(x - y)2 = 2, i.e. 3x2 - 2xy + 3y2 - 2x - 2y - 1 = 0.

Q5. Prove that the latus rectum of the ellipse x2/a2 + y2/b2 = 1 is 2b2/a.

The latus rectum is the chord through a focus perpendicular to the major axis; take the focus (ae, 0), so the chord is x = ae.

Putting x = ae in the ellipse gives y2/b2 = 1 - e2 = b2/a2, so y = +-b2/a.

Answer: the length of the chord is 2b2/a.

Q6. The major axis of an ellipse in standard form lies along the x-axis and has length 4 sqrt(2).

The distance between the foci equals the length of the minor axis. Write an equation of the ellipse. Major axis 2a = 4 sqrt(2) gives a = 2 sqrt(2). Distance between foci 2c equals minor axis 2b, so c = b.

Then a2 = b2 + c2 = 2b2 gives b2 = a2/2 = 4.

Answer: x2/8 + y2/4 = 1.

Q7. An asteroid has elliptic orbit with the sun at one focus.

Its distance from the sun ranges from 17 million miles to 183 million miles. Write an equation of the orbit of the asteroid. Perihelion a - c = 17 and aphelion a + c = 183 (million miles), so a = 100 and c = 83.

Then b2 = a2 - c2 = 10,000 - 6,889 = 3,111.

Answer: with the centre at the origin, x2/10,000 + y2/3,111 = 1 (distances in million miles).

Q8. An arch in the shape of a semi-ellipse is 90m wide at the base and 30m high at the centre.

At what distance from the centre is the arch 20 sqrt(2) m high?

Take the semi-ellipse x2/452 + y2/302 = 1 with y >= 0 (a = 45, b = 30).

At height y = 20 sqrt(2): x2/2025 = 1 - 800/900 = 1/9, so x2 = 225 and x = 15.

Answer: the arch is 20 sqrt(2) m high at a distance of 15 m from the centre.

Q9. The moon orbits the earth in an elliptic path with earth at one focus.

The major and minor axes of the orbit are 768,806 km and 767,746 km respectively. Find the greatest and least distances (in Astronomy called the apogee and perigee respectively) of the moon from the earth. Semi-axes: a = 384,403 km, b = 383,873 km. Then c = sqrt(a2 - b2) = sqrt(530 times 768,276) = approx. 20,179 km.

Greatest distance (apogee) = a + c = approx. 404,582 km; least distance (perigee) = a - c = approx. 364,224 km.

Answer: apogee approx. 404,582 km, perigee approx. 364,224 km.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the ellipse with foci (+/-3, 0) and minor axis of length 10.
mcqs.why: c = 3 and minor axis 2b = 10 gives b = 5. Then a^2 = b^2 + c^2 = 25 + 9 = 34. The foci are on the x-axis, so the equation is x^2/34 + y^2/25 = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the ellipse with foci (0, -1) and (0, -5) and major axis of length 6.
mcqs.why: Centre is the midpoint of the foci: (0, -3). c = half the focal distance = 2; major axis 2a = 6 gives a = 3. b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 9 - 4 = 5. The major axis is vertical, so the equation is x^2/5 + (y + 3)^2/9 = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the ellipse with foci (+/-3 sqrt(3), 0) and vertices (+/-6, 0).
mcqs.why: a = 6 (vertices) and c = 3 sqrt(3) (foci). b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 36 - 27 = 9. Major axis horizontal: x^2/36 + y^2/9 = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the ellipse with vertices (-1, 1), (5, 1) and foci (4, 1) and (0, 1).
mcqs.why: Centre is the midpoint (2, 1). a = half the vertex distance = 3, c = half the focal distance = 2. b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 9 - 4 = 5. Major axis horizontal: (x - 2)^2/9 + (y - 1)^2/5 = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the ellipse with foci (+/-sqrt(5), 0) passing through (3/2, sqrt(3)).
mcqs.why: c^2 = 5, so b^2 = a^2 - 5. Substituting (3/2, sqrt(3)) into x^2/a^2 + y^2/(a^2 - 5) = 1 gives a^2 = 9 (the other root 5/4 is rejected because a^2 must exceed c^2 = 5). Then b^2 = 9 - 5 = 4, giving x^2/9 + y^2/4 = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the ellipse with vertices (0, +/-5) and eccentricity 3/5.
mcqs.why: a = 5 and e = 3/5, so c = a e = 3. b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 25 - 9 = 16. The vertices are on the y-axis, so the major axis is vertical: x^2/16 + y^2/25 = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the eccentricity and foci of the ellipse x^2 + 4y^2 = 16.
mcqs.why: Divide by 16: x^2/16 + y^2/4 = 1, so a = 4, b = 2. c = sqrt(a^2 - b^2) = sqrt(16 - 4) = 2 sqrt(3). e = c/a = 2 sqrt(3)/4 = sqrt(3)/2, foci (+/-2 sqrt(3), 0), directrices x = +/-8 sqrt(3)/3.

mcqs.q: Find the vertices and foci of the ellipse 25x^2 + 9y^2 = 225.
mcqs.why: Divide by 225: x^2/9 + y^2/25 = 1, so a = 5 (vertical), b = 3. c = sqrt(25 - 9) = 4, e = 4/5. Vertices (0, +/-5), foci (0, +/-4), directrices y = +/-25/4.

mcqs.q: The length of the latus rectum of the ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 is:
mcqs.why: The latus rectum is the chord through a focus perpendicular to the major axis, x = a e. Putting x = a e in the ellipse: y^2/b^2 = 1 - e^2 = b^2/a^2, so y = +/-b^2/a. The chord length is the difference, 2b^2/a.

mcqs.q: An asteroid's elliptic orbit has the sun at one focus; its distance from the sun ranges from 17 to 183 million miles. Its orbit equation (centre at origin, million miles) is:

lessons.title: Exercise 6.6 — Hyperbola
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find an equation of the hyperbola with the given data.

Sketch the graph of each. (i) Centre (0, 0), focus (6, 0), vertex (4, 0) (ii) Foci (+-5, 0), vertex (3, 0) (iii) Foci (2 +- 5 sqrt(2), -7), length of the transverse axis 10 (iv) Foci (0, +-6), e = 2 (v) Foci (0, +-9), directrices y = +-4 (vi) Centre (2, 2), horizontal transverse axis of length 6 and eccentricity e = 2 (vii) Vertices (2, +-3), (0, 5) lies on the curve (viii) Foci (5, -2), (5, 4) and one vertex (5, 3). (i) a = 4, c = 6, b2 = 36 - 16 = 20: x2/16 - y2/20 = 1. (ii) a = 3, c = 5, b2 = 16: x2/9

- y2/16 = 1.

(iii) Centre (2, -7), c = 5 sqrt(2), a = 5, b2 = 50 - 25 = 25: (x - 2)2/25 - (y + 7)2/25 = 1.

(iv) c = 6, a = c/e = 3, b2 = 36 - 9 = 27, transverse axis vertical: y2/9 - x2/27 = 1.

(v) c = 9 and a/e = 4 with ae = 9 give a2 = 36, so a = 6, e = 3/2, b2 = 45: y2/36 x2/45 = 1.

(vi) Centre (2, 2), a = 3, c = ae = 6, b2 = 27: (x - 2)2/9 - (y - 2)2/27 = 1.

(vii) Centre (2, 0), a = 3, transverse axis vertical; (0, 5) on y2/9 - (x - 2)2/b2 = 1 gives 25/9 - 4/b2 = 1, so b2 = 9/4: y2 - 4(x - 2)2 = 9.

Answer: (viii) Centre (5, 1), c = 3, a = 2, b2 = 5, transverse axis vertical: (y - 1)2/4 (x - 5)2/5 = 1.

Q2. Find the centre, foci, eccentricity, vertices and equations of directrices of each of the following: (i) x2 - y2 = 9 (ii) x2/4 - y2/9 = 1 (iii) y2/16 - x2/9 = 1 (iv) y2/4 - x2 = 1 (v) (x - 1)2/2 - (y - 1)2/9 = 1 (vi) (y + 2)2/9 - (x - 2)2/16 = 1 (vii) 9x2 - 12x - y2 2y + 2 = 0 (viii) 4y2 + 12y - x2 + 4x + 1 = 0 (ix) x2 - y2 + 8x - 2y - 10 = 0 (x) 9x2 y2 - 36x - 6y + 18 = 0.

(i) x2/9 - y2/9 = 1: centre (0, 0), a = 3, b = 3, c = 3 sqrt(2), e = sqrt(2), vertices (+-3, 0), foci (+-3 sqrt(2), 0), directrices x = +-3/sqrt(2).

(ii) a = 2, b = 3, c = sqrt(13), e = sqrt(13)/2, vertices (+-2, 0), foci (+-sqrt(13), 0), directrices x = +-4/sqrt(13).

(iii) a = 4, b = 3, c = 5, e = 5/4, vertices (0, +-4), foci (0, +-5), directrices y = +-16/5.

(iv) a = 2, b = 1, c = sqrt(5), e = sqrt(5)/2, vertices (0, +-2), foci (0, +-sqrt(5)), directrices y = +-8/sqrt(5).

(v) Centre (1, 1), a = sqrt(2), b = 3, c = sqrt(11), e = sqrt(22)/2, vertices (1 +sqrt(2), 1), foci (1 +- sqrt(11), 1), directrices x = 1 +- 2/sqrt(11).

(vi) Centre (2, -2), a = 3, b = 4, c = 5, e = 5/3, vertices (2, 1), (2, -5), foci (2, 3), (2, -7), directrices y = -1/5, y = -19/5.

(vii) (x - 2/3)2/(1/9) - (y + 1)2 = 1: centre (2/3, -1), a = 1/3, b = 1, c = sqrt(10)/3, e = sqrt(10), vertices (1, -1), (1/3, -1), foci (2/3 +- sqrt(10)/3, -1), directrices x = 2/3 +- 1/(3 sqrt(10)).

(viii) (y + 3/2)2 - (x - 2)2/4 = 1: centre (2, -3/2), a = 1, b = 2, c = sqrt(5), e = sqrt(5), vertices (2, -1/2), (2, -5/2), foci (2, -3/2 +- sqrt(5)), directrices y = -3/2 +1/sqrt(5).

(ix) (x + 4)2/25 - (y + 1)2/25 = 1: centre (-4, -1), a = 5, b = 5, c = 5 sqrt(2), e = sqrt(2), vertices (1, -1), (-9, -1), foci (-4 +- 5 sqrt(2), -1), directrices x = -4 +5/sqrt(2).

Answer: (x) (x - 2)2 - (y + 3)2/9 = 1: centre (2, -3), a = 1, b = 3, c = sqrt(10), e = sqrt(10), vertices (3, -3), (1, -3), foci (2 +- sqrt(10), -3), directrices x = 2 +1/sqrt(10).

Q3. Let 0 < a < c and F'(-c, 0), F(c, 0) be two fixed points.

Show that the set of points P(x, y) such that |PF| - |PF'| = 2a, is the hyperbola x2/a2 - y2/(c2 - a2) = 1. (F, F' are foci of the hyperbola.) The condition is |sqrt((x - c)2 + y2) - sqrt((x + c)2 + y2)| = 2a; take the positive branch sqrt((x - c)2 + y2) = 2a + sqrt((x + c)2 + y2).

Squaring and simplifying twice gives (c2 - a2)x2 - a2y2 = a2(c2 - a2).

Answer: since c > a, b2 = c2 - a2 > 0, and dividing gives x2/a2 - y2/b2 = 1, a hyperbola with foci (+-c, 0).

Q4. Using Problem 3, find an equation of the hyperbola with foci (-5, -5) and (5, 5), vertices (-3 sqrt(2), -3 sqrt(2)) and (3 sqrt(2), 3 sqrt(2)).

Centre (0, 0), transverse axis along y = x; c = distance to a focus = 5 sqrt(2), a = distance to a vertex = 6, so b2 = 50 - 36 = 14.

With u = (x + y)/sqrt(2) along the axis and v = (x - y)/sqrt(2) perpendicular, u2/36 v2/14 = 1.

Answer: (x + y)2/72 - (x - y)2/28 = 1, i.e. 11x2 - 50xy + 11y2 + 504 = 0.

Q5. For any point on a hyperbola the difference of its distances from the points (2, 2) and (10, 2) is 6.

Find an equation of the hyperbola. The points are the foci: centre (6, 2), 2c = 8 so c = 4, and 2a = 6 so a = 3; hence b2

= 16 - 9 = 7.

Answer: (x - 6)2/9 - (y - 2)2/7 = 1.

Q6. Two listening posts hear the sound of an enemy gun.

The difference in time is one second. If the listening posts are 1400 feet apart, write an equation of the hyperbola passing through the position of the enemy gun. (Sound travels at 1080 ft/sec). The difference of distances from the two posts is 1080 times 1 = 1080 feet, so 2a = 1080 and a = 540; the posts are the foci, so 2c = 1400 and c = 700.

Then b2 = 7002 - 5402 = 198,400.

Answer: with the posts at (+-700, 0), x2/291,600 - y2/198,400 = 1 (distances in feet).

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the hyperbola with centre (0, 0), focus (6, 0) and vertex (4, 0).
mcqs.why: a = 4 (vertex) and c = 6 (focus). b^2 = c^2 - a^2 = 36 - 16 = 20. Transverse axis horizontal: x^2/16 - y^2/20 = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the hyperbola with foci (+/-5, 0) and vertex (3, 0).
Find the equation of the hyperbola with foci (0, +/-6) and eccentricity e = 2.
mcqs.why: c = 6 and a = c/e = 6/2 = 3. b^2 = c^2 - a^2 = 36 - 9 = 27. The foci are on the y-axis, so the transverse axis is vertical: y^2/9 - x^2/27 = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the eccentricity of the hyperbola x^2 - y^2 = 9.
mcqs.why: Write x^2/9 - y^2/9 = 1: a = 3, b = 3. c = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) = sqrt(18) = 3 sqrt(2). e = c/a = 3 sqrt(2)/3 = sqrt(2). Vertices (+/-3, 0), foci (+/-3 sqrt(2), 0), directrices x = +/-3/sqrt(2).

mcqs.q: Find the foci and directrices of the hyperbola x^2/4 - y^2/9 = 1.
mcqs.why: a = 2, b = 3, so c = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) = sqrt(4 + 9) = sqrt(13) and e = c/a = sqrt(13)/2. Foci (+/-sqrt(13), 0); directrices x = +/-a/e = +/-2/(sqrt(13)/2) = +/-4/sqrt(13). Vertices (+/-2, 0).

mcqs.q: Find the vertices and eccentricity of the hyperbola y^2/16 - x^2/9 = 1.
mcqs.why: a = 4 (along the y-axis), b = 3. c = sqrt(16 + 9) = 5, e = c/a = 5/4. Vertices (0, +/-4), foci (0, +/-5), directrices y = +/-16/5.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of the hyperbola with centre (2, 2), horizontal transverse axis of length 6 and eccentricity 2.
mcqs.why: Transverse axis 2a = 6 gives a = 3. c = a e = 3 x 2 = 6. b^2 = c^2 - a^2 = 36 - 9 = 27. With centre (2, 2) and horizontal transverse axis: (x - 2)^2/9 - (y - 2)^2/27 = 1.

mcqs.q: A hyperbola has foci (5, -2) and (5, 4) and one vertex (5, 3). Find its centre, a and b^2.
mcqs.why: Centre is the midpoint of the foci: (5, (-2 + 4)/2) = (5, 1). c = half the focal distance = 3. a = distance from centre to vertex (5, 3) = 2. b^2 = c^2 - a^2 = 9 - 4 = 5, giving (y - 1)^2/4 - (x - 5)^2/5 = 1.

mcqs.q: For any point on a hyperbola the difference of its distances from (2, 2) and (10, 2) is 6. Find its equation.
mcqs.why: The two points are the foci: centre is their midpoint (6, 2), 2c = 8 so c = 4, and 2a = 6 (the constant difference) so a = 3. b^2 = c^2 - a^2 = 16 - 9 = 7. Hence (x - 6)^2/9 - (y - 2)^2/7 = 1.

mcqs.q: Two listening posts 1400 feet apart hear a gun with a time difference of 1 second (sound travels at 1080 ft/sec). For the hyperbola through the gun's position, a and b^2 are:
mcqs.why: Difference of distances = 1080 x 1 = 1080 ft, so 2a = 1080 and a = 540. The posts are the foci: 2c = 1400, c = 700. b^2 = c^2 - a^2 = 490000 - 291600 = 198400, giving x^2/291600 - y^2/198400 = 1 with the posts at (+/-700, 0).

lessons.title: Exercise 6.7 — Tangents and normals to conics
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find equations of the tangent and normal to each of the following at the indicated point: (i) y2 = 4ax at (a t2, 2a t) (ii) x2/a2 + y2/b2 = 1 at (a cos(theta), b sin(theta)) (iii) x2/a2 - y2/b2 = 1 at (a sec(theta), b tan(theta)).

(i) Tangent: y(2at) = 2a(x + at2), i.e. ty = x + at2. Normal (slope -t): y - 2at = -t(x at2).

(ii) Tangent: x cos(theta)/a + y sin(theta)/b = 1. Normal: y - b sin(theta) = (a sin(theta)/(b cos(theta)))(x - a cos(theta)), i.e. a x sin(theta) - b y cos(theta) = (a2 b2) sin(theta) cos(theta).

Answer: (iii) Tangent: x sec(theta)/a - y tan(theta)/b = 1. Normal: y - b tan(theta) = (-a sin(theta)/b)(x - a sec(theta)).

Q2. Write equation of the tangent to the given conic at the indicated point (i) 3x2 = -16y at the points whose ordinate is -3 (ii) 3x2 - 7y2 = 20 at the points where y = -1 (iii) 3x2 - 7y2 + 2x - y - 48 = 0 at the point where x = 4.

(i) Ordinate -3 gives 3x2 = 48, so x = +-4. Tangents: at (4, -3): x + 2y + 6 = 0; at (-4, -3): x - 2y - 6 = 0.

(ii) y = -1 gives 3x2 = 27, so x = +-3. Tangents: at (3, -1): 9x + 7y = 20; at (-3, -1): -9x + 7y = 20.

Answer: (iii) x = 4 gives 7y2 + y - 8 = 0, so y = 1 or y = -8/7. Tangents: at (4, 1): 26x - 15y - 89 = 0; at (4, -8/7): 182x + 105y - 608 = 0.

Q3. Find equations of the tangents to each of the following through the given point: (i) x2 + y2 = 25 through (7, -1) (ii) y2 = 12x through (1, 4) (iii) x2 - 2y2 = 2 through (1, -2).

(i) Chord of contact: 7x - y = 25; with the circle this gives points of contact (3, -4) and (4, 3). Tangents: 3x - 4y = 25 and 4x + 3y = 25.

(ii) Chord of contact: 2y = 3x + 3; with the parabola this gives points of contact (3, 6) and (1/3, 2). Tangents: y = x + 3 and y = 3x + 1.

Answer: (iii) Chord of contact: x + 4y = 2; with the hyperbola this gives points of contact (-2, 1) and (10/7, 1/7). Tangents: x + y + 1 = 0 and 5x - y - 7 = 0.

Q4. Find equations of the normals to the parabola y2 = 8x which are parallel to the line 2x + 3y = 10.

Here a = 2. The normal at (2t2, 4t) has slope -t; parallel to 2x + 3y = 10 (slope -2/3) requires t = 2/3.

The point is (8/9, 8/3), and the normal is y - 8/3 = -(2/3)(x - 8/9).

Answer: 18x + 27y - 88 = 0.

Q5. Find equations of the tangents to the ellipse x2/4 + y2 = 1 which are parallel to the line 2x - 4y + 5 = 0.

The line has slope 1/2. A tangent of slope m to x2/4 + y2 = 1 is y = mx +- sqrt(4m2 + 1).

With m = 1/2: y = (1/2)x +- sqrt(2).

Answer: x - 2y + 2 sqrt(2) = 0 and x - 2y - 2 sqrt(2) = 0.

Q6. Find equations of the tangents to the conic 9x2 - 4y2 = 36 parallel to 5x - 2y + 7 = 0.

The conic is x2/4 - y2/9 = 1; the line has slope 5/2. A tangent of slope m is y = mx +- sqrt(4m2 - 9).

With m = 5/2: y = (5/2)x +- 4.

Answer: 5x - 2y + 8 = 0 and 5x - 2y - 8 = 0.

Q7. Find equations of the common tangents to the given conics (i) x2 = 80y and x2 + y2 = 81 (ii) y2 = 16x and x2 = 2y.

(i) A tangent of slope m to x2 = 80y is y = mx - 20m2; its distance from the origin must equal 9, giving 400m4 = 81(1 + m2), so m2 = 9/16 and m = +-3/4.

Tangents: y = (3/4)x - 45/4 and y = -(3/4)x - 45/4.

Answer: (ii) A tangent of slope m to y2 = 16x is y = mx + 4/m, and to x2 = 2y is y = mx - (1/2)m2; equating gives m3 = -8, so m = -2 and the tangent is y = -2x - 2. Also y = 0 is tangent to both conics at the origin.

Q8. Find the points of intersection of the given conics (i) x2/18 + y2/8 = 1 and x2/3 y2/3 = 1 (ii) x2 + y2 = 8 and x2 - y2 = 1 (iii) 3x2 - 4y2 = 12 and 3y2 - 2x2 = 7 (iv) 3x2 + 5y2 = 60 and 9x2 + y2 = 124 (v) 4x2 + y2 = 16 and x2 + y2 + y + 8 = 0.

(i) From x2 - y2 = 3 and 4x2 + 9y2 = 72: 13x2 = 99, so the four points are (+-3 sqrt(11/13), +-2 sqrt(15/13)).

(ii) Adding and subtracting: 2x2 = 9 and 2y2 = 7, so the four points are (+-3/sqrt(2), +-sqrt(7/2)).

(iii) Solving gives x2 = 64 and y2 = 45, so the four points are (+-8, +-3 sqrt(5)).

(iv) Solving gives y2 = 4 and x2 = 40/3, so the four points are (+-2 sqrt(10/3), +-2).

Answer: (v) Subtracting gives y = 3x2 - 24; substituting gives 9x4 - 140x2 + 560 = 0, whose discriminant is negative, so the conics have no real points of intersection.

mcqs.q: Find the tangent to the parabola y^2 = 4ax at the point (a t^2, 2a t).
mcqs.why: Tangent T = 0: y y1 = 2a(x + x1) with (x1, y1) = (a t^2, 2a t) gives y(2a t) = 2a(x + a t^2); dividing by 2a: t y = x + a t^2. (The normal there has slope -t.)

mcqs.q: Find the tangent to the ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 at (a cos(theta), b sin(theta)).
options: a x cos(theta) + b y sin(theta) = 1
mcqs.why: Tangent T = 0: x x1/a^2 + y y1/b^2 = 1. With x1 = a cos(theta), y1 = b sin(theta): x (a cos(theta))/a^2 + y (b sin(theta))/b^2 = x cos(theta)/a + y sin(theta)/b = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the tangent to the hyperbola x^2/a^2 - y^2/b^2 = 1 at (a sec(theta), b tan(theta)).
mcqs.why: Tangent T = 0: x x1/a^2 - y y1/b^2 = 1. With x1 = a sec(theta), y1 = b tan(theta): x sec(theta)/a - y tan(theta)/b = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the tangents to the circle x^2 + y^2 = 25 drawn through (7, -1).
mcqs.why: Chord of contact from (7, -1): 7x - y = 25. Solving with x^2 + y^2 = 25 gives the points of contact (3, -4) and (4, 3). Tangents by T = 0: 3x - 4y = 25 (at (3, -4): 9 + 16 = 25) and 4x + 3y = 25 (at (4, 3): 16 + 9 = 25).

mcqs.q: Find the tangents to the parabola y^2 = 12x drawn through (1, 4).
mcqs.why: Here 4a = 12, a = 3. Chord of contact from (1, 4): y(4) = 6(x + 1), i.e. 2y = 3x + 3; solving with y^2 = 12x gives points of contact (3, 6) and (1/3, 2). Tangent at (3, 6): 6y = 6(x + 3), i.e. y = x + 3. Tangent at (1/3, 2): 2y = 6(x + 1/3), i.e. y = 3x + 1.

mcqs.q: Find the normal to the parabola y^2 = 8x which is parallel to the line 2x + 3y = 10.
mcqs.why: Here a = 2, so the normal at (2t^2, 4t) has slope -t. The line 2x + 3y = 10 has slope -2/3, so t = 2/3 and the point is (2(4/9), 4(2/3)) = (8/9, 8/3). Normal: y - 8/3 = -(2/3)(x - 8/9); multiplying by 27: 27y - 72 = -18x + 16, i.e. 18x + 27y - 88 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the tangents to the ellipse x^2/4 + y^2 = 1 parallel to the line 2x - 4y + 5 = 0.
mcqs.why: The line has slope 1/2. A tangent of slope m to x^2/4 + y^2 = 1 is y = m x +/- sqrt(4m^2 + 1). With m = 1/2: y = (1/2)x +/- sqrt(2). Multiplying by 2 and rearranging: x - 2y + 2 sqrt(2) = 0 and x - 2y - 2 sqrt(2) = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the tangents to the conic 9x^2 - 4y^2 = 36 parallel to 5x - 2y + 7 = 0.
mcqs.why: The conic is x^2/4 - y^2/9 = 1 and the line has slope 5/2. A tangent of slope m is y = m x +/- sqrt(4m^2 - 9). With m = 5/2: sqrt(25 - 9) = 4, so y = (5/2)x +/- 4, i.e. 5x - 2y + 8 = 0 and 5x - 2y - 8 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the common tangents to the conics y^2 = 16x and x^2 = 2y.
mcqs.why: A tangent of slope m to y^2 = 16x is y = m x + 4/m, and to x^2 = 2y is y = m x - (1/2)m^2. Equating intercepts: 4/m = -(1/2)m^2, so m^3 = -8, m = -2, giving y = -2x - 2. Also y = 0 is tangent to both conics at the origin.

mcqs.q: Find the points of intersection of the conics x^2 + y^2 = 8 and x^2 - y^2 = 1.
mcqs.why: Adding the equations: 2x^2 = 9, so x^2 = 9/2, x = +/-3/sqrt(2). Subtracting: 2y^2 = 7, so y^2 = 7/2, y = +/-sqrt(7/2). The four points are (+/-3/sqrt(2), +/-sqrt(7/2)).

lessons.title: Exercise 6.8 — Translation and rotation of axes
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find an equation of each of the following with respect to new parallel axes obtained by shifting the origin to the indicated point: (i) x2 + 16y - 16 = 0, O'(0, 1) (ii) 4x2 + y2 + 16x - 10y + 37 = 0, O'(2, 5) (iii) 9x2 + 4x2 + 18x - 16y - 11 = 0, O'(-1, 2) (iv) x2 - y2 + 4x + 8y - 11 = 0, O'(-2, 4) (v) 9x2 - 4y2 + 36x + 8y - 4 = 0, O'(2, 1).

(Print note for (iii): as printed in this copy the equation reads 9x2 + 4x2, i.e. 13x2; solved as printed below. If the second term were the misprint for 4y2, the shifted equation would be the clean 9X2 + 4Y2 = 36.) (i) x = X, y = Y + 1: X2 + 16Y = 0. (ii) x = X + 2, y = Y + 5: 4X2 + Y2 + 32X + 60 = 0.

(iii) As printed: x = X - 1, y = Y + 2 in 13x2 + 18x - 16y - 11 = 0 gives 13X2 - 8X 16Y - 48 = 0.

(iv) x = X - 2, y = Y + 4: X2 - Y2 + 1 = 0.

Answer: (v) x = X + 2, y = Y + 1: 9X2 - 4Y2 + 72X + 108 = 0.

Q2. Find coordinates of the new origin (axes remaining parallel) so that first degree terms are removed from the transformed equation of each of the following.

Also find the transformed equation: (i) 3x2 - 2y2 + 24x + 12y + 24 = 0 (ii) 25x2 + 9y2 + 50x - 36y - 164 = 0 (iii) x2 - y2 - 6x + 2y + 7 = 0. (i) 3(x + 4)2 - 2(y - 3)2 = 6: new origin (-4, 3), transformed equation 3X2 - 2Y2 = 6.

(ii) 25(x + 1)2 + 9(y - 2)2 = 225: new origin (-1, 2), transformed equation 25X2 + 9Y2 = 225.

Answer: (iii) (x - 3)2 - (y - 1)2 = 1: new origin (3, 1), transformed equation X2 - Y2 = 1.

Q3. In each of the following, find an equation referred to the new axes obtained by rotation of axes about the origin through the given angle: (i) xy = 1, theta = 45 degrees (ii) 7x2 - 8xy + y2 - 9 = 0, theta = arctan 2 (iii) 9x2 + 12xy + 4y2 - x - y = 0, theta = arctan(2/3) (iv) x2 - 2xy + y2 - 2 sqrt(2) x - 2 sqrt(2) y + 2 = 0, theta = 45 degrees.

(i) With x = (X - Y)/sqrt(2), y = (X + Y)/sqrt(2): (X2 - Y2)/2 = 1, i.e. X2 - Y2 = 2.

(ii) With cos(theta) = 1/sqrt(5), sin(theta) = 2/sqrt(5): the XY term cancels and -X2 + 9Y2 - 9 = 0.

(iii) With cos(theta) = 3/sqrt(13), sin(theta) = 2/sqrt(13): 3x + 2y = sqrt(13) X, so 13X2 - (5X + Y)/sqrt(13) = 0, i.e. 13 sqrt(13) X2 - 5X - Y = 0.

Answer: (iv) x - y = -sqrt(2) Y and x + y = sqrt(2) X, so 2Y2 - 4X + 2 = 0, i.e. Y2 - 2X + 1 = 0.

Q4. Find measure of the angle through which the axes be rotated so that the product term XY is removed from the transformed equation.

Also find the transformed equation: (i) 2x2 + 6xy + 10y2 - 11 = 0 (ii) xy + 4x - 3y - 10 = 0 (iii) 5x2 - 6xy + 5y2 - 8 = 0. (i) tan(2 theta) = 6/(2 - 10) = -3/4, so 2 theta = 143.13 degrees and theta = 71.57 degrees; transformed coefficients 37/5 and 23/5 give 37X2 + 23Y2 = 55.

(ii) tan(2 theta) is infinite, so theta = 45 degrees; transformed equation X2 - Y2 + sqrt(2) X - 7 sqrt(2) Y - 20 = 0.

Answer: (iii) tan(2 theta) is infinite, so theta = 45 degrees; transformed equation 2X2 + 8Y2 - 8 = 0, i.e. X2 + 4Y2 = 4.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of x^2 + 16y - 16 = 0 referred to parallel axes with new origin O'(0, 1).
mcqs.why: Shift: x = X, y = Y + 1. Substituting: X^2 + 16(Y + 1) - 16 = X^2 + 16Y + 16 - 16 = X^2 + 16Y. Hence the transformed equation is X^2 + 16Y = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of x^2 - y^2 + 4x + 8y - 11 = 0 referred to parallel axes with new origin O'(-2, 4).
mcqs.why: Shift: x = X - 2, y = Y + 4. Substituting and expanding: (X - 2)^2 - (Y + 4)^2 + 4(X - 2) + 8(Y + 4) - 11 = X^2 - Y^2 + (4 - 16 - 8 + 32 - 11) = X^2 - Y^2 + 1, the X and Y terms cancelling. Hence X^2 - Y^2 + 1 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of 9x^2 - 4y^2 + 36x + 8y - 4 = 0 referred to parallel axes with new origin O'(2, 1).
Find the new origin (axes parallel) that removes the first-degree terms from 3x^2 - 2y^2 + 24x + 12y + 24 = 0, and the transformed equation.
mcqs.why: Complete the squares: 3(x + 4)^2 - 2(y - 3)^2 = 6 (check: 3(x + 4)^2 - 2(y - 3)^2 expands to the given left side plus 30 - 24 = 6). So the new origin is (-4, 3) and with X = x + 4, Y = y - 3 the equation is 3X^2 - 2Y^2 = 6.

mcqs.q: Find the new origin that removes the first-degree terms from 25x^2 + 9y^2 + 50x - 36y - 164 = 0, and the transformed equation.
mcqs.why: Complete the squares: 25(x + 1)^2 + 9(y - 2)^2 = 225 (expanding gives the stated equation, since 25 + 36 + 164 = 225). So the new origin is (-1, 2) and the transformed equation is 25X^2 + 9Y^2 = 225.

mcqs.q: Find the new origin that removes the first-degree terms from x^2 - y^2 - 6x + 2y + 7 = 0, and the transformed equation.
mcqs.why: Complete the squares: (x - 3)^2 - (y - 1)^2 = 1 (expanding: x^2 - 6x + 9 - y^2 + 2y - 1 = 1, i.e. x^2 - y^2 - 6x + 2y + 7 = 0). So the new origin is (3, 1) and the transformed equation is X^2 - Y^2 = 1.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of xy = 1 referred to axes rotated about the origin through 45 degrees.
mcqs.why: For theta = 45 degrees: x = (X - Y)/sqrt(2), y = (X + Y)/sqrt(2). Then xy = ((X - Y)(X + Y))/2 = (X^2 - Y^2)/2. Setting this equal to 1: X^2 - Y^2 = 2.

mcqs.q: Find the equation of 7x^2 - 8xy + y^2 - 9 = 0 referred to axes rotated through theta = arctan 2.
mcqs.why: With tan(theta) = 2: cos(theta) = 1/sqrt(5), sin(theta) = 2/sqrt(5). Substituting the rotation formulas, the XY term cancels and the X^2 and Y^2 coefficients become -1 and 9, giving -X^2 + 9Y^2 - 9 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the angle of rotation that removes the XY term from 5x^2 - 6xy + 5y^2 - 8 = 0, and the transformed equation.
mcqs.why: tan(2 theta) = B/(A - C) with A = C = 5, so tan(2 theta) is infinite, 2 theta = 90 degrees and theta = 45 degrees. The transformed equation is 2X^2 + 8Y^2 - 8 = 0; dividing by 2: X^2 + 4Y^2 = 4.

mcqs.q: Exercise 6.8 Q1(iii) is printed as 9x^2 + 4x^2 + 18x - 16y - 11 = 0, and the print note says the second term may be a misprint for 4y^2. With that correction, shifting the origin to O'(-1, 2) gives:

lessons.title: Exercise 6.9 — The general equation of second degree
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. By a rotation of axes, eliminate the xy-term in each of the following equations.

Identify the conic and find its elements: (i) 4x2 - 4xy + y2 - 6 = 0 (ii) x2 - 2xy + y2 8x - 8y = 0 (iii) x2 + 2xy + y2 + 2 sqrt(2) x - 2 sqrt(2) y + 2 = 0 (iv) x2 + xy + y2 4 = 0 (v) 7x2 - 6 sqrt(3) xy + 13y2 - 16 = 0 (vi) 4x2 - 4xy + 7y2 + 12x + 6y - 9 = 0 (vii) xy - 4x - 2y = 0 (viii) x2 + 4xy - 2y2 - 6 = 0 (ix) x2 - 4xy - 2y2 + 10x + 4y = 0. (i) Eigenvalues 5 and 0: rotated form 5X2 = 6, i.e. a pair of parallel lines 2x - y = +-sqrt(6) (a degenerate conic).

(ii) Rotation 45 degrees: Y2 = 4 sqrt(2) X, a parabola with vertex at the origin in XY-coordinates, a = sqrt(2), focus (sqrt(2), 0), directrix X = -sqrt(2).

(iii) Rotation 45 degrees: X2 = 2(Y - 1/2), a parabola with vertex (0, 1/2) in XY-coordinates, a = 1/2, focus (0, 1), directrix Y = 0.

(iv) Rotation 45 degrees: (3/2)X2 + (1/2)Y2 = 4, i.e. X2/(8/3) + Y2/8 = 1, an ellipse with semi-major axis 2 sqrt(2) along Y, semi-minor axis 2 sqrt(2/3), eccentricity sqrt(2/3).

(v) Rotation 30 degrees: 16X2 + 4Y2 = 16, i.e. X2 + Y2/4 = 1, an ellipse with semi-major axis 2 along Y, semi-minor axis 1, eccentricity sqrt(3)/2.

(vi) Rotation with tan(2 theta) = 4/3: 8X2 + 3Y2 + 6 sqrt(5) X - 9 = 0, i.e. an ellipse with centre (-3 sqrt(5)/8, 0) in XY-coordinates, semi-major axis sqrt(39/8) along Y, eccentricity sqrt(10)/4.

(vii) Rotation 45 degrees: (X - 3 sqrt(2))2/16 - (Y - sqrt(2))2/16 = 1, a rectangular hyperbola with centre (3 sqrt(2), sqrt(2)) in XY-coordinates, a = b = 4, eccentricity sqrt(2).

(viii) Rotation with tan(2 theta) = 4/3: 2X2 - 3Y2 = 6, i.e. X2/3 - Y2/2 = 1, a hyperbola with a = sqrt(3), b = sqrt(2), eccentricity sqrt(5/3).

Answer: (ix) Rotation with tan(2 theta) = -4/3: a hyperbola with centre (-9/(2 sqrt(5)), -8/(3 sqrt(5))) in XY-coordinates, a2 = 23/12, b2 = 23/18, eccentricity sqrt(5/3).

Q2. Show that (i) 10xy + 8x - 15y - 12 = 0 and (ii) 6x2 + xy - y2 - 21x - 8y + 9 = 0 each represents a pair of straight lines and find an equation of each line.

(i) Factoring: 10xy + 8x - 15y - 12 = (5y + 4)(2x - 3), so the lines are y = -4/5 and x = 3/2.

Answer: (ii) The homogeneous part factors as (3x - y)(2x + y); writing (3x - y + a)(2x + y + b) and matching coefficients gives a = -9, b = -1 (and ab = 9 checks), so the lines are 3x - y - 9 = 0 and 2x + y - 1 = 0.

Q3. Find an equation of the tangent to each of the given conics at the indicated point.

(i) 3x2 - 7y2 + 2x - y - 48 = 0 at (4, 1) (ii) x2 + 5xy - 4y2 + 4 = 0 at y = -1 (iii) x2 + 4xy - 3y2 - 5x - 9y + 6 = 0 at x = 3.

(i) The point lies on the conic (48 - 7 + 8 - 1 - 48 = 0). Tangent T = 0: 26x - 15y - 89 = 0.

(ii) y = -1 gives x2 - 5x = 0, so the points are (0, -1) and (5, -1). Tangents: at (0, -1): 5x - 8y - 8 = 0; at (5, -1): 5x + 33y + 8 = 0.

Answer: (iii) x = 3 gives -3y2 + 3y = 0, so the points are (3, 0) and (3, 1). Tangents: at (3, 0): x + 3y - 3 = 0; at (3, 1): 5x - 3y - 12 = 0.

mcqs.q: By rotation of axes, the equation 4x^2 - 4xy + y^2 - 6 = 0 represents:
options: A pair of parallel lines 2x - y = +/-sqrt(6), a degenerate conic
A parabola with vertex at the origin
An ellipse with semi-axes sqrt(6) and sqrt(30)
mcqs.why: The quadratic part has eigenvalues 5 and 0, so rotation gives 5X^2 = 6, i.e. X^2 = 6/5 in the rotated frame; back in xy-coordinates 4x^2 - 4xy + y^2 = (2x - y)^2 = 6, so 2x - y = +/-sqrt(6): a pair of parallel lines, a degenerate conic.

mcqs.q: By a 45-degree rotation, x^2 - 2xy + y^2 - 8x - 8y = 0 becomes:
options: Y^2 = 4 sqrt(2) X, a parabola with a = sqrt(2), focus (sqrt(2), 0), directrix X = -sqrt(2)
Y^2 = 2 sqrt(2) X, a parabola with a = sqrt(2)/2
mcqs.why: Rotating through 45 degrees removes the xy-term and gives Y^2 = 4 sqrt(2) X in XY-coordinates. This is a parabola with vertex at the origin; comparing with Y^2 = 4aX gives a = sqrt(2), focus (sqrt(2), 0) and directrix X = -sqrt(2).

mcqs.q: By a 45-degree rotation, x^2 + 2xy + y^2 + 2 sqrt(2) x - 2 sqrt(2) y + 2 = 0 becomes a parabola. Its elements in XY-coordinates are:
options: X^2 = 2(Y - 1/2); vertex (0, 1/2), a = 1/2, focus (0, 1), directrix Y = 0
mcqs.why: Rotation through 45 degrees gives X^2 = 2(Y - 1/2). Comparing with X^2 = 4a(Y - k): 4a = 2, a = 1/2, vertex (0, 1/2). Focus is a above the vertex: (0, 1/2 + 1/2) = (0, 1); directrix is Y = 1/2 - 1/2 = 0.

mcqs.q: By a 45-degree rotation, x^2 + xy + y^2 - 4 = 0 becomes an ellipse. Its equation and eccentricity are:
mcqs.why: Rotation gives (3/2)X^2 + (1/2)Y^2 = 4, i.e. X^2/(8/3) + Y^2/8 = 1. Semi-major axis along Y: a = 2 sqrt(2) (a^2 = 8); semi-minor b^2 = 8/3. e = sqrt(1 - b^2/a^2) = sqrt(1 - (8/3)/8) = sqrt(1 - 1/3) = sqrt(2/3).

mcqs.q: By a rotation through 30 degrees, 7x^2 - 6 sqrt(3) xy + 13y^2 - 16 = 0 becomes:
options: Ellipse X^2 + Y^2/4 = 1 with e = sqrt(3)/2
Hyperbola X^2 - Y^2/4 = 1 with e = sqrt(3)/2
Ellipse X^2/4 + Y^2 = 1 with e = sqrt(3)/2
mcqs.why: The eigenvalues of the quadratic part are 16 and 4, so rotation through 30 degrees gives 16X^2 + 4Y^2 = 16, i.e. X^2 + Y^2/4 = 1. Semi-major axis 2 along Y, semi-minor 1: e = sqrt(1 - 1/4) = sqrt(3)/2.

mcqs.q: By a 45-degree rotation, xy - 4x - 2y = 0 represents:
options: A rectangular hyperbola with a = b = 2 and e = sqrt(2)
A rectangular hyperbola with centre (3 sqrt(2), sqrt(2)) in XY-coordinates, a = b = 4, e = sqrt(2)
A hyperbola with a = 4, b = 2 and e = sqrt(2)
A circle with centre (3 sqrt(2), sqrt(2)) in XY-coordinates
mcqs.why: Rotation through 45 degrees gives (X - 3 sqrt(2))^2/16 - (Y - sqrt(2))^2/16 = 1. Centre (3 sqrt(2), sqrt(2)) in XY-coordinates and a = b = 4, so it is a rectangular hyperbola with e = sqrt(1 + b^2/a^2) = sqrt(2).

mcqs.q: By rotation (tan(2 theta) = 4/3), x^2 + 4xy - 2y^2 - 6 = 0 becomes:
options: Hyperbola X^2/3 - Y^2/2 = 1 with e = sqrt(3/5)
Hyperbola X^2/3 - Y^2/2 = 1 with a = sqrt(3), b = sqrt(2), e = sqrt(5/3)
Ellipse X^2/3 + Y^2/2 = 1 with e = sqrt(5/3)
mcqs.why: Rotation gives 2X^2 - 3Y^2 = 6, i.e. X^2/3 - Y^2/2 = 1, a hyperbola with a = sqrt(3), b = sqrt(2). e = sqrt(1 + b^2/a^2) = sqrt(1 + 2/3) = sqrt(5/3).

mcqs.q: The equation 10xy + 8x - 15y - 12 = 0 represents a pair of straight lines. The lines are:
mcqs.why: Factor: (5y + 4)(2x - 3) = 10xy - 15y + 8x - 12, which matches the given left side exactly. So the conic splits into 5y + 4 = 0, i.e. y = -4/5, and 2x - 3 = 0, i.e. x = 3/2. (The last option gives 2x + 3 = 0, a different line.)

mcqs.q: The equation 6x^2 + xy - y^2 - 21x - 8y + 9 = 0 represents a pair of straight lines. The lines are:
mcqs.why: The homogeneous part factors: 6x^2 + xy - y^2 = (3x - y)(2x + y). Write (3x - y + a)(2x + y + b) and match coefficients of x, y and the constant: this gives a = -9, b = -1, and the check a b = 9 matches the constant term. Hence the lines are 3x - y - 9 = 0 and 2x + y - 1 = 0.

mcqs.q: Find the tangent to the conic 3x^2 - 7y^2 + 2x - y - 48 = 0 at the point (4, 1).
mcqs.why: First check the point lies on the conic: 3(16) - 7(1) + 2(4) - 1 - 48 = 48 - 7 + 8 - 1 - 48 = 0. The tangent T = 0 at (4, 1) simplifies to 26x - 15y - 89 = 0; incidence check: 26(4) - 15(1) - 89 = 104 - 15 - 89 = 0, so (4, 1) lies on it.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.1 — Vectors in the plane
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Write the vector PQ in the form x i + y j. (i) P(2, 3), Q(6, -2) (ii) P(0, 5), Q(-1, -6).

(i) PQ = Q - P = (6 - 2) i + (-2 - 3) j = 4 i - 5 j.

Answer: (ii) PQ = (-1 - 0) i + (-6 - 5) j = -i - 11 j.

Q2. Find the magnitude of the vector u: (i) u = 2 i - 7 j (ii) u = i + j (iii) u = [3, -4].

(i) |u| = sqrt(4 + 49) = sqrt(53). (ii) |u| = sqrt(1 + 1) = sqrt(2).

Answer: (iii) |u| = sqrt(9 + 16) = 5.

Q3. If u = 2 i - 7 j, v = i - 6 j and w = -i + j.

Find the following vectors: (i) u + v - w (ii) 2 u - 3 v + 4 w (iii) (1/2) u + (1/2) v + (1/2) w. (i) u + v - w = (2 + 1 + 1) i + (-7 - 6 - 1) j = 4 i - 14 j.

(ii) 2 u - 3 v + 4 w = (4 - 3 - 4) i + (-14 + 18 + 4) j = -3 i + 8 j.

Answer: (iii) (1/2)(u + v + w) = (1/2)(1 i - 12 j) = i - 6 j.

Q4. Find the sum of the vectors AB and CD, given the four points A(1, -1), B(2, 0), C(-1, 3) and D(-2, 2).

AB = (2 - 1, 0 + 1) = (1, 1) and CD = (-2 + 1, 2 - 3) = (-1, -1).

Answer: AB + CD = (0, 0), the zero vector.

Q5. Find the vector from the point A to the origin where AB = 4 i - 2 j and B is the point (-2, 5).

A = B - AB = (-2 - 4, 5 + 2) = (-6, 7).

Answer: the vector from A to the origin is O - A = 6 i - 7 j.

Q6. Find a unit vector in the direction of the vector given below: (i) v = 2 i - j (ii) v = (1/2) i + (sqrt(3)/2) j (iii) v = (sqrt(3)/2) i - (1/2) j. (i) |v| = sqrt(5), so the unit vector is (2/sqrt(5)) i - (1/sqrt(5)) j.

(ii) |v| = sqrt(1/4 + 3/4) = 1, so v is already a unit vector.

Answer: (iii) |v| = sqrt(3/4 + 1/4) = 1, so v is already a unit vector.

Q7. If A, B and C are respectively the points (2, -4), (4, 0) and (1, 6).

Use vector method to find the coordinates of the point D if: (i) ABCD is a parallelogram (ii) ADBC is a parallelogram.

(i) In ABCD, D = A + C - B = (2 + 1 - 4, -4 + 6 - 0) = (-1, 2).

Answer: (ii) In ADBC, D = A + B - C = (2 + 4 - 1, -4 + 0 - 6) = (5, -10).

Q8. If B, C and D are respectively (4, 1), (-2, 3) and (-8, 0).

Use vector method to find the coordinates of the point: (i) A if ABCD is a parallelogram. (ii) E if AEBD is a parallelogram. (i) A = B + D - C = (4 - 8 + 2, 1 + 0 - 3) = (-2, -2).

Answer: (ii) With A(-2, -2), E = A + B - D = (-2 + 4 + 8, -2 + 1 - 0) = (10, -1).

Q9. If O is the origin and OP = AB, find the point P when A and B are (-3, 7) and (1, 0) respectively.

AB = (1 + 3, 0 - 7) = (4, -7), and OP = AB with O the origin.

Answer: P = (4, -7).

Q10. Use vectors, to show that ABCD is a parallelogram, when the points A, B, C and D are respectively (0, 0), (a, 0), (b, c) and (b - a, c).

AB = (a, 0) and DC = (b - (b - a), c - 0) = (a, 0), so AB = DC.

Also BC = (b - a, c) and AD = (b - a, c), so BC = AD.

Answer: opposite sides are equal and parallel, so ABCD is a parallelogram.

Q11. If AB = CD, find the coordinates of the point A when points B, C, D are (1, 2), (-2, 5), (4, 11) respectively.

CD = (4 + 2, 11 - 5) = (6, 6), so AB = (6, 6).

Answer: A = B - AB = (1 - 6, 2 - 6) = (-5, -4).

Q12. Find the position vectors of the point of division of the line segments joining the following pair of points, in the given ratio: (i) Point C with position vector 2 i - 3 j and point D with position vector 3 i + 2 j in the ratio 4 : 3 (ii) Point E with position vector 5 j and point F with position vector 4 i + j in ratio 2 : 5.

(i) The dividing point is (3 C + 4 D)/7 = (18/7) i - (1/7) j.
