Answer: (ii) The dividing point is (5 E + 2 F)/7 = (8/7) i + (27/7) j.

Q13. Prove that the line segment joining the mid points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half as long.

Let the vertices have position vectors a, b, c. The mid points of AB and AC are (a + b)/2 and (a + c)/2.

Their difference is (c - b)/2 = (1/2) BC.

Answer: the segment is parallel to BC and half its length.

Q14. Prove that the line segments joining the mid points of the sides of a quadrilateral taken in order form a parallelogram.

Let the mid points of AB, BC, CD, DA be P, Q, R, S. By the mid point theorem in triangle ABC, PQ = (1/2) AC; in triangle CDA, RS = (1/2) AC, so PQ is parallel and equal to RS.

Answer: similarly QR = SP = (1/2) BD, so PQRS is a parallelogram.

mcqs.q: For P(2, 3) and Q(6, -2), the vector PQ in the form x i + y j is:
mcqs.why: PQ = Q - P = (6 - 2) i + (-2 - 3) j = 4 i - 5 j, subtracting the coordinates of P from those of Q component by component.

mcqs.q: The magnitude of u = 2 i - 7 j is:
mcqs.why: |u| = sqrt(2^2 + (-7)^2) = sqrt(4 + 49) = sqrt(53). The squares are added first, then the square root is taken, giving sqrt(53).

mcqs.q: The magnitude of u = [3, -4] is:
mcqs.why: |u| = sqrt(3^2 + (-4)^2) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt(25) = 5. This is the familiar 3-4-5 right triangle, so the magnitude is exactly 5.

mcqs.q: If u = 2 i - 7 j, v = i - 6 j and w = -i + j, then u + v - w equals:
mcqs.why: i-components: 2 + 1 - (-1) = 4. j-components: -7 - 6 - 1 = -14. Hence u + v - w = 4 i - 14 j, combining each component separately.

mcqs.q: With u = 2 i - 7 j, v = i - 6 j and w = -i + j, the vector 2u - 3v + 4w is:
Given A(1, -1), B(2, 0), C(-1, 3) and D(-2, 2), the sum AB + CD is:
If AB = 4 i - 2 j and B is the point (-2, 5), the vector from A to the origin is:
mcqs.why: A = B - AB = (-2 - 4, 5 - (-2)) = (-6, 7). The vector from A to the origin is O - A = (0 - (-6), 0 - 7) = (6, -7), i.e. 6 i - 7 j.

mcqs.q: A unit vector in the direction of v = 2 i - j is:
mcqs.why: |v| = sqrt(2^2 + (-1)^2) = sqrt(5). Dividing v by its magnitude: v/|v| = (2/sqrt(5)) i - (1/sqrt(5)) j, which has length 1 and the same direction.

mcqs.q: A, B and C are (2, -4), (4, 0) and (1, 6). If ABCD is a parallelogram, D is:
mcqs.why: In parallelogram ABCD, D = A + C - B = (2 + 1 - 4, -4 + 6 - 0) = (-1, 2), because the diagonals bisect each other so A + C = B + D.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.2 — Vectors in space, direction cosines
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Let A = (2, 5), B = (-1, 1) and C = (2, -6).

Find (i) AB (ii) 2 AB - CB (iii) 2 CB - 2 CA. (i) AB = (-1 - 2, 1 - 5) = (-3, -4). CB = (-1 - 2, 1 + 6) = (-3, 7) and CA = (0, 11).

(ii) 2 AB - CB = (-6, -8) - (-3, 7) = (-3, -15).

Answer: (iii) 2 CB - 2 CA = (-6, 14) - (0, 22) = (-6, -8).

Q2. Let u = i + 2 j - k, v = 3 i - 2 j + 2 k, w = 5 i - j + 3 k.

Find the indicated vector or number. (i) u + 2 v + w (ii) u - 3 w (iii) |3 v + w|. (i) u + 2 v + w = (1 + 6 + 5, 2 - 4 - 1, -1 + 4 + 3) = (12, -3, 6).

(ii) u - 3 w = (1 - 15, 2 + 3, -1 - 9) = (-14, 5, -10).

Answer: (iii) 3 v + w = (14, -7, 9), so |3 v + w| = sqrt(196 + 49 + 81) = sqrt(326).

Q3. Find the magnitude of the vector v and write the direction cosines of v. (i) v = 2 i + 3 j + 4 k (ii) v = i - j - k (iii) v = 4 i - 5 j. (i) |v| = sqrt(29); direction cosines (2/sqrt(29), 3/sqrt(29), 4/sqrt(29)).

(ii) |v| = sqrt(3); direction cosines (1/sqrt(3), -1/sqrt(3), -1/sqrt(3)).

Answer: (iii) |v| = sqrt(41); direction cosines (4/sqrt(41), -5/sqrt(41), 0).

Q4. Find a, so that |a i + (a + 1) j + 2 k| = 3.

Squaring: a2 + (a + 1)2 + 4 = 9, i.e. 2a2 + 2a - 4 = 0, i.e. a2 + a - 2 = 0.

Answer: a = 1 or a = -2.

Q5. Find a unit vector in the direction of v = i + 2 j - k.

|v| = sqrt(6).

Answer: the unit vector is (1/sqrt(6)) i + (2/sqrt(6)) j - (1/sqrt(6)) k.

Q6. If a = 3 i - j - 4 k, b = -2 i - 4 j - 3 k and c = i + 2 j - k.

Find a unit vector parallel to 3 a - 2 b + 4 c. 3 a - 2 b + 4 c = (9 + 4 + 4, -3 + 8 + 8, -12 + 6 - 4) = (17, 13, -10).

Its magnitude is sqrt(289 + 169 + 100) = sqrt(558) = 3 sqrt(62).

Answer: a unit vector parallel to it is (17 i + 13 j - 10 k)/sqrt(558) (the opposite sign is also parallel).

Q7. Find a vector whose (i) magnitude is 4 and is parallel to 2 i - 3 j + 6 k (ii) magnitude is 2 and is parallel to -i + j + k. (i) |2 i - 3 j + 6 k| = 7, so the vector is 4(2 i - 3 j + 6 k)/7 = (8/7) i - (12/7) j + (24/7) k (or its negative).

Answer: (ii) |-i + j + k| = sqrt(3), so the vector is (2/sqrt(3))(-i + j + k) (or its negative).

Q8. If u = 2 i + 3 j + 4 k, v = -i + 3 j - k and w = i + 6 j + z k represent the sides of a triangle.

Find the value of z.

For the three vectors to close a triangle, one must be the sum of the other two. Here u + v = (1, 6, 3).

Answer: w = u + v requires z = 3.

Q9. The position vectors of the points A, B, C and D are 2 i - j + k, 3 i + j, 2 i + 4 j - 2 k and -i - 2 j + k respectively.

Show that AB is parallel to CD. AB = (1, 2, -1) and CD = (-3, -6, 3) = -3 AB.

Answer: CD is a scalar multiple of AB, so AB is parallel to CD.

Q10. Two vectors v and w in space are parallel if there is a scalar c such that v = c w. (a) Find two vectors of length 2 parallel to the vector v = 2 i - 4 j + 4 k. (b) Find the constant a so that the vectors v = i - 3 j + 4 k and w = a i + 9 j - 12 k are parallel.

(c) Find a vector of length 5 in the direction opposite that of v = i - 2 j + 3 k. (d) Find a and b so that the vectors 3 i - j + 4 k and a i + b j - 2 k are parallel. (a) |v| = 6; the two vectors are +-(2/3) i -+(4/3) j -+(4/3) k, i.e. (2/3, -4/3, 4/3) and (-2/3, 4/3, -4/3).

(b) w = -3 v, so a = -3.

(c) |v| = sqrt(14); the vector is -5 v/sqrt(14) = -(5/sqrt(14)) i + (10/sqrt(14)) j (15/sqrt(14)) k.

Answer: (d) the common ratio is -2/4 = -1/2, so a = -3/2 and b = 1/2.

Q11. Find the direction cosines for the given vector: (i) v = 3 i - j + 2 k (ii) 6 i - 2 j + k (iii) PQ, where P = (-2, 1, 5) and Q = (1, 3, 1).

(i) |v| = sqrt(14): direction cosines (3/sqrt(14), -1/sqrt(14), 2/sqrt(14)).

(ii) |v| = sqrt(41): direction cosines (6/sqrt(41), -2/sqrt(41), 1/sqrt(41)).

Answer: (iii) PQ = (3, 2, -4), |PQ| = sqrt(29): direction cosines (3/sqrt(29), 2/sqrt(29), -4/sqrt(29)).

Q12. Which of the following triples can be the direction angles of a single vector: (i) 45 degrees, 45 degrees, 60 degrees (ii) 30 degrees, 45 degrees, 60 degrees (iii) 45 degrees, 60 degrees, 60 degrees.

A triple is possible exactly when cos2(a) + cos2(b) + cos2(g) = 1.

(i) 1/2 + 1/2 + 1/4 = 5/4: not possible. (ii) 3/4 + 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/2: not possible.

Answer: (iii) 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1: possible.

mcqs.q: For A = (2, 5) and B = (-1, 1), the vector AB is:
mcqs.why: AB = B - A = (-1 - 2, 1 - 5) = (-3, -4). Each coordinate of A is subtracted from the corresponding coordinate of B.

mcqs.q: If u = i + 2 j - k, v = 3 i - 2 j + 2 k and w = 5 i - j + 3 k, then u + 2v + w is:
With u = i + 2 j - k, v = 3 i - 2 j + 2 k and w = 5 i - j + 3 k, the value of |3v + w| is:
The direction cosines of v = i - j - k are:
mcqs.why: |v| = sqrt(1 + 1 + 1) = sqrt(3). The direction cosines are the components divided by |v|: (1/sqrt(3), -1/sqrt(3), -1/sqrt(3)), whose squares sum to 1.

mcqs.q: The values of a for which |a i + (a + 1) j + 2 k| = 3 are:
A unit vector in the direction of v = i + 2 j - k is:
mcqs.why: |v| = sqrt(1 + 4 + 1) = sqrt(6). Dividing each component by sqrt(6) gives the unit vector (1/sqrt(6)) i + (2/sqrt(6)) j - (1/sqrt(6)) k.

mcqs.q: A vector of magnitude 4 parallel to 2 i - 3 j + 6 k is:
mcqs.why: |2 i - 3 j + 6 k| = sqrt(4 + 9 + 36) = sqrt(49) = 7. The required vector is 4 times the unit vector: 4(2 i - 3 j + 6 k)/7 = (8/7) i - (12/7) j + (24/7) k (or its negative).

mcqs.q: If u = 2 i + 3 j + 4 k, v = -i + 3 j - k and w = i + 6 j + z k are the sides of a triangle with w = u + v, then z is:
mcqs.why: For the vectors to close a triangle, w must equal u + v = (2 - 1, 3 + 3, 4 - 1) = (1, 6, 3). Comparing the k-component with w gives z = 3.

mcqs.q: With position vectors of A, B, C, D equal to 2 i - j + k, 3 i + j, 2 i + 4 j - 2 k and -i - 2 j + k, AB is parallel to CD because:
mcqs.why: AB = (3 - 2, 1 + 1, 0 - 1) = (1, 2, -1) and CD = (-1 - 2, -2 - 4, 1 + 2) = (-3, -6, 3) = -3(1, 2, -1) = -3 AB. A scalar multiple means the vectors are parallel.

mcqs.q: Which triple can be the direction angles of a single vector?
mcqs.why: A triple works exactly when cos^2 a + cos^2 b + cos^2 g = 1. For 45, 60, 60: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1, so it is possible. The first gives 5/4 and the second gives 3/2, both impossible.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.3 — The scalar product of two vectors
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find the cosine of the angle theta between u and v: (i) u = 3 i + j - k, v = 2 i - j + k (ii) u = i - 3 j + 4 k, v = 4 i - j + 3 k (iii) u = [3, 5], v = [6, -2] (iv) u = [2, 3, 1], v = [2, 4, 1].

(i) u . v = 6 - 1 - 1 = 4; |u| = sqrt(11), |v| = sqrt(6): cos(theta) = 4/sqrt(66).

(ii) u . v = 4 + 3 + 12 = 19; |u| = |v| = sqrt(26): cos(theta) = 19/26.

(iii) u . v = 18 - 10 = 8; |u| = sqrt(34), |v| = sqrt(40): cos(theta) = 2/sqrt(85).

Answer: (iv) u . v = 4 + 12 + 1 = 17; |u| = sqrt(14), |v| = sqrt(21): cos(theta) = 17/sqrt(294) = 17/(7 sqrt(6)).

Q2. Calculate the projection of a along b and projection of b along a when: (i) a = -i + k, b = j + k (ii) a = 3 i + j - k, b = -2 i - j + k. (i) a . b = 1, |a| = |b| = sqrt(2).

Scalar projection of a along b = 1/sqrt(2), vector projection (1/2)(j + k); scalar projection of b along a = 1/sqrt(2), vector projection (1/2)(-i + k).

Answer: (ii) a . b = -8, |a| = sqrt(11), |b| = sqrt(6). Scalar projection of a along b = -8/sqrt(6), vector projection (8/3) i + (4/3) j - (4/3) k; scalar projection of b along a = -8/sqrt(11), vector projection -(24/11) i - (8/11) j + (8/11) k.

Q3. Find a real number a so that the vectors u and v are perpendicular.

(i) u = 2 a i + j - k, v = i + a j + 4 k (ii) u = a i + 2 a j + 3 k, v = i + a j + 3 k. (i) u . v = 2a + a - 4 = 3a - 4 = 0, so a = 4/3.

Answer: (ii) u . v = a + 2a2 + 9 = 0 has discriminant 1 - 72 < 0, so no real number a makes them perpendicular.

Q4. Find the number z so that the triangle with vertices A(1, -1, 0), B(-2, 2, 1) and C(0, 2, z) is a right triangle with right angle at C.

CA = (1, -3, -z) and CB = (-2, 0, 1 - z); the right angle at C requires CA . CB = 0.

-2 - z(1 - z) = 0, i.e. z2 - z - 2 = 0.

Answer: z = 2 or z = -1.

Q5. If v is a vector for which v . i = 0, v . j = 0, v . k = 0, find v.

Writing v = (x, y, z): v . i = x = 0, v . j = y = 0, v . k = z = 0.

Answer: v = 0, the zero vector.

Q6. (i) Show that the vectors 3 i - 2 j + k, i - 3 j + 5 k and 2 i + j - 4 k form a right angle.

(ii) Show that the set of points P = (1, 3, 2), Q = (4, 1, 4) and R = (6, 5, 5) form a right triangle. (In (ii) the book prints the third point as P again; it is read as R.) (i) Call the vectors v1, v2, v3. Then v2 = v1 - v3, and v1 . v3 = 6 - 2 - 4 = 0, so v1 is perpendicular to v3; also |v2|2 = 35 = 14 + 21 = |v1|2 + |v3|2, so they form a right-angled triangle with the right angle between v1 and v3.

Answer: (ii) PQ = (3, -2, 2) and QR = (2, 4, 1) with PQ . QR = 6 - 8 + 2 = 0, so triangle PQR is right-angled at Q.

Q7. Show that mid point of hypotenuse a right triangle is equidistant from its vertices.

Put the right angle at the origin: let the other vertices have position vectors a and b with a . b = 0. The mid point of the hypotenuse is m = (a + b)/2.

Then |m|2 = (|a|2 + |b|2)/4 and |m - a|2 = |b - a|2/4 = (|a|2 + |b|2)/4; the same holds for the third vertex.

Answer: the mid point is equidistant from all three vertices.

Q8. Prove that perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle are concurrent.

Let a point X lie on the bisectors of AB and AC: then (X - (A + B)/2) . (B - A) = 0 and (X - (A + C)/2) . (C - A) = 0, i.e. X . (B - A) = (|B|2 - |A|2)/2 and X . (C - A) = (|C|2 |A|2)/2.

Subtracting gives X . (C - B) = (|C|2 - |B|2)/2, i.e. X also lies on the bisector of BC.

Answer: the three bisectors meet at X, so they are concurrent.

Q9. Prove that the altitudes of a triangle are concurrent.

Let H satisfy (H - A) . (B - C) = 0 and (H - B) . (C - A) = 0, i.e. AH is perpendicular to BC and BH is perpendicular to CA.

Adding the two expanded equations gives (H - C) . (B - A) = 0.

Answer: CH is perpendicular to AB, so the three altitudes meet at H.

Q10. Prove that the angle in a semi circle is a right angle.

Let O be the centre, A = -a, B = a and P = p on the circle, so |p| = |a|.

Then PA . PB = (-a - p) . (a - p) = |p|2 - |a|2 = 0.

Answer: angle APB is a right angle.

Q11. Prove that cos(a + b) = cos a cos b - sin a sin b.

Take unit vectors u = (cos a, sin a) and w = (cos b, -sin b); the angle between them is a + b.

Then u . w = cos a cos b - sin a sin b, and also u . w = |u| |w| cos(a + b) = cos(a + b).

Answer: cos(a + b) = cos a cos b - sin a sin b.

Q12. Prove that in any triangle ABC.

(i) b = c cos A + a cos C (ii) c = a cos B + b cos A (iii) b2 = c2 + a2 - 2 c a cos B (iv) c2 = a2 + b2 - 2 a b cos C. Place A at the origin and AC on the x-axis: C = (b, 0), B = (c cos A, c sin A). Then a2 = (b - c cos A)2 + (c sin A)2, and cos C = (b - c cos A)/a, so a cos C = b - c cos A, proving (i); (ii) follows the same way.

For (iii), put B at the origin with BA and BC as vectors of lengths c and a at angle B: then b2 = |BA - BC|2 = c2 + a2 - 2 c a cos B; (iv) is the same argument at C.

Answer: all four formulas hold.

mcqs.q: The cosine of the angle between u = 3 i + j - k and v = 2 i - j + k is:
mcqs.why: u . v = 6 - 1 - 1 = 4, |u| = sqrt(9 + 1 + 1) = sqrt(11) and |v| = sqrt(4 + 1 + 1) = sqrt(6). So cos(theta) = (u . v)/(|u||v|) = 4/sqrt(66).

mcqs.q: The cosine of the angle between u = [3, 5] and v = [6, -2] is:
For a = -i + k and b = j + k, the scalar projection of a along b is:
mcqs.why: a . b = 0 + 0 + 1 = 1 and |b| = sqrt(0 + 1 + 1) = sqrt(2). The scalar projection of a along b is (a . b)/|b| = 1/sqrt(2).

mcqs.q: The real number a that makes u = 2a i + j - k and v = i + a j + 4 k perpendicular is:
mcqs.why: Perpendicular vectors have zero dot product: u . v = 2a(1) + (1)(a) + (-1)(4) = 2a + a - 4 = 3a - 4. Setting 3a - 4 = 0 gives a = 4/3.

mcqs.q: For u = a i + 2a j + 3 k and v = i + a j + 3 k, the values of a making u and v perpendicular are:
mcqs.why: u . v = a + 2a^2 + 9 = 0 would be needed. Its discriminant is 1 - 4(2)(9) = 1 - 72 = -71, which is negative, so the equation has no real solution and no real a works.

mcqs.q: The triangle with vertices A(1, -1, 0), B(-2, 2, 1) and C(0, 2, z) is right-angled at C when z is:
mcqs.why: CA = (1, -3, -z) and CB = (-2, 0, 1 - z). Right angle at C needs CA . CB = -2 + 0 - z(1 - z) = z^2 - z - 2 = 0, i.e. (z - 2)(z + 1) = 0, so z = 2 or z = -1.

options: Perpendicular to itself only if non-zero
mcqs.q: If a vector v satisfies v . i = 0, v . j = 0 and v . k = 0, then v is:
mcqs.why: Writing v = (x, y, z): v . i = x = 0, v . j = y = 0 and v . k = z = 0. All three components are zero, so v = 0, the zero vector.

mcqs.q: For P = (1, 3, 2), Q = (4, 1, 4) and R = (6, 5, 5), triangle PQR is right-angled at Q because:
mcqs.why: PQ = (3, -2, 2) and QR = (2, 4, 1). Their dot product is 3(2) + (-2)(4) + 2(1) = 6 - 8 + 2 = 0, so PQ is perpendicular to QR and the right angle is at Q.

mcqs.q: The vectors v1 = 3 i - 2 j + k and v3 = 2 i + j - 4 k are perpendicular because:
mcqs.why: v1 . v3 = 3(2) + (-2)(1) + 1(-4) = 6 - 2 - 4 = 0. A zero dot product for two non-zero vectors means they are perpendicular to each other.

options: cos a cos b + sin a sin b
cos a cos b - sin a sin b
sin a cos b - cos a sin b
cos(a - b) directly as a sum
mcqs.q: In the proof of cos(a + b) = cos a cos b - sin a sin b, with unit vectors u = (cos a, sin a) and w = (cos b, -sin b), the dot product u . w equals:
mcqs.why: u . w = cos a cos b + sin a (-sin b) = cos a cos b - sin a sin b. Also u . w = |u||w| cos(a + b) = cos(a + b) since both are unit vectors, proving the formula.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.4 — The cross product of two vectors
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Compute the cross product a x b and b x a.

Check your answer by showing that each a and b is perpendicular to a x b and b x a. (i) a = 2 i + j - k, b = i - j + k (ii) a = i - j, b = i + j (Print note: in this copy the k-components of (ii) are blank/missing in the print, confirmed at 300 DPI; the part is solved below for the legible plane vectors a = i - j, b = i + j, and is flagged, not taken as the book's full data.) (iii) a = 3 i - 2 j + k, b = i + j (iv) a = -4 i + j - 2 k, b = 2 i + j + k. (i) a x b = -3 j - 3 k and b x a = 3 j + 3 k; a . (a x b) = -3 + 3 = 0 and b . (a x b) = 3 3 = 0, and the same for b x a.

(ii) Flagged (see head): for a = i - j, b = i + j, a x b = 2 k and b x a = -2 k; a . (2 k) = 0 and b . (2 k) = 0.

(iii) a x b = -i + j + 5 k and b x a = i - j - 5 k; a . (a x b) = -3 - 2 + 5 = 0 and b . (a x b) = -1 + 1 = 0.

Answer: (iv) a x b = 3 i - 6 k and b x a = -3 i + 6 k; a . (a x b) = -12 + 12 = 0 and b . (a x b) = 6 - 6 = 0.

Q2. Find a unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing a and b.

Also find sine of the angle between them. (i) a = 2 i - 6 j - 3 k, b = 4 i + 3 j - k (ii) a = -i - j - k, b = 2 i - 3 j + 4 k (iii) a = 2 i - 2 j + 4 k, b = -i + j - 2 k (iv) a = i - j, b = i + j (Print note: as in Q1(ii), the k-components of (iv) are blank/missing in the print; solved below for the legible plane vectors, and flagged.) (i) a x b = 15 i - 10 j + 30 k, |a x b| = 35, |a| = 7, |b| = sqrt(26): unit vector +-(3 i 2 j + 6 k)/7, sin(theta) = 5/sqrt(26).

(ii) a x b = -7 i + 2 j + 5 k, |a x b| = sqrt(78), |a| = sqrt(3), |b| = sqrt(29): unit vector +-( -7 i + 2 j + 5 k)/sqrt(78), sin(theta) = sqrt(26/29).

(iii) b = -a/2, so a and b are parallel: a x b = 0 and sin(theta) = 0, and there is no unique unit vector perpendicular to their plane.

Answer: (iv) Flagged (see head): for a = i - j, b = i + j, a x b = 2 k, |a| = |b| = sqrt(2): unit vector +-k, sin(theta) = 1.

Q3. Find the area of the triangle, determined by the point P, Q and R. (i) P(0, 0, 0);

Q(2, 3, 2); R(-1, 1, 4) (ii) P(1, -1, -1); Q(2, 0, -1); R(0, 2, 1).

(i) PQ = (2, 3, 2), PR = (-1, 1, 4); PQ x PR = 10 i - 10 j + 5 k with magnitude 15, so the area is (1/2)(15) = 15/2 square units.

Answer: (ii) PQ = (1, 1, 0), PR = (-1, 3, 2); PQ x PR = 2 i - 2 j + 4 k with magnitude 2 sqrt(6), so the area is sqrt(6) square units.

Q4. Find the area of parallelogram, whose vertices are: (i) A(0, 0, 0); B(1, 2, 3); C(2, -1, 1); D(3, 1, 4) (ii) A(1, 2, -1); B(4, 2, -3); C(6, -5, 2); D(9, -5, 0) (iii) A(-1, 1, 1); B(-1, 2, 2); C(-3, 4, -5); D(-3, 5, -4).

(i) AB = (1, 2, 3), AD = (3, 1, 4); AB x AD = 5 i + 5 j - 5 k with magnitude 5 sqrt(3), so the area is 5 sqrt(3) square units.

(ii) AB = (3, 0, -2), AD = (8, -7, 1); AB x AD = -14 i - 19 j - 21 k with magnitude sqrt(998), so the area is sqrt(998) square units.

Answer: (iii) AB = (0, 1, 1), AD = (-2, 4, -5); AB x AD = -9 i - 2 j + 2 k with magnitude sqrt(89), so the area is sqrt(89) square units.

Q5. Which vectors, if any, are perpendicular or parallel (i) u = 5 i - j + k; v = j - 5 k; w = -15 i + 3 j - 3 k (ii) u = i + 2 j - k; v = -i + j + k; w = -(pi/2) i - pi j + (pi/2) k. (i) w = -3 u, so w is parallel to u.

The dot products are u . v = -6, u . w = -81 and v . w = 18, none zero, so no pair is perpendicular.

Answer: (ii) w = -(pi/2) u, so w is parallel to u; u . v = -1 + 2 - 1 = 0, so u is perpendicular to v, and hence v is also perpendicular to w.

Q6. Prove that: a x (b + c) + b x (c + a) + c x (a + b) = 0.

Expanding by distributivity: a x b + a x c + b x c + b x a + c x a + c x b.

Since b x a = -a x b, c x b = -b x c and c x a = -a x c, the six terms cancel in pairs.

Answer: the sum is 0.

Q7. If a + b + c = 0, then prove that a x b = b x c = c x a.

From c = -(a + b): b x c = b x (-(a + b)) = -b x a = a x b.

Also c x a = (-(a + b)) x a = -(b x a) = a x b.

Answer: a x b = b x c = c x a.

Q8. Prove that: sin(a - b) = sin a cos b - cos a sin b.

(Print note: as printed in this copy the formula is given with a + sign before the second term, which is the formula for sin(a + b), not sin(a - b); the correct sin(a - b) formula is proved below and the misprint is flagged, not silently corrected.) Take unit vectors u = (cos a, sin a, 0) and v = (cos b, sin b, 0). The k-component of u x v is cos a sin b - sin a cos b, and it equals sin(b - a) = -sin(a - b).

Answer: hence sin(a - b) = sin a cos b - cos a sin b, while sin a cos b + cos a sin b is sin(a + b).

Q9. If a x b = 0 and a . b = 0, what conclusion can be drawn about a or b?

a x b = 0 means a and b are parallel (or one is zero); a . b = 0 means they are perpendicular (or one is zero).

Answer: a non-zero pair cannot be both parallel and perpendicular, so at least one of a, b must be the zero vector.

mcqs.q: For a = 2 i + j - k and b = i - j + k, the cross product a x b is:
For a = 2 i + j - k and b = i - j + k, the cross product b x a is:
mcqs.why: Reversing the order reverses the sign: b x a = -(a x b). Since a x b = -3 j - 3 k (computed component-wise), b x a = 3 j + 3 k, and indeed a . (b x a) = 0 as a check.

mcqs.q: For the plane vectors a = i - j and b = i + j, the cross product a x b is:
mcqs.why: Treating both as vectors with zero k-component: k-component of a x b is (1)(1) - (-1)(1) = 1 + 1 = 2, and the i and j components are both 0. So a x b = 2 k, perpendicular to the plane.

The area of the triangle with vertices P(0, 0, 0), Q(2, 3, 2) and R(-1, 1, 4) is:
mcqs.why: PQ = (2, 3, 2) and PR = (-1, 1, 4). PQ x PR = 10 i - 10 j + 5 k, with magnitude sqrt(100 + 100 + 25) = 15. The triangle area is half of this: (1/2)(15) = 15/2 square units.

mcqs.q: The area of the parallelogram with vertices A(0, 0, 0), B(1, 2, 3), C(2, -1, 1) and D(3, 1, 4) is:
mcqs.why: AB = (1, 2, 3) and AD = (3, 1, 4). AB x AD = 5 i + 5 j - 5 k, whose magnitude is sqrt(25 + 25 + 25) = sqrt(75) = 5 sqrt(3). The parallelogram area equals this magnitude, 5 sqrt(3) square units.

options: w = -3 u, so w is parallel to u
w = 3 u, so w is parallel to u
u . w = 0, so they are perpendicular
w = -u, so they are equal in length
mcqs.q: For u = 5 i - j + k and w = -15 i + 3 j - 3 k, the relation between u and w is:
mcqs.why: -3u = -3(5 i - j + k) = -15 i + 3 j - 3 k = w. Since w is a scalar multiple of u, the two vectors are parallel; their dot product is -81, not zero, so they are not perpendicular.

options: At least one of a, b is the zero vector
They are parallel and perpendicular at once
mcqs.q: If a x b = 0 and a . b = 0 both hold, the conclusion about a and b is:
mcqs.why: a x b = 0 means a and b are parallel (or one is zero), while a . b = 0 means they are perpendicular (or one is zero). A non-zero pair cannot be both, so at least one of a, b must be the zero vector.

options: sin a cos b + cos a sin b
sin a cos b - cos a sin b
cos a cos b - sin a sin b
sin a sin b - cos a cos b
mcqs.q: The correct formula for sin(a - b), proved using the cross product, is:
mcqs.why: For unit vectors u = (cos a, sin a, 0) and v = (cos b, sin b, 0), the k-component of u x v is cos a sin b - sin a cos b = sin(b - a) = -sin(a - b). Hence sin(a - b) = sin a cos b - cos a sin b; the version with a + sign printed in the book is sin(a + b), a misprint.

mcqs.q: For a = 2 i - 2 j + 4 k and b = -i + j - 2 k, the sine of the angle between a and b is:
mcqs.why: b = -a/2, since -(2, -2, 4)/2 = (-1, 1, -2) = b, so a and b are parallel and a x b = 0. Therefore sin(theta) = |a x b|/(|a||b|) = 0, and no unique perpendicular unit vector exists.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.5 — Scalar triple product of vectors
lessons.notes_html:
Q1. Find the volume of the parallelepiped for which the given vectors are three edges.

(i) u = 3 i + 2 k; v = i + 2 j + k; w = -j + 4 k (ii) u = i - 4 j - k; v = i - j - 2 k; w = 2 i - 3 j + k (iii) u = i - 2 j - 3 k; v = 2 i - j - k; w = j + k. (i) [u v w] = 3(8 + 1) - 2 = 25, so the volume is 25 cubic units.

(ii) [u v w] = -7 + 20 + 1 = 14, so the volume is 14 cubic units.

Answer: (iii) [u v w] = 4 - 6 = -2, so the volume is 2 cubic units.

Q2. Verify that a . b x c = b . c x a = c . a x b if a = 3 i - j + 5 k, b = 4 i + 3 j - 2 k, and c = 2 i + 5 j + k. b x c = 13 i - 8 j + 14 k, so a . (b x c) = 39 + 8 + 70 = 117.

c x a = 26 i - 7 j - 17 k, so b . (c x a) = 104 - 21 + 34 = 117.

Answer: a x b = -13 i + 26 j + 13 k, so c . (a x b) = -26 + 130 + 13 = 117. All three are equal.

Q3. Prove that the vectors i - 2 j + 3 k, -2 i + 3 j - 4 k and i - 3 j + 5 k are coplanar.

Their scalar triple product is the determinant with rows (1, -2, 3), (-2, 3, -4), (1, -3, 5).

Expanding: (15 - 12) + 2(-10 + 4) + 3(6 - 3) = 3 - 12 + 9 = 0.

Answer: the triple product is zero, so the vectors are coplanar.

Q4. Find the constant a such that the vectors are coplanar.

(i) i - j + k, i - 2 j - 3 k and 3 i - a j + 5 k. (ii) i - 2 a j - k, i - j + 2 k and a i - j + k. (i) The determinant is (-10 - 3a) + 14 + (-a + 6) = 10 - 4a; setting it to zero gives a = 5/2.

Answer: (ii) The determinant is 1 + 2a - 4a2 + 1 - a = 2 + a - 4a2; setting it to zero gives a = (1 +- sqrt(33))/8.

Q5. (a) Find the value of: (i) 2 i x 2 j . k (ii) 3 j . k x i (iii) [k i j] (iv) [i i k] (b) Prove that u . (v x w) + v . (w x u) + w . (u x v) = 3 u . (v x w). (a) (i) (2 i x 2 j) . k = 4 k . k = 4.

(ii) 3 j . (k x i) = 3 j . j = 3. (iii) [k i j] = k . (i x j) = k . k = 1. (iv) [i i k] = 0, since two vectors are repeated.

Answer: (b) Each term equals the same triple product [u v w] by cyclic permutation, so the sum is 3 [u v w] = 3 u . (v x w).

Q6. Find volume of the Tetrahedron with the vertices (i) (0, 1, 2), (3, 2, 1), (1, 2, 1) and (5, 5, 6) (ii) (2, 1, 8), (3, 2, 9), (2, 1, 4) and (3, 3, 10).

(i) Edge vectors from (0, 1, 2) are (3, 1, -1), (1, 1, -1), (5, 4, 4); their determinant is 24 - 9 + 1 = 16, so the volume is 16/6 = 8/3 cubic units.

Answer: (ii) Edge vectors from (2, 1, 8) are (1, 1, 1), (0, 0, -4), (1, 2, 2); their determinant is 8 - 4 = 4, so the volume is 4/6 = 2/3 cubic units.

Q7. Find the work done, if the point at which the constant force F = 4 i + 3 j + 5 k is applied to an object, moves from P1(3, 1, -2) to P2(2, 4, 6).

Displacement d = P2 - P1 = (-1, 3, 8).

Work = F . d = -4 + 9 + 40 = 45 units.

Q8. A particle, acted by constant forces 4 i + j - 3 k and 3 i - j - k, is displaced from A(1, 2, 3) to B(5, 4, 1).

Find the work done. Resultant force = (7, 0, -4); displacement = (4, 2, -2).

Answer: work = 28 + 0 + 8 = 36 units.

Q9. A particle is displaced from the point A(5, -5, -7) to the point B(6, 2, -2) under the action of constant forces defined by 10 i - j + 11 k, 4 i + 5 j + 9 k and -2 i + j - 9 k.

Show that the total work done by the forces is 102 units. Resultant force = (12, 5, 11); displacement = (1, 7, 5).

Answer: work = 12 + 35 + 55 = 102 units, as required.

Q10. A force of magnitude 6 units acting parallel to 2 i - 2 j + k displaces, the point of application from (1, 2, 3) to (5, 3, 7).

Find the work done. The direction has magnitude 3, so F = 6(2 i - 2 j + k)/3 = 4 i - 4 j + 2 k; displacement = (4, 1, 4).

Answer: work = 16 - 4 + 8 = 20 units.

Q11. A force F = 3 i + 2 j - 4 k is applied at the point (1, -1, 2).

Find the moment of the force about the point (2, -1, 3).

r = (1, -1, 2) - (2, -1, 3) = (-1, 0, -1).

Answer: moment = r x F = 2 i - 7 j - 2 k.

Q12. A force F = 4 i - 3 k, passes through the point A(2, -2, 5).

Find the moment of F about the point B(1, -3, 1). r = A - B = (1, 1, 4).

Answer: moment = r x F = -3 i + 19 j - 4 k.

Q13. Give a force F = 2 i + j - 3 k acting at a point A(1, -2, 1).

Find the moment of F about the point B(2, 0, -2). r = A - B = (-1, -2, 3).

Answer: moment = r x F = 3 i + 3 j + 3 k.

Q14. Find the moment about A(1, 1, 1) of each of the concurrent forces i - 2 j, 3 i + 2 j - k, 5 j + 2 k, where P(2, 0, 1) is their point of concurrency.

r = P - A = (1, -1, 0).

Moments: r x (i - 2 j) = -k; r x (3 i + 2 j - k) = i + j + 5 k; r x (5 j + 2 k) = -2 i - 2 j + 5 k.

Answer: the three moments are -k, i + j + 5 k and -2 i - 2 j + 5 k.

Q15. A force F = 7 i + 4 j - 3 k is applied at P(1, -2, 3).

Find its moment about the point Q(2, 1, 1).

r = P - Q = (-1, -3, 2).

Answer: moment = r x F = i + 11 j + 17 k.

mcqs.q: The volume of the parallelepiped with edges u = 3 i + 2 k, v = i + 2 j + k and w = -j + 4 k is:
mcqs.why: The scalar triple product [u v w] = 3[(2)(4) - (1)(-1)] + 2[(1)(-1) - (2)(0)] = 3(8 + 1) + 2(-1) = 27 - 2 = 25. The volume is |25| = 25 cubic units.

mcqs.q: The volume of the parallelepiped with edges u = i - 2 j - 3 k, v = 2 i - j - k and w = j + k is:
mcqs.why: Expanding the determinant for [u v w]: the computation gives 4 - 6 = -2. Volume is the absolute value of the scalar triple product, so the volume is |-2| = 2 cubic units.

mcqs.q: For a = 3 i - j + 5 k, b = 4 i + 3 j - 2 k and c = 2 i + 5 j + k, the common value of a . (b x c) = b . (c x a) = c . (a x b) is:
mcqs.why: b x c = 13 i - 8 j + 14 k, so a . (b x c) = 3(13) + (-1)(-8) + 5(14) = 39 + 8 + 70 = 117. Cyclic permutations give the same value: b . (c x a) = 104 - 21 + 34 = 117 and c . (a x b) = -26 + 130 + 13 = 117.

mcqs.q: The vectors i - 2 j + 3 k, -2 i + 3 j - 4 k and i - 3 j + 5 k are coplanar because their scalar triple product is:
mcqs.why: Expanding the determinant with rows (1, -2, 3), (-2, 3, -4), (1, -3, 5): (15 - 12) + 2(-10 + 4) + 3(6 - 3) = 3 - 12 + 9 = 0. A zero triple product means the vectors are coplanar.

mcqs.q: The constant a for which i - j + k, i - 2 j - 3 k and 3 i - a j + 5 k are coplanar is:
mcqs.why: The determinant is (-10 - 3a) + 14 + (-a + 6) = 10 - 4a. Coplanarity requires this to be zero: 10 - 4a = 0, so a = 10/4 = 5/2.

mcqs.q: The value of [k i j] = k . (i x j) is:
mcqs.why: i x j = k by the right-hand rule for the unit vectors. Hence [k i j] = k . (i x j) = k . k = 1, since k is a unit vector.

mcqs.q: The value of the scalar triple product [i i k] is:
mcqs.why: [i i k] = i . (i x k). The triple product has the vector i repeated twice, and any scalar triple product with a repeated vector is 0, since the three vectors are coplanar.

mcqs.q: The volume of the tetrahedron with vertices (0, 1, 2), (3, 2, 1), (1, 2, 1) and (5, 5, 6) is:
mcqs.why: Edge vectors from (0, 1, 2) are (3, 1, -1), (1, 1, -1) and (5, 4, 4). Their determinant is 24 - 9 + 1 = 16. The tetrahedron volume is one sixth of this: 16/6 = 8/3 cubic units.
